title: Full Stack Developer / Backend Developer needed for phase 2 admin build (Laravel Vue)
description:
Hi, I run a niche marketplace built on Laravel and Vue. It launched a few months ago, sellers are getting paid out through Stripe, and the back office has not kept up with any of it. Every dispute between a buyer and a seller is handled by hand right now, and I am still the only person with admin access. I am looking for a senior full stack developer to build phase 2 of the admin side end to end.

What phase 2 has to cover:
a structured dispute workflow - a case per dispute, states, evidence files, and a record of who did what and when
roles and permissions, so I can give two ops people access without handing them everything
an audit trail I can actually read: what changed on a listing, an order or a payout, and by whom
saved views, bulk actions and exports, so moderation stops being one click per row
the existing moderation queue extended rather than replaced

Stack I want to keep: Laravel, Vue 3 with Inertia, MySQL, Stripe. Same stack as the product grows - nothing new introduced for this.

The product is live, so the repository, the current admin screens and the payout setup go to the person I hire, under NDA - not before. Nobody needs access to anything to apply.

I am not technical, so I want someone who drives this: the plan written down before anything gets built, the dispute workflow phased in first, and honest pushback when I ask for something that will hurt us later. A backend developer read of where the audit trail meets the payout side matters more here than the screens do.

To apply, share 2-3 Laravel and Vue admin or back-office builds you have shipped and a short note on how you would phase this.

title: Custom WordPress Website — Two Claude API Conversational Tools, Gumroad Access Gating, PWA
description:
I'm building a revenue hub for Unpacking Quiet - a digital self-guided tools business serving women navigating high-conflict co-parenting. The site needs to be live and generating revenue. This is not a branding project or a design exercise. It's a functional, secure, revenue-generating web application.

What I'm Building
A custom WordPress website on my existing SiteGround hosting with:
• Two AI-powered conversational tools built on the Anthropic Claude API
• Gumroad payment gating with email verification
• A digital product shop page
• Mobile-first PWA build
• Google Analytics 4 with goal tracking
• Post-launch support

The Two Tools
Tool 1 — The Co-Parent Coach
A structured four-step communication tool. The user pastes a message from their co-parent. The tool assesses whether a response is needed, presents four response style options, drafts a response in the chosen style, then identifies every manipulation tactic in the original message. Full multi-turn conversational flow, not a single input/output form.

Tool 2 — The Quiet Room
An emotional support and regulation tool for after difficult interactions. Four-phase conversational flow: receive what happened, witness what the user did, guide through processing questions one at a time, offer a grounding anchor. Warm, unhurried, non-clinical.

Both tools require true multi-turn conversation. The user and tool exchange multiple messages in sequence as part of a structured flow.

Technical Requirements
• Custom WordPress build on existing SiteGround hosting
• Both tools powered by Anthropic Claude API (claude-sonnet-4-6)
• Custom system prompt for each tool stored securely server-side, never exposed to frontend or users under any circumstances. This is proprietary IP and a non-negotiable requirement.
• Backend and Claude integration built from scratch. No templates, no white-label platforms
• Gumroad webhook integration specifically, not general payment processing
• After purchase: Gumroad delivers unique access link to buyer
• Email verification: buyer's email must match Gumroad purchase record before tool loads
• If verification fails: redirect to purchase page
• One tool: $17. Both tools bundled: $27. One-time purchase, unlimited use.
• Shop page: product grid with Gumroad buy buttons for PDF guides ($9-27)
• Mobile-first, fully responsive, PWA capable
• Google Analytics 4 with goal tracking on tool purchase clicks and shop buy button clicks
• Client needs ability to make basic content updates independently after launch

Safety Requirements - Non-Negotiable
Both tools serve women in emotionally activated states navigating high-conflict dynamics. The following guardrails must be built into both system prompts and frontend interface:
• The Co-Parent Coach stays within co-parenting communication guidance only. No legal advice, therapy, or mental health counseling
• The Quiet Room is an emotional support tool, not therapy, no clinical guidance, no risk assessment
• If a user expresses self-harm thoughts or appears to be in crisis, either tool must respond warmly, refer immediately to appropriate crisis resources, and not attempt to manage the crisis itself
• Visible disclaimer on both tool pages stating they are not substitutes for professional legal, therapeutic, or mental health support

What I Need From You Before Hiring
Please include in your proposal:
1. Portfolio examples of AI-powered web applications with payment gating or access control specifically Claude or OpenAI API integrations
2. Your proposed approach to keeping system prompts server-side and never exposed to the frontend
3. Confirmation of specific Gumroad webhook experience, not just general payment processing
4. Confirmation you can build true multi-turn conversational chat interfaces, not single input/output forms
5. Your realistic timeline and how you would phase the build
Applications that do not address these five points specifically will not be considered.

Project Details
• Budget: $800–$1,200 USD
• Timeline: 6–8 weeks
• Platform: WordPress on existing SiteGround hosting
• Language: English fluency required, strong written communication essential throughout

What I'll Provide At Project Start
• Complete system prompts for both tools (shared securely)
• Anthropic API key (shared securely)
• Gumroad account access for webhook setup
• All brand assets - logo SVG, color codes, typography
• All written content for homepage and product pages
• SiteGround collaborator access (not main account credentials)

title: Senior WordPress/PHP Developer needed, Custom Enrollment Portal with DocuSign & Stripe
description:
We're a marketing agency building an enrollment portal for a client's B2B program, launching September 1. This is a custom development project on WordPress — not theme customization or page-builder work.

The build: a standalone portal (subdomain, managed hosting) where invited companies enter an access code, see their company data pre-filled from a ~2,500-record database, review a program page, then either enroll or request a meeting. Enrollment includes a scroll-enforced terms acceptance and an embedded DocuSign signing ceremony generated from a pre-filled template. Two paid services are sold via Stripe Checkout. Admins manage codes and region eligibility through the WP dashboard with CSV import/export. Designs, copy, and PM are handled on our side — you build.

Must-have skills: custom plugin development (hooks, custom tables, WP REST API); third-party REST API integration from PHP, including OAuth/JWT auth and webhook handling — DocuSign eSignature API experience is a big plus; Stripe Checkout; solid vanilla JS for multi-step pre-filled forms; security fundamentals (nonces, sanitization, server-side lookups, hardening a site that handles legal documents and payments).

Scope & timeline: ~100–130 hours over 3 weeks, starting immediately. Core flow demo-ready by Aug 21, launch Aug 31. Fixed milestones or hourly — tell us your preference and rate.

To apply, briefly answer: (1) Describe a custom plugin you wrote and why an existing plugin couldn't do the job. (2) Which OAuth/JWT-authenticated APIs have you integrated from PHP, and how did you handle token refresh and webhook verification? (3) How would you store and query a 2,500-row lookup table in WordPress without exposing the data client-side?

Applications without the three answers won't be considered.

(2) Which OAuth/JWT-authenticated APIs have you integrated from PHP, and how did you handle token refresh and webhook verification? title: WordPress Developer: Custom Theme Speed, SEO Foundations & Conversion Tracking
description:
looking for an experienced WordPress developer to deliver a defined technical improvement project on a client website in the healthcare sector.

Important: this is not a page builder site. It runs a custom, hand-coded WordPress theme built on Bootstrap 5. You will be working directly in theme PHP, template files and custom post types. If your experience is mainly Elementor, Divi or WPBakery, this is not the right fit and we would rather you skip it than take it on.

The site looks good and the client is happy with the design. We are explicitly not redesigning it. The work is entirely about how the site is built, how fast it loads, how it is structured for search, and whether we can measure what it produces.
The problems we are solving
The homepage takes around 13 seconds to load its main content on mobile
An old duplicate homepage is still live and indexed
Page titles and meta descriptions are wrong or duplicated across key pages
Blog articles are published at root level rather than in a blog section
Key service categories are bundled onto single pages rather than having individual pages
Booking hands off to a third-party platform on another domain, which breaks conversion tracking entirely
Structured data and internal linking are thin or absent

Scope of work
1. Speed rebuild Take mobile LCP from around 13s to under 3s. Image compression and WebP conversion, correct srcset, self-hosted fonts with proper caching, deferred and async JS, critical CSS, lazy loading below the fold, cache plugin configuration. There is a hero video on the homepage that must stay exactly as it is visually, but must be moved out of the critical rendering path.

2. Site restructure Redirect a duplicate homepage, move blog content into a proper blog section, restructure service and category hierarchies. Full redirect mapping with 301s, no chains, no lost URLs. Sitemap regeneration and resubmission.

3. SEO foundations Unique titles and meta descriptions across every URL, correction of wrongly assigned metadata, heading structure fixes, local search targeting, schema implementation (LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, Article, Person, Review), internal linking structure built into templates.

4. New templates A category/condition page template and a campaign landing page template, both matching existing brand styling, both field-driven so non-developers can add pages afterwards without dev time. Roughly 15-20 pages built from these templates.

5. Conversion tracking GA4 event tracking across all forms and contact methods, Google Ads and Meta conversion tracking, first-party storage of UTMs and click IDs passed through to the third-party booking platform so attribution survives the handoff, plus a proper post-submission thank-you page. Full documentation of every tag, trigger and variable.

6. Additional builds Pricing page rebuild with a single-source price system, a finance page with a BNPL provider integration, before/after gallery blocks, a live reviews block pulling from the Google Places API, and site-wide WhatsApp contact buttons with click tracking.

7. Accessibility and crawl basics Descriptive link names, alt text, WCAG 2.1 AA contrast checks, keyboard navigation and focus states, form label associations, canonical and robots sanity check.
How we work
All work on staging. Nothing goes live without our sign-off
Full backup before you start
Child theme or version control from day one, no editing live theme files through the dashboard
Baseline metrics captured before any change is made
Short written update at the end of each working day
We supply a full written brief with acceptance criteria for every task, so there is no ambiguity about what "done" means
Requirements
Demonstrable Core Web Vitals work on custom-coded themes, not page builder sites
Strong PHP and WordPress template hierarchy knowledge, comfortable with custom post types and custom fields
Technical SEO understanding, including schema and redirect management
GA4 and GTM implementation experience, including cross-domain and third-party platform tracking
Confident written English and reliable daily communication
Available to start within the next week
Nice to have
Experience with regulated or healthcare sector sites
Google Places API integration experience
BNPL or payment provider integration experience

This is initially an immediate project, but I’m looking for someone I can continue working with on an ongoing, piece-by-piece basis as budget becomes available.

What I’m Looking For

You should be highly comfortable with:

WordPress
Elementor Pro
Crocoblock / JetEngine
JetFormBuilder
Dynamic content and custom fields
WordPress user roles and permissions
Membership/access-control systems
WooCommerce and/or WooCommerce Subscriptions
Recurring memberships/subscriptions
Payment gateway integrations
PHP/custom WordPress development when necessary
Troubleshooting existing WordPress/Crocoblock implementations

Experience building membership, subscription, community, content, or creator platforms is a major plus.

The Initial Project

The first priority is helping me determine the best technical architecture for the paid membership system and then helping build it.

I already have much of the website and user system built using WordPress, Elementor, and Crocoblock.

I need someone who can evaluate the existing setup and help answer questions such as:

Should the membership be built primarily with Crocoblock/JetEngine?
Should WooCommerce be used for subscriptions and billing?
Would WooCommerce Memberships + WooCommerce Subscriptions make sense?
Would another membership solution be a better fit?
How should paid users be assigned/managed?
How should recurring payments automatically grant/revoke access?
How should premium content and features be restricted?
How should membership status be displayed throughout the site?
What should be handled with Crocoblock versus custom development?
How can we keep the system maintainable as the site grows?

I don't necessarily need someone who will build every component themselves. Part of the job is helping me define the scope and architecture so I can take on some of the simpler implementation work myself.

I want to work collaboratively with the developer rather than simply handing over the entire project.

Adult-Content Experience Is Important - Just text and some images

This is an adult-content website, so you must be comfortable working with adult businesses and understand some of the additional technical/business constraints that come with this industry.

In particular, payment processing can be more complicated than with a conventional membership website. Mainstream processors such as Stripe may not be appropriate for the business, so the membership architecture may need to accommodate adult-friendly payment processors/gateways such as Segpay, Paxum, or similar providers.

You should be comfortable researching and working around these types of limitations rather than assuming a standard Stripe/WooCommerce setup will work.

You do not need to have previously worked on an adult website, but you need to be comfortable doing so.

Ongoing Work

After the initial architecture and membership system are established, I expect there will be ongoing development work.

Rather than committing to a large fixed project upfront, I'd like to work on a budget-available / piece-by-piece basis.

Potential future work could include:

New membership features
Premium content functionality
User dashboards
Author/creator features
User profiles
Custom JetEngine queries
Front-end submission functionality
Notifications
User roles and permissions
Search/filter improvements
Performance optimization
Custom PHP/JavaScript
API/payment integrations
UX improvements
Troubleshooting and maintenance
New features as the platform grows

The website is thesmuthub.com if you'd like to better understand.

Completed remediation of all identified critical and high-priority issues
Written audit report (before and after)
Brief documentation or handoff notes for future maintenance

title: WordPress Developer: Custom Theme Speed, SEO Foundations & Conversion Tracking
description:
looking for an experienced WordPress developer to deliver a defined technical improvement project on a client website in the healthcare sector.

Important: this is not a page builder site. It runs a custom, hand-coded WordPress theme built on Bootstrap 5. You will be working directly in theme PHP, template files and custom post types. If your experience is mainly Elementor, Divi or WPBakery, this is not the right fit and we would rather you skip it than take it on.

The site looks good and the client is happy with the design. We are explicitly not redesigning it. The work is entirely about how the site is built, how fast it loads, how it is structured for search, and whether we can measure what it produces.
The problems we are solving
The homepage takes around 13 seconds to load its main content on mobile
An old duplicate homepage is still live and indexed
Page titles and meta descriptions are wrong or duplicated across key pages
Blog articles are published at root level rather than in a blog section
Key service categories are bundled onto single pages rather than having individual pages
Booking hands off to a third-party platform on another domain, which breaks conversion tracking entirely
Structured data and internal linking are thin or absent

Scope of work
1. Speed rebuild Take mobile LCP from around 13s to under 3s. Image compression and WebP conversion, correct srcset, self-hosted fonts with proper caching, deferred and async JS, critical CSS, lazy loading below the fold, cache plugin configuration. There is a hero video on the homepage that must stay exactly as it is visually, but must be moved out of the critical rendering path.

2. Site restructure Redirect a duplicate homepage, move blog content into a proper blog section, restructure service and category hierarchies. Full redirect mapping with 301s, no chains, no lost URLs. Sitemap regeneration and resubmission.

3. SEO foundations Unique titles and meta descriptions across every URL, correction of wrongly assigned metadata, heading structure fixes, local search targeting, schema implementation (LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, Article, Person, Review), internal linking structure built into templates.

4. New templates A category/condition page template and a campaign landing page template, both matching existing brand styling, both field-driven so non-developers can add pages afterwards without dev time. Roughly 15-20 pages built from these templates.

5. Conversion tracking GA4 event tracking across all forms and contact methods, Google Ads and Meta conversion tracking, first-party storage of UTMs and click IDs passed through to the third-party booking platform so attribution survives the handoff, plus a proper post-submission thank-you page. Full documentation of every tag, trigger and variable.

6. Additional builds Pricing page rebuild with a single-source price system, a finance page with a BNPL provider integration, before/after gallery blocks, a live reviews block pulling from the Google Places API, and site-wide WhatsApp contact buttons with click tracking.

7. Accessibility and crawl basics Descriptive link names, alt text, WCAG 2.1 AA contrast checks, keyboard navigation and focus states, form label associations, canonical and robots sanity check.
How we work
All work on staging. Nothing goes live without our sign-off
Full backup before you start
Child theme or version control from day one, no editing live theme files through the dashboard
Baseline metrics captured before any change is made
Short written update at the end of each working day
We supply a full written brief with acceptance criteria for every task, so there is no ambiguity about what "done" means
Requirements
Demonstrable Core Web Vitals work on custom-coded themes, not page builder sites
Strong PHP and WordPress template hierarchy knowledge, comfortable with custom post types and custom fields
Technical SEO understanding, including schema and redirect management
GA4 and GTM implementation experience, including cross-domain and third-party platform tracking
Confident written English and reliable daily communication
Available to start within the next week
Nice to have
Experience with regulated or healthcare sector sites
Google Places API integration experience
BNPL or payment provider integration experience

1. Product schema markup + SEO-friendly URLs/meta data (per product, using my keywords) — foundation for Google discoverability
2. Fast site speed (image compression, CDN, minimal plugins) — impacts both SEO ranking and conversion
3. Frictionless mobile checkout (guest checkout, 1-click pay like Shop Pay/PayPal Express, minimal form fields) — 60-70% of traffic is mobile
4. High-impact product pages (benefit-driven copy, multiple photos, video, clear specs) — converts visitors once SEO gets them there
5. Trust signals sitewide (badges near Add to Cart, visible return policy, contact/chat widget) — new stores fail most often on trust
6. Social proof / reviews (UGC) via Judge.me/Loox/Yotpo — reinforces trust, doubles as fresh SEO content
7. Full analytics tracking pre-launch (GA4 + e-commerce tracking, Meta Pixel/CAPI, GTM) — needed to measure and optimize post-launch
8. Abandoned cart recovery (email/SMS sequence) — recovers otherwise-lost sales passively
9. Email/SMS capture with welcome offer — captures first-time visitors who aren't ready to buy yet
10. AOV boosters (free shipping threshold, in-cart upsells) — increases revenue per visitor

A few things that matter a lot to me for this project:

- Full ownership: I need complete ownership of the website, theme, plugins, and all files/credentials once the project is done. No lock-in.
- Full transparency: I'd like clear communication throughout — what's being installed, why, and access to everything (hosting, admin, plugin licenses, etc.) as we go, not just at the end.
- Trust: This is important to me, so I'm looking for someone reliable who works cleanly and explains me with transparency on what they do.

Could you share:
1. Examples of WooCommerce sites you've built (ideally similar product-line/e-commerce launches)
2. Your general process and timeline for a build of this scope
3. Your experience with the items listed above (SEO, checkout optimization, cart recovery, analytics, etc.)
4. How you handle ownership/transfer of credentials, licenses, and code
5. A cost estimate broken down by design, development, and setup

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Best,
Neel

title: Web Developer Needed: Backend Integration for Equine Steward (Phased Project)
description:
Equine Steward is a website selling customizable legal contracts for horse owners (leases, sale agreements). The front end is fully built — homepage, product pages, and interactive contract-questionnaire tools are live and functional. What's missing is the backend: real payments, real document delivery, and (in a later phase) user accounts.

This is a Two-Phase Project. I want a developer who can start with Phase 1 now and continue into Phase 2 later, so continuity matters — please speak to your availability for both phases in your proposal, even though we're scoping and pricing Phase 1 first.

I am **not technical**, so I need someone who can own this end-to-end and explain decisions in plain language, not just execute tickets.

What's Already Done
- Complete website: homepage, multiple product pages, three interactive contract-building tools, blog/resources section — all built as static HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- All visual design, branding, and copy is finalized
- The interactive questionnaires (conditional logic, live document preview) are fully functional client-side — this does not need to be rebuilt
- A "Purchase & Download" button exists on each contract tool but is currently a placeholder — it doesn't charge anyone or gate the actual document
- A contact form exists on the site but doesn't send or store submissions anywhere yet — it's a visual mockup

---

PHASE 1 (Scope This Now)

1. Stripe Integration
- Real checkout for each contract product (each is priced individually, single one-time purchase per contract)
- Handle payment confirmation before releasing any document content

2. PDF Generation + Paywall Gating
- Generate a clean, finished PDF of the completed contract from the questionnaire's answers
- Critical requirement: the complete document must only be generated/served **after** Stripe confirms payment. Right now all the document logic runs client-side, which means a determined visitor could technically view the full document text before paying — this needs to be fixed with a real backend, not just front-end tricks (disabling copy/right-click, etc., which is not real protection)
- Document should be deliverable via download link and/or email after purchase (whichever you recommend as more reliable)

3. Contact Form Backend
- The existing contact form (name, email, message) needs to actually deliver submissions — to my email inbox at minimum, or to a simple CRM/inbox tool if you think that's a better long-term fit
- Please recommend the simplest reliable option (e.g., a transactional email service) rather than the most complex

**Note:** Items #2 and #3 both likely depend on the same piece of infrastructure — a transactional email service (e.g., SendGrid, Postmark, or similar) for delivering PDFs and forwarding form submissions. Please account for that shared setup in your Phase 1 estimate rather than treating them as fully separate systems.

---

PHASE 2 (Scope Later, Described Here for Context)

- User accounts (signup/login)
- Saved drafts — a visitor should be able to start a questionnaire, leave, and come back later to finish where they left off. This is already promised on the site's FAQ page, so it's a real commitment, not a stretch goal.
- Subscription payments — in addition to the one-time purchases from Phase 1, a recurring/subscription payment option (exact structure still being defined on my end)

I don't need a detailed Phase 2 proposal yet, but I'd like your high-level read on how Phase 1 architecture choices might affect Phase 2, so we don't build something in Phase 1 that has to be torn out later.

---

## Deliverables (Phase 1)
- Live, working checkout on all contract products
- PDF documents generated and delivered only after confirmed payment
- Working contact form that reliably delivers submissions
- Brief written documentation of what you built, including any accounts/services created (Stripe, email service, hosting) and how to access them
- A short written note on Phase 2 considerations, per above

## In Your Proposal, Please Include
- Relevant experience with Stripe integration and PDF generation for a small business — examples/links welcome
- Your recommended approach for the "paywall gating" requirement in #2 above
- Your recommended transactional email service and why
- Whether you're available and interested in continuing to Phase 2 after this phase wraps
- Estimated timeline and cost for Phase 1 specifically (flat rate preferred over hourly, if possible)
- Any questions about scope before we start

A Note on Fit
I'm not a developer, so I'm relying on you to flag anything in this brief that doesn't make sense technically, and to explain trade-offs in plain language as we go. Clear communication matters as much as technical skill for this project — especially since this is a multi-phase relationship, not a one-off task.

A Note On Time
This project is time sensitive.  I would like to have it completed as quickly as possible.

title: WordPress Recurring 500/503 Errors, Fatal Theme Bug, Slow Queries (Custom Theme + Events Calendar)
description:
Our WordPress site (Cloudways-hosted, custom theme "mangala-shri-bhuti," running WooCommerce + The Events Calendar) has had a pattern of recurring instability over the past several days — different specific errors each time, but a consistent shape: slow Events Calendar queries, PHP worker exhaustion, and now a fatal PHP error, together causing intermittent outages for both site visitors and backend/admin users.

What we know so far (from our host's diagnostics and our own investigation):

A fatal PHP error in our custom theme, header-dharma-post-meta-info.php line 6 — appears to loop over post taxonomy terms without handling the case where get_the_terms() returns false (no terms assigned). Currently causing ~50% of page loads to fail with HTTP 500.

The Events Calendar plugin's date-filtered/paginated pages are taking 150-255 seconds to load, tying up PHP workers and contributing to server-wide slowdowns (load average 26-43 on a 4-core server).

Our PHP-FPM configuration allows up to 40 concurrent workers × 2GB memory each (80GB theoretical) against only 8GB of actual server RAM — a mismatch that has previously caused repeated out-of-memory crashes.

We enabled Redis at the server level, but WordPress may not yet be fully using it as a persistent object cache — needs verification.

We identified and blocked two bot IPs that were aggressively crawling paginated event-archive URLs, which had been a contributing traffic trigger.

A cosmetic PHP warning in Elementor (dynamic-tags) has also appeared in logs but is confirmed unrelated to the outages.

What we need: someone who can look at this holistically rather than just patch the latest reported error — diagnose whether these are one root cause manifesting differently under load, or several distinct issues, fix the theme bug, resolve or substantially improve the Events Calendar query performance, correct the PHP worker/memory configuration, and confirm the object cache is actually functioning. We can provide full hosting diagnostic reports, server access, and everything we've investigated so far.

Deliverables:

Fatal theme error fixed and verified (including for posts/admin views with no assigned topic)

Events Calendar date-filtered pages loading in a reasonable time

PHP-FPM worker/memory settings corrected to match actual server resources

Object cache confirmed active and functioning (via WordPress Site Health)

Brief written report: root cause(s) identified, what was changed, and any remaining risk

title: Technical content manager - AI-driven CMS migration + ongoing site work
description:

title: WordPress + Google Ads Tracking EXPERT Needed Now, Then Full Website Redesign
description:
Do NOT apply by emailing or calling privately. You MUST apply through UpWork.

WordPress Developer Needed – Google Ads Tracking, GTM, Lead Attribution & Website Redesign

Project Overview:

We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer with strong Google Ads conversion tracking, Google Tag Manager, dataLayer, lead attribution, CRM integration, and website performance experience.

This project will be completed in two phases.

Phase 1 – Update the Existing Website

Before the website redesign begins, we need our existing WordPress website updated so it meets the technical requirements necessary to begin running and accurately tracking Google Ads.

The current website has never been properly set up for paid advertising or conversion tracking.

Our immediate goal is to implement the required tracking, attribution, lead capture, call tracking readiness, and performance improvements on the existing website first.

We do NOT want to wait for the redesign before we can begin advertising.

Phase 2 – Full Website Redesign

After the existing site is properly configured and verified, we will move into a complete website redesign/rebuild.

The redesigned website must retain and fully support all of the tracking, attribution, lead-generation, performance, and advertising requirements established during Phase 1.

The redesign cannot break, remove, simplify, or reduce the tracking functionality implemented on the current site.

We are looking for someone who can ideally handle both phases and build the infrastructure correctly the first time.

PHASE 1 – EXISTING WEBSITE

The first priority is making the current website Google Ads-ready.

Before redesign work begins, we need the following implemented and tested.

Google Tag Manager & Conversion Tracking

• Install/configure Google Tag Manager across the existing website
• Ensure GTM is the primary location for analytics and advertising tracking
• Remove or prevent duplicate tracking scripts
• Configure a properly initialized dataLayer
• Ensure conversion events fire only after confirmed actions
• Give our marketing team appropriate GTM access and publishing capability

Required events include:

• generate_lead
• phone_click
• form_start
• form_error
• project_view

The generate_lead event must include qualifying information such as:

• Unique reference ID
• Project type
• Budget range
• Timeline
• Service area
• Form location

 Google Ads Attribution

The existing website must capture Google advertising identifiers and campaign parameters when visitors arrive from advertisements.

This includes support for:

• GCLID
• GBRAID
• WBRAID
• UTM parameters

These identifiers must:

• Be captured upon arrival
• Survive navigation throughout the website
• Be retained for up to 90 days
• Remain available if a visitor leaves and returns later
• Be submitted with the enquiry
• Reach the CRM along with the lead record

Ultimately, we need to be able to connect:

Google Ad → Website Visitor → Lead → CRM → Signed Customer

This attribution chain is one of the most important requirements of the project.

Existing Lead Forms

The existing enquiry forms need to be updated so they collect better lead qualification information.

Required fields will include:

• Name
• Email
• Phone
• Project type
• Budget range
• Project timeline
• Property/service location

Additional fields may include:

• Property type
• Whether a landscape design already exists
• How the customer heard about us

Forms must also:

• Capture advertising attribution data
• Generate a unique reference ID
• Pass attribution into the CRM
• Trigger conversion events only after confirmed submission
• Deliver leads in real time
• Store a backup copy of each enquiry
• Redirect successful enquiries to a dedicated confirmation URL

Gravity Forms experience is strongly preferred.

Phone Tracking Readiness

The current website must also be prepared for call tracking.

This includes:

• Phone number prominently displayed
• Phone number in the header
• Tap-to-call functionality on mobile
• Proper HTML telephone links
• phone_click tracking through GTM
• Stable markup that supports dynamic number replacement
• Call tracking scripts loaded through GTM rather than hardcoded

Existing Website Performance

The existing site may require optimization before advertising begins.

We want campaign and landing pages to target:

• Lighthouse Mobile Performance Score of 90+
• Largest Contentful Paint under 2.0 seconds
• Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1
• Landing page weight under approximately 500 KB

Performance testing must be completed with the real production tracking scripts enabled.

Phase 1 Completion

We will consider Phase 1 complete when the existing website has been tested and verified for:

• GTM installation
• Correct lead conversion tracking
• Correct phone tracking
• Lead qualification parameters
• GCLID/UTM persistence
• Return-visit attribution
• CRM handoff
• Unique reference IDs
• Spam protection
• Confirmation pages
• Landing-page tracking compatibility
• Mobile performance

Once this is working correctly, we can begin actively running paid advertising while Phase 2 is developed.

PHASE 2 – COMPLETE WEBSITE REDESIGN

After Phase 1 is complete, we will redesign the website.

This will involve rebuilding the site into a more modern, professional, conversion-focused website for an established high-end landscape design and construction company.

However, the redesigned website must meet all of the same technical standards implemented during Phase 1.

The redesign must preserve:

• Google Tag Manager infrastructure
• Google Ads conversion tracking
• dataLayer events
• GCLID/GBRAID/WBRAID attribution
• UTM tracking
• CRM lead attribution
• Enhanced Conversion capability
• Form tracking
• Call tracking capability
• Unique lead/reference IDs
• Landing page functionality
• Performance standards

Tracking should be treated as part of the website architecture, not something added as an afterthought once the redesign is complete.

Landing Page System

The redesigned site must include reusable campaign landing-page templates.

Our internal marketing team must be able to create new landing pages without hiring a developer every time.

We need control over:

• Page title
• Meta description
• Canonical URL
• Index/noindex
• Form selection
• Service
• Service area/city
• Page content

Landing pages must continue to function correctly when tracking parameters are appended to the URL.

Website Ownership

The redesigned website must remain fully controlled by our company.

We require:

• Company-owned WordPress installation
• Company-controlled hosting
• Company-controlled third-party accounts
• No proprietary agency platform
• No agency lock-in
• Full administrative access

Performance Requirements for the Redesigned Website

The redesigned website must meet or exceed the same performance standards established during Phase 1.

Targets include:

• Lighthouse Mobile Performance Score: 90+
• Largest Contentful Paint: under 2 seconds
• Cumulative Layout Shift: under 0.1
• Campaign landing pages: approximately 500 KB or less where practical

These metrics must be tested with the actual production tracking stack active.

Technical Environment

Current/expected environment:

• WordPress
• Elementor / Hello Elementor
• Gravity Forms preferred
• Company-controlled hosting
• Google Tag Manager
• Google Analytics 4
• Google Ads

Future integrations may include:

• CRM integration
• Offline conversion imports
• Google Ads Enhanced Conversions
• Dynamic call tracking
• Server-side Google Tag Manager
• A/B landing-page testing

The website architecture should allow these systems to be added without requiring another rebuild.

Who We Are Looking For

Please apply only if you have strong experience in several of the following areas:

• WordPress development
• WordPress redesigns
• Elementor
• Gravity Forms
• Google Tag Manager
• GA4
• Google Ads conversion tracking
• Custom dataLayer implementation
• Enhanced Conversions
• GCLID attribution
• UTM attribution
• CRM integrations
• Webhooks and APIs
• Offline conversion tracking
• Dynamic call tracking
• WordPress speed optimization
• Cloudflare/security configuration

We are NOT looking for someone whose experience is primarily website appearance or Elementor page design.

We need someone who understands both website development and the technical infrastructure behind paid lead generation.

When Applying

Please answer the following:

1. Have you implemented Google Ads attribution on an existing WordPress site before a redesign?

2. Describe a project where you captured GCLID or another Google Ads identifier and passed it into a CRM.

3. Have you created custom dataLayer events through Google Tag Manager?

4. Have you implemented Google Ads Enhanced Conversions?

5. Have you worked extensively with Gravity Forms hidden fields, hooks, webhooks, or APIs?

6. How would you preserve an original Google Ads click identifier if someone returns several days later and submits a form?

7. How would you make sure generate_lead fires only after a successful submission and does not fire twice?

8. Have you implemented offline conversion tracking where a completed sale was connected back to the original advertisement?

9. Have you completed a WordPress redesign while preserving an existing GTM and attribution setup?

10. What tools do you use to test GTM, GA4, Google Ads conversions, dataLayer events, attribution, and website performance?

11. Please provide examples of relevant websites or projects.

12. What is your hourly or project rate?

13. Please provide a time estimate for:
    • Phase 1 – Updating and configuring the existing website
    • Phase 2 – Full website redesign

We prefer someone who is available to work full-time on this project now as the company is in a seasonal crunch and time is running short. We also prefer someone who can complete both phases and remain available for future technical support as our Google Ads campaigns and lead-tracking systems expand.

title: REQUEST - Senior Full-Stack Developer (NON GREENFIELD)
description:
Revision Note — v1.4 (identity & tracking — a first-class citizen). Made explicit that a service_request is a first-class
object in the shared operational object model (Library/Board v1.5 §2), carrying the platform-standard identity ( uuid
VARCHAR(36) + human-readable reference_id , exactly as organizations/hotels do per migration 010), tenant scope, lifecycle,
immutable provenance, and relationship links — defined once, reused, never a parallel identity or tracking scheme. Added §11A
Tracked with everything else — toward outcomes: requests correlate to the guest stay, room/asset, property, and time so
reactive-work performance reports alongside all operational data and rolls up toward guest-experience outcomes (OHI). Object
model, audit, and milestones updated.
Revision Note — v1.3 (notifications & delivery, reconciled to Communications Layer v4). Added §7B Notifications & delivery
— an event-based model where Requests emits its lifecycle events and subscribes to Comms intent events, never reaching into the
Comms layer (Comms v4 §23 anti-rewrite spine). Channels: live voice announce, push via the Thin Native Container (Comms
§20), in-app, email, SMS fallback — with delivery owned by Comms/the container, not Requests. Reuses Comms addressing
resolvers (presence / department / position / area / board) instead of inventing routing. Adds a configurable settings matrix (event ×
channel × role, org/property defaults, shift-aware quiet hours, escalation ladder, safety override). §9 corrected: Comms transcribes +
classifies + emits the intent event; Requests is the consumer (the one Comms v4 says is "built later in Agenda/PDEE"), with
acknowledge ↔ request correlation so a spoken "taking it" can't drift from an open request. Dependencies, milestones, audit
updated.
Revision Note — v1.2 (communication intelligence + share + view receipts). Per direction, the request's communication is
treated as a first-class data source — not just a thread to read later. Added: share (give someone visibility without making them an
owner — a viewer grant via the existing chat participant role); view receipts (delivered → viewed → acknowledged, reusing
messages_seen + last_read_at , with unviewed-by-assignee surfaced for accountability); voice notes transcribed into the
searchable thread; and Intelligence over the thread (§8) — theme/asset extraction ("TV remote again"), sentiment/guest-impact
flags, thread summaries for handoff, and resolution-knowledge capture that mines how a request was fixed and drafts it into the
Library. All advisory, tenant-scoped, and functional with Intelligence disabled.
Revision Note — v1.1 (collaboration added). A gap was caught: v1.0 covered evidence-on-close but not the live, day-to-day team
interaction on a request — comments, responses, adding people, and attaching photos/files mid-flight — which the legacy system
had. §7A is added to specify request collaboration, built entirely on existing infrastructure: the tie-message thread pattern
( message_model ), the chat participant model ( Chat_model — add/remove people, search), and the governed media spine
( Media_attachment / Media_file / Media_link ). No second chat system is built. Object model, dependencies, milestones,
and audit updated to match.
Revision Note — v1.0 (code-audit reconciliation). The develop branch was audited against this scope. Most dependencies
check out and are richer than assumed; several findings changed this document so the developer builds onto existing infrastructure
instead of reinventing it.
Confirmed present (reuse, don't rebuild): the Foundations spine — organization , hotels , hotel_branches (hotel
locations), and user_hotel_location_assignments + user_active_hotel_location for portfolio scoping; the
inventory_usage / inventory_adjustment / inventory_restock ledger (a mature subsystem); the
NotificationService library (the single notification entry point — the legacy ticket even disabled its own writes in favor of it); the
ai_governance_* layer plus ai_structured_output_model (ideal for voice → structured draft); per-user language
preferences + the translation layer; immutable audit_logs triggers.
Findings that changed the scope: (1) scoping resolves through hotel_location_id (org → hotel → location), not hotel_id
alone — corrected

This is a Two-Phase Project. I want a developer who can start with Phase 1 now and continue into Phase 2 later, so continuity matters — please speak to your availability for both phases in your proposal, even though we're scoping and pricing Phase 1 first.

I am **not technical**, so I need someone who can own this end-to-end and explain decisions in plain language, not just execute tickets.

What's Already Done
- Complete website: homepage, multiple product pages, three interactive contract-building tools, blog/resources section — all built as static HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- All visual design, branding, and copy is finalized
- The interactive questionnaires (conditional logic, live document preview) are fully functional client-side — this does not need to be rebuilt
- A "Purchase & Download" button exists on each contract tool but is currently a placeholder — it doesn't charge anyone or gate the actual document
- A contact form exists on the site but doesn't send or store submissions anywhere yet — it's a visual mockup

---

PHASE 1 (Scope This Now)

1. Stripe Integration
- Real checkout for each contract product (each is priced individually, single one-time purchase per contract)
- Handle payment confirmation before releasing any document content

2. PDF Generation + Paywall Gating
- Generate a clean, finished PDF of the completed contract from the questionnaire's answers
- Critical requirement: the complete document must only be generated/served **after** Stripe confirms payment. Right now all the document logic runs client-side, which means a determined visitor could technically view the full document text before paying — this needs to be fixed with a real backend, not just front-end tricks (disabling copy/right-click, etc., which is not real protection)
- Document should be deliverable via download link and/or email after purchase (whichever you recommend as more reliable)

3. Contact Form Backend
- The existing contact form (name, email, message) needs to actually deliver submissions — to my email inbox at minimum, or to a simple CRM/inbox tool if you think that's a better long-term fit
- Please recommend the simplest reliable option (e.g., a transactional email service) rather than the most complex

**Note:** Items #2 and #3 both likely depend on the same piece of infrastructure — a transactional email service (e.g., SendGrid, Postmark, or similar) for delivering PDFs and forwarding form submissions. Please account for that shared setup in your Phase 1 estimate rather than treating them as fully separate systems.

---

PHASE 2 (Scope Later, Described Here for Context)

- User accounts (signup/login)
- Saved drafts — a visitor should be able to start a questionnaire, leave, and come back later to finish where they left off. This is already promised on the site's FAQ page, so it's a real commitment, not a stretch goal.
- Subscription payments — in addition to the one-time purchases from Phase 1, a recurring/subscription payment option (exact structure still being defined on my end)

I don't need a detailed Phase 2 proposal yet, but I'd like your high-level read on how Phase 1 architecture choices might affect Phase 2, so we don't build something in Phase 1 that has to be torn out later.

---

## Deliverables (Phase 1)
- Live, working checkout on all contract products
- PDF documents generated and delivered only after confirmed payment
- Working contact form that reliably delivers submissions
- Brief written documentation of what you built, including any accounts/services created (Stripe, email service, hosting) and how to access them
- A short written note on Phase 2 considerations, per above

## In Your Proposal, Please Include
- Relevant experience with Stripe integration and PDF generation for a small business — examples/links welcome
- Your recommended approach for the "paywall gating" requirement in #2 above
- Your recommended transactional email service and why
- Whether you're available and interested in continuing to Phase 2 after this phase wraps
- Estimated timeline and cost for Phase 1 specifically (flat rate preferred over hourly, if possible)
- Any questions about scope before we start

A Note on Fit
I'm not a developer, so I'm relying on you to flag anything in this brief that doesn't make sense technically, and to explain trade-offs in plain language as we go. Clear communication matters as much as technical skill for this project — especially since this is a multi-phase relationship, not a one-off task.

A Note On Time
This project is time sensitive.  I would like to have it completed as quickly as possible.

title: WordPress Recurring 500/503 Errors, Fatal Theme Bug, Slow Queries (Custom Theme + Events Calendar)
description:
Our WordPress site (Cloudways-hosted, custom theme "mangala-shri-bhuti," running WooCommerce + The Events Calendar) has had a pattern of recurring instability over the past several days — different specific errors each time, but a consistent shape: slow Events Calendar queries, PHP worker exhaustion, and now a fatal PHP error, together causing intermittent outages for both site visitors and backend/admin users.

What we know so far (from our host's diagnostics and our own investigation):

A fatal PHP error in our custom theme, header-dharma-post-meta-info.php line 6 — appears to loop over post taxonomy terms without handling the case where get_the_terms() returns false (no terms assigned). Currently causing ~50% of page loads to fail with HTTP 500.

The Events Calendar plugin's date-filtered/paginated pages are taking 150-255 seconds to load, tying up PHP workers and contributing to server-wide slowdowns (load average 26-43 on a 4-core server).

Our PHP-FPM configuration allows up to 40 concurrent workers × 2GB memory each (80GB theoretical) against only 8GB of actual server RAM — a mismatch that has previously caused repeated out-of-memory crashes.

We enabled Redis at the server level, but WordPress may not yet be fully using it as a persistent object cache — needs verification.

We identified and blocked two bot IPs that were aggressively crawling paginated event-archive URLs, which had been a contributing traffic trigger.

A cosmetic PHP warning in Elementor (dynamic-tags) has also appeared in logs but is confirmed unrelated to the outages.

What we need: someone who can look at this holistically rather than just patch the latest reported error — diagnose whether these are one root cause manifesting differently under load, or several distinct issues, fix the theme bug, resolve or substantially improve the Events Calendar query performance, correct the PHP worker/memory configuration, and confirm the object cache is actually functioning. We can provide full hosting diagnostic reports, server access, and everything we've investigated so far.

Deliverables:

Fatal theme error fixed and verified (including for posts/admin views with no assigned topic)

Events Calendar date-filtered pages loading in a reasonable time

PHP-FPM worker/memory settings corrected to match actual server resources

Object cache confirmed active and functioning (via WordPress Site Health)

Brief written report: root cause(s) identified, what was changed, and any remaining risk

title: WordPress + Google Ads Tracking EXPERT Needed Now, Then Full Website Redesign
description:
Do NOT apply by emailing or calling privately. You MUST apply through UpWork.

WordPress Developer Needed – Google Ads Tracking, GTM, Lead Attribution & Website Redesign

Project Overview:

We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer with strong Google Ads conversion tracking, Google Tag Manager, dataLayer, lead attribution, CRM integration, and website performance experience.

This project will be completed in two phases.

Phase 1 – Update the Existing Website

Before the website redesign begins, we need our existing WordPress website updated so it meets the technical requirements necessary to begin running and accurately tracking Google Ads.

The current website has never been properly set up for paid advertising or conversion tracking.

Our immediate goal is to implement the required tracking, attribution, lead capture, call tracking readiness, and performance improvements on the existing website first.

We do NOT want to wait for the redesign before we can begin advertising.

Phase 2 – Full Website Redesign

After the existing site is properly configured and verified, we will move into a complete website redesign/rebuild.

The redesigned website must retain and fully support all of the tracking, attribution, lead-generation, performance, and advertising requirements established during Phase 1.

The redesign cannot break, remove, simplify, or reduce the tracking functionality implemented on the current site.

We are looking for someone who can ideally handle both phases and build the infrastructure correctly the first time.

PHASE 1 – EXISTING WEBSITE

The first priority is making the current website Google Ads-ready.

Before redesign work begins, we need the following implemented and tested.

Google Tag Manager & Conversion Tracking

• Install/configure Google Tag Manager across the existing website
• Ensure GTM is the primary location for analytics and advertising tracking
• Remove or prevent duplicate tracking scripts
• Configure a properly initialized dataLayer
• Ensure conversion events fire only after confirmed actions
• Give our marketing team appropriate GTM access and publishing capability

Required events include:

• generate_lead
• phone_click
• form_start
• form_error
• project_view

The generate_lead event must include qualifying information such as:

• Unique reference ID
• Project type
• Budget range
• Timeline
• Service area
• Form location

 Google Ads Attribution

The existing website must capture Google advertising identifiers and campaign parameters when visitors arrive from advertisements.

This includes support for:

• GCLID
• GBRAID
• WBRAID
• UTM parameters

These identifiers must:

• Be captured upon arrival
• Survive navigation throughout the website
• Be retained for up to 90 days
• Remain available if a visitor leaves and returns later
• Be submitted with the enquiry
• Reach the CRM along with the lead record

Ultimately, we need to be able to connect:

Google Ad → Website Visitor → Lead → CRM → Signed Customer

This attribution chain is one of the most important requirements of the project.

Existing Lead Forms

The existing enquiry forms need to be updated so they collect better lead qualification information.

Required fields will include:

• Name
• Email
• Phone
• Project type
• Budget range
• Project timeline
• Property/service location

Additional fields may include:

• Property type
• Whether a landscape design already exists
• How the customer heard about us

Forms must also:

• Capture advertising attribution data
• Generate a unique reference ID
• Pass attribution into the CRM
• Trigger conversion events only after confirmed submission
• Deliver leads in real time
• Store a backup copy of each enquiry
• Redirect successful enquiries to a dedicated confirmation URL

Gravity Forms experience is strongly preferred.

Phone Tracking Readiness

The current website must also be prepared for call tracking.

This includes:

• Phone number prominently displayed
• Phone number in the header
• Tap-to-call functionality on mobile
• Proper HTML telephone links
• phone_click tracking through GTM
• Stable markup that supports dynamic number replacement
• Call tracking scripts loaded through GTM rather than hardcoded

Existing Website Performance

The existing site may require optimization before advertising begins.

We want campaign and landing pages to target:

• Lighthouse Mobile Performance Score of 90+
• Largest Contentful Paint under 2.0 seconds
• Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1
• Landing page weight under approximately 500 KB

Performance testing must be completed with the real production tracking scripts enabled.

Phase 1 Completion

We will consider Phase 1 complete when the existing website has been tested and verified for:

• GTM installation
• Correct lead conversion tracking
• Correct phone tracking
• Lead qualification parameters
• GCLID/UTM persistence
• Return-visit attribution
• CRM handoff
• Unique reference IDs
• Spam protection
• Confirmation pages
• Landing-page tracking compatibility
• Mobile performance

Once this is working correctly, we can begin actively running paid advertising while Phase 2 is developed.

PHASE 2 – COMPLETE WEBSITE REDESIGN

After Phase 1 is complete, we will redesign the website.

This will involve rebuilding the site into a more modern, professional, conversion-focused website for an established high-end landscape design and construction company.

However, the redesigned website must meet all of the same technical standards implemented during Phase 1.

The redesign must preserve:

• Google Tag Manager infrastructure
• Google Ads conversion tracking
• dataLayer events
• GCLID/GBRAID/WBRAID attribution
• UTM tracking
• CRM lead attribution
• Enhanced Conversion capability
• Form tracking
• Call tracking capability
• Unique lead/reference IDs
• Landing page functionality
• Performance standards

Tracking should be treated as part of the website architecture, not something added as an afterthought once the redesign is complete.

Landing Page System

The redesigned site must include reusable campaign landing-page templates.

Our internal marketing team must be able to create new landing pages without hiring a developer every time.

We need control over:

• Page title
• Meta description
• Canonical URL
• Index/noindex
• Form selection
• Service
• Service area/city
• Page content

Landing pages must continue to function correctly when tracking parameters are appended to the URL.

Website Ownership

The redesigned website must remain fully controlled by our company.

We require:

• Company-owned WordPress installation
• Company-controlled hosting
• Company-controlled third-party accounts
• No proprietary agency platform
• No agency lock-in
• Full administrative access

Performance Requirements for the Redesigned Website

The redesigned website must meet or exceed the same performance standards established during Phase 1.

Targets include:

• Lighthouse Mobile Performance Score: 90+
• Largest Contentful Paint: under 2 seconds
• Cumulative Layout Shift: under 0.1
• Campaign landing pages: approximately 500 KB or less where practical

These metrics must be tested with the actual production tracking stack active.

Technical Environment

Current/expected environment:

• WordPress
• Elementor / Hello Elementor
• Gravity Forms preferred
• Company-controlled hosting
• Google Tag Manager
• Google Analytics 4
• Google Ads

Future integrations may include:

• CRM integration
• Offline conversion imports
• Google Ads Enhanced Conversions
• Dynamic call tracking
• Server-side Google Tag Manager
• A/B landing-page testing

The website architecture should allow these systems to be added without requiring another rebuild.

Who We Are Looking For

Please apply only if you have strong experience in several of the following areas:

• WordPress development
• WordPress redesigns
• Elementor
• Gravity Forms
• Google Tag Manager
• GA4
• Google Ads conversion tracking
• Custom dataLayer implementation
• Enhanced Conversions
• GCLID attribution
• UTM attribution
• CRM integrations
• Webhooks and APIs
• Offline conversion tracking
• Dynamic call tracking
• WordPress speed optimization
• Cloudflare/security configuration

We are NOT looking for someone whose experience is primarily website appearance or Elementor page design.

We need someone who understands both website development and the technical infrastructure behind paid lead generation.

When Applying

Please answer the following:

1. Have you implemented Google Ads attribution on an existing WordPress site before a redesign?

2. Describe a project where you captured GCLID or another Google Ads identifier and passed it into a CRM.

3. Have you created custom dataLayer events through Google Tag Manager?

4. Have you implemented Google Ads Enhanced Conversions?

5. Have you worked extensively with Gravity Forms hidden fields, hooks, webhooks, or APIs?

6. How would you preserve an original Google Ads click identifier if someone returns several days later and submits a form?

7. How would you make sure generate_lead fires only after a successful submission and does not fire twice?

8. Have you implemented offline conversion tracking where a completed sale was connected back to the original advertisement?

9. Have you completed a WordPress redesign while preserving an existing GTM and attribution setup?

10. What tools do you use to test GTM, GA4, Google Ads conversions, dataLayer events, attribution, and website performance?

11. Please provide examples of relevant websites or projects.

12. What is your hourly or project rate?

13. Please provide a time estimate for:
    • Phase 1 – Updating and configuring the existing website
    • Phase 2 – Full website redesign

We prefer someone who is available to work full-time on this project now as the company is in a seasonal crunch and time is running short. We also prefer someone who can complete both phases and remain available for future technical support as our Google Ads campaigns and lead-tracking systems expand.

VARCHAR(36) + human-readable reference_id , exactly as organizations/hotels do per migration 010), tenant scope, lifecycle,

title: WooCommerce Website Project Scope
description:
Beyond the build itself, here are the specific things I'd like included as part of this project:

1. Product schema markup + SEO-friendly URLs/meta data (per product, using my keywords) — foundation for Google discoverability
2. Fast site speed (image compression, CDN, minimal plugins) — impacts both SEO ranking and conversion
3. Frictionless mobile checkout (guest checkout, 1-click pay like Shop Pay/PayPal Express, minimal form fields) — 60-70% of traffic is mobile
4. High-impact product pages (benefit-driven copy, multiple photos, video, clear specs) — converts visitors once SEO gets them there
5. Trust signals sitewide (badges near Add to Cart, visible return policy, contact/chat widget) — new stores fail most often on trust
6. Social proof / reviews (UGC) via Judge.me/Loox/Yotpo — reinforces trust, doubles as fresh SEO content
7. Full analytics tracking pre-launch (GA4 + e-commerce tracking, Meta Pixel/CAPI, GTM) — needed to measure and optimize post-launch
8. Abandoned cart recovery (email/SMS sequence) — recovers otherwise-lost sales passively
9. Email/SMS capture with welcome offer — captures first-time visitors who aren't ready to buy yet
10. AOV boosters (free shipping threshold, in-cart upsells) — increases revenue per visitor

A few things that matter a lot to me for this project:

title: WordPress Recurring 500/503 Errors, Fatal Theme Bug, Slow Queries (Custom Theme + Events Calendar)
description:
Our WordPress site (Cloudways-hosted, custom theme "mangala-shri-bhuti," running WooCommerce + The Events Calendar) has had a pattern of recurring instability over the past several days — different specific errors each time, but a consistent shape: slow Events Calendar queries, PHP worker exhaustion, and now a fatal PHP error, together causing intermittent outages for both site visitors and backend/admin users.

What we know so far (from our host's diagnostics and our own investigation):

A fatal PHP error in our custom theme, header-dharma-post-meta-info.php line 6 — appears to loop over post taxonomy terms without handling the case where get_the_terms() returns false (no terms assigned). Currently causing ~50% of page loads to fail with HTTP 500.

The Events Calendar plugin's date-filtered/paginated pages are taking 150-255 seconds to load, tying up PHP workers and contributing to server-wide slowdowns (load average 26-43 on a 4-core server).

Our PHP-FPM configuration allows up to 40 concurrent workers × 2GB memory each (80GB theoretical) against only 8GB of actual server RAM — a mismatch that has previously caused repeated out-of-memory crashes.

We enabled Redis at the server level, but WordPress may not yet be fully using it as a persistent object cache — needs verification.

We identified and blocked two bot IPs that were aggressively crawling paginated event-archive URLs, which had been a contributing traffic trigger.

A cosmetic PHP warning in Elementor (dynamic-tags) has also appeared in logs but is confirmed unrelated to the outages.

What we need: someone who can look at this holistically rather than just patch the latest reported error — diagnose whether these are one root cause manifesting differently under load, or several distinct issues, fix the theme bug, resolve or substantially improve the Events Calendar query performance, correct the PHP worker/memory configuration, and confirm the object cache is actually functioning. We can provide full hosting diagnostic reports, server access, and everything we've investigated so far.

Deliverables:

Fatal theme error fixed and verified (including for posts/admin views with no assigned topic)

Events Calendar date-filtered pages loading in a reasonable time

PHP-FPM worker/memory settings corrected to match actual server resources

Object cache confirmed active and functioning (via WordPress Site Health)

Brief written report: root cause(s) identified, what was changed, and any remaining risk

model, audit, and milestones updated.

Comms layer (Comms v4 §23 anti-rewrite spine). Channels: live voice announce, push via the Thin Native Container (Comms
§20), in-app, email, SMS fallback — with delivery owned by Comms/the container, not Requests. Reuses Comms addressing
resolvers (presence / department / position / area / board) instead of inventing routing. Adds a configurable settings matrix (event ×
channel × role, org/property defaults, shift-aware quiet hours, escalation ladder, safety override). §9 corrected: Comms transcribes +
classifies + emits the intent event; Requests is the consumer (the one Comms v4 says is "built later in Agenda/PDEE"), with
acknowledge ↔ request correlation so a spoken "taking it" can't drift from an open request. Dependencies, milestones, audit
updated.

treated as a first-class data source — not just a thread to read later. Added: share (give someone visibility without making them an
owner — a viewer grant via the existing chat participant role); view receipts (delivered → viewed → acknowledged, reusing
messages_seen + last_read_at , with unviewed-by-assignee surfaced for accountability); voice notes transcribed into the
searchable thread; and Intelligence over the thread (§8) — theme/asset extraction ("TV remote again"), sentiment/guest-impact
flags, thread summaries for handoff, and resolution-knowledge capture that mines how a request was fixed and drafts it into the
Library. All advisory, tenant-scoped, and functional with Intelligence disabled.

interaction on a request — comments, responses, adding people, and attaching photos/files mid-flight — which the legacy system
had. §7A is added to specify request collaboration, built entirely on existing infrastructure: the tie-message thread pattern
( message_model ), the chat participant model ( Chat_model — add/remove people, search), and the governed media spine
( Media_attachment / Media_file / Media_link ). No second chat system is built. Object model, dependencies, milestones,
and audit updated to match.
Revision Note — v1.0 (code-audit reconciliation). The develop branch was audited against this scope. Most dependencies
check out and are richer than assumed; several findings changed this document so the developer builds onto existing infrastructure
instead of reinventing it.
Confirmed present (reuse, don't rebuild): the Foundations spine — organization , hotels , hotel_branches (hotel
locations), and user_hotel_location_assignments + user_active_hotel_location for portfolio scoping; the
inventory_usage / inventory_adjustment / inventory_restock ledger (a mature subsystem); the
NotificationService library (the single notification entry point — the legacy ticket even disabled its own writes in favor of it); the
ai_governance_* layer plus ai_structured_output_model (ideal for voice → structured draft); per-user language
preferences + the translation layer; immutable audit_logs triggers.
Findings that changed the scope: (1) scoping resolves through hotel_location_id (org → hotel → location), not hotel_id
alone — corrected

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.
