Revision Note — v1.4 (identity & tracking — a first-class citizen). Made explicit that a service_request is a first-class
object in the shared operational object model (Library/Board v1.5 §2), carrying the platform-standard identity ( uuid
VARCHAR(36) + human-readable reference_id , exactly as organizations/hotels do per migration 010), tenant scope, lifecycle,
immutable provenance, and relationship links — defined once, reused, never a parallel identity or tracking scheme. Added §11A
Tracked with everything else — toward outcomes: requests correlate to the guest stay, room/asset, property, and time so
reactive-work performance reports alongside all operational data and rolls up toward guest-experience outcomes (OHI). Object
model, audit, and milestones updated.
Revision Note — v1.3 (notifications & delivery, reconciled to Communications Layer v4). Added §7B Notifications & delivery
— an event-based model where Requests emits its lifecycle events and subscribes to Comms intent events, never reaching into the
Comms layer (Comms v4 §23 anti-rewrite spine). Channels: live voice announce, push via the Thin Native Container (Comms
§20), in-app, email, SMS fallback — with delivery owned by Comms/the container, not Requests. Reuses Comms addressing
resolvers (presence / department / position / area / board) instead of inventing routing. Adds a configurable settings matrix (event ×
channel × role, org/property defaults, shift-aware quiet hours, escalation ladder, safety override). §9 corrected: Comms transcribes +
classifies + emits the intent event; Requests is the consumer (the one Comms v4 says is "built later in Agenda/PDEE"), with
acknowledge ↔ request correlation so a spoken "taking it" can't drift from an open request. Dependencies, milestones, audit
updated.
Revision Note — v1.2 (communication intelligence + share + view receipts). Per direction, the request's communication is
treated as a first-class data source — not just a thread to read later. Added: share (give someone visibility without making them an
owner — a viewer grant via the existing chat participant role); view receipts (delivered → viewed → acknowledged, reusing
messages_seen + last_read_at , with unviewed-by-assignee surfaced for accountability); voice notes transcribed into the
searchable thread; and Intelligence over the thread (§8) — theme/asset extraction ("TV remote again"), sentiment/guest-impact
flags, thread summaries for handoff, and resolution-knowledge capture that mines how a request was fixed and drafts it into the
Library. All advisory, tenant-scoped, and functional with Intelligence disabled.
Revision Note — v1.1 (collaboration added). A gap was caught: v1.0 covered evidence-on-close but not the live, day-to-day team
interaction on a request — comments, responses, adding people, and attaching photos/files mid-flight — which the legacy system
had. §7A is added to specify request collaboration, built entirely on existing infrastructure: the tie-message thread pattern
( message_model ), the chat participant model ( Chat_model — add/remove people, search), and the governed media spine
( Media_attachment / Media_file / Media_link ). No second chat system is built. Object model, dependencies, milestones,
and audit updated to match.
Revision Note — v1.0 (code-audit reconciliation). The develop branch was audited against this scope. Most dependencies
check out and are richer than assumed; several findings changed this document so the developer builds onto existing infrastructure
instead of reinventing it.
Confirmed present (reuse, don't rebuild): the Foundations spine — organization , hotels , hotel_branches (hotel
locations), and user_hotel_location_assignments + user_active_hotel_location for portfolio scoping; the
inventory_usage / inventory_adjustment / inventory_restock ledger (a mature subsystem); the
NotificationService library (the single notification entry point — the legacy ticket even disabled its own writes in favor of it); the
ai_governance_* layer plus ai_structured_output_model (ideal for voice → structured draft); per-user language
preferences + the translation layer; immutable audit_logs triggers.
Findings that changed the scope: (1) scoping resolves through hotel_location_id (org → hotel → location), not hotel_id
alone — corrected

title: WooCommerce Website Project Scope
description:
Beyond the build itself, here are the specific things I'd like included as part of this project:

1. Product schema markup + SEO-friendly URLs/meta data (per product, using my keywords) — foundation for Google discoverability
2. Fast site speed (image compression, CDN, minimal plugins) — impacts both SEO ranking and conversion
3. Frictionless mobile checkout (guest checkout, 1-click pay like Shop Pay/PayPal Express, minimal form fields) — 60-70% of traffic is mobile
4. High-impact product pages (benefit-driven copy, multiple photos, video, clear specs) — converts visitors once SEO gets them there
5. Trust signals sitewide (badges near Add to Cart, visible return policy, contact/chat widget) — new stores fail most often on trust
6. Social proof / reviews (UGC) via Judge.me/Loox/Yotpo — reinforces trust, doubles as fresh SEO content
7. Full analytics tracking pre-launch (GA4 + e-commerce tracking, Meta Pixel/CAPI, GTM) — needed to measure and optimize post-launch
8. Abandoned cart recovery (email/SMS sequence) — recovers otherwise-lost sales passively
9. Email/SMS capture with welcome offer — captures first-time visitors who aren't ready to buy yet
10. AOV boosters (free shipping threshold, in-cart upsells) — increases revenue per visitor

A few things that matter a lot to me for this project:

- Full ownership: I need complete ownership of the website, theme, plugins, and all files/credentials once the project is done. No lock-in.
- Full transparency: I'd like clear communication throughout — what's being installed, why, and access to everything (hosting, admin, plugin licenses, etc.) as we go, not just at the end.
- Trust: This is important to me, so I'm looking for someone reliable who works cleanly and explains me with transparency on what they do.

Could you share:
1. Examples of WooCommerce sites you've built (ideally similar product-line/e-commerce launches)
2. Your general process and timeline for a build of this scope
3. Your experience with the items listed above (SEO, checkout optimization, cart recovery, analytics, etc.)
4. How you handle ownership/transfer of credentials, licenses, and code

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Neel

title: Web Developer Needed: Backend Integration for Equine Steward (Phased Project)
description:
Equine Steward is a website selling customizable legal contracts for horse owners (leases, sale agreements). The front end is fully built — homepage, product pages, and interactive contract-questionnaire tools are live and functional. What's missing is the backend: real payments, real document delivery, and (in a later phase) user accounts.

This is a Two-Phase Project. I want a developer who can start with Phase 1 now and continue into Phase 2 later, so continuity matters — please speak to your availability for both phases in your proposal, even though we're scoping and pricing Phase 1 first.

I am **not technical**, so I need someone who can own this end-to-end and explain decisions in plain language, not just execute tickets.

What's Already Done
- Complete website: homepage, multiple product pages, three interactive contract-building tools, blog/resources section — all built as static HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- All visual design, branding, and copy is finalized
- The interactive questionnaires (conditional logic, live document preview) are fully functional client-side — this does not need to be rebuilt
- A "Purchase & Download" button exists on each contract tool but is currently a placeholder — it doesn't charge anyone or gate the actual document
- A contact form exists on the site but doesn't send or store submissions anywhere yet — it's a visual mockup

---

PHASE 1 (Scope This Now)

1. Stripe Integration
- Real checkout for each contract product (each is priced individually, single one-time purchase per contract)
- Handle payment confirmation before releasing any document content

2. PDF Generation + Paywall Gating
- Generate a clean, finished PDF of the completed contract from the questionnaire's answers
- Critical requirement: the complete document must only be generated/served **after** Stripe confirms payment. Right now all the document logic runs client-side, which means a determined visitor could technically view the full document text before paying — this needs to be fixed with a real backend, not just front-end tricks (disabling copy/right-click, etc., which is not real protection)
- Document should be deliverable via download link and/or email after purchase (whichever you recommend as more reliable)

3. Contact Form Backend
- The existing contact form (name, email, message) needs to actually deliver submissions — to my email inbox at minimum, or to a simple CRM/inbox tool if you think that's a better long-term fit
- Please recommend the simplest reliable option (e.g., a transactional email service) rather than the most complex

**Note:** Items #2 and #3 both likely depend on the same piece of infrastructure — a transactional email service (e.g., SendGrid, Postmark, or similar) for delivering PDFs and forwarding form submissions. Please account for that shared setup in your Phase 1 estimate rather than treating them as fully separate systems.

---

PHASE 2 (Scope Later, Described Here for Context)

- User accounts (signup/login)
- Saved drafts — a visitor should be able to start a questionnaire, leave, and come back later to finish where they left off. This is already promised on the site's FAQ page, so it's a real commitment, not a stretch goal.
- Subscription payments — in addition to the one-time purchases from Phase 1, a recurring/subscription payment option (exact structure still being defined on my end)

I don't need a detailed Phase 2 proposal yet, but I'd like your high-level read on how Phase 1 architecture choices might affect Phase 2, so we don't build something in Phase 1 that has to be torn out later.

---

## Deliverables (Phase 1)
- Live, working checkout on all contract products
- PDF documents generated and delivered only after confirmed payment
- Working contact form that reliably delivers submissions
- Brief written documentation of what you built, including any accounts/services created (Stripe, email service, hosting) and how to access them
- A short written note on Phase 2 considerations, per above

## In Your Proposal, Please Include
- Relevant experience with Stripe integration and PDF generation for a small business — examples/links welcome
- Your recommended approach for the "paywall gating" requirement in #2 above
- Your recommended transactional email service and why
- Whether you're available and interested in continuing to Phase 2 after this phase wraps
- Estimated timeline and cost for Phase 1 specifically (flat rate preferred over hourly, if possible)
- Any questions about scope before we start

A Note on Fit
I'm not a developer, so I'm relying on you to flag anything in this brief that doesn't make sense technically, and to explain trade-offs in plain language as we go. Clear communication matters as much as technical skill for this project — especially since this is a multi-phase relationship, not a one-off task.

A Note On Time
This project is time sensitive.  I would like to have it completed as quickly as possible.

title: REQUEST - Senior Full-Stack Developer (NON GREENFIELD)
description:
Revision Note — v1.4 (identity & tracking — a first-class citizen). Made explicit that a service_request is a first-class
object in the shared operational object model (Library/Board v1.5 §2), carrying the platform-standard identity ( uuid
VARCHAR(36) + human-readable reference_id , exactly as organizations/hotels do per migration 010), tenant scope, lifecycle,
immutable provenance, and relationship links — defined once, reused, never a parallel identity or tracking scheme. Added §11A
Tracked with everything else — toward outcomes: requests correlate to the guest stay, room/asset, property, and time so
reactive-work performance reports alongside all operational data and rolls up toward guest-experience outcomes (OHI). Object
model, audit, and milestones updated.
Revision Note — v1.3 (notifications & delivery, reconciled to Communications Layer v4). Added §7B Notifications & delivery
— an event-based model where Requests emits its lifecycle events and subscribes to Comms intent events, never reaching into the
Comms layer (Comms v4 §23 anti-rewrite spine). Channels: live voice announce, push via the Thin Native Container (Comms
§20), in-app, email, SMS fallback — with delivery owned by Comms/the container, not Requests. Reuses Comms addressing
resolvers (presence / department / position / area / board) instead of inventing routing. Adds a configurable settings matrix (event ×
channel × role, org/property defaults, shift-aware quiet hours, escalation ladder, safety override). §9 corrected: Comms transcribes +
classifies + emits the intent event; Requests is the consumer (the one Comms v4 says is "built later in Agenda/PDEE"), with
acknowledge ↔ request correlation so a spoken "taking it" can't drift from an open request. Dependencies, milestones, audit
updated.
Revision Note — v1.2 (communication intelligence + share + view receipts). Per direction, the request's communication is
treated as a first-class data source — not just a thread to read later. Added: share (give someone visibility without making them an
owner — a viewer grant via the existing chat participant role); view receipts (delivered → viewed → acknowledged, reusing
messages_seen + last_read_at , with unviewed-by-assignee surfaced for accountability); voice notes transcribed into the
searchable thread; and Intelligence over the thread (§8) — theme/asset extraction ("TV remote again"), sentiment/guest-impact
flags, thread summaries for handoff, and resolution-knowledge capture that mines how a request was fixed and drafts it into the
Library. All advisory, tenant-scoped, and functional with Intelligence disabled.
Revision Note — v1.1 (collaboration added). A gap was caught: v1.0 covered evidence-on-close but not the live, day-to-day team
interaction on a request — comments, responses, adding people, and attaching photos/files mid-flight — which the legacy system
had. §7A is added to specify request collaboration, built entirely on existing infrastructure: the tie-message thread pattern
( message_model ), the chat participant model ( Chat_model — add/remove people, search), and the governed media spine
( Media_attachment / Media_file / Media_link ). No second chat system is built. Object model, dependencies, milestones,
and audit updated to match.
Revision Note — v1.0 (code-audit reconciliation). The develop branch was audited against this scope. Most dependencies
check out and are richer than assumed; several findings changed this document so the developer builds onto existing infrastructure
instead of reinventing it.
Confirmed present (reuse, don't rebuild): the Foundations spine — organization , hotels , hotel_branches (hotel
locations), and user_hotel_location_assignments + user_active_hotel_location for portfolio scoping; the
inventory_usage / inventory_adjustment / inventory_restock ledger (a mature subsystem); the
NotificationService library (the single notification entry point — the legacy ticket even disabled its own writes in favor of it); the
ai_governance_* layer plus ai_structured_output_model (ideal for voice → structured draft); per-user language
preferences + the translation layer; immutable audit_logs triggers.
Findings that changed the scope: (1) scoping resolves through hotel_location_id (org → hotel → location), not hotel_id
alone — corrected

title: WooCommerce Website Project Scope
description:
Beyond the build itself, here are the specific things I'd like included as part of this project:

1. Product schema markup + SEO-friendly URLs/meta data (per product, using my keywords) — foundation for Google discoverability
2. Fast site speed (image compression, CDN, minimal plugins) — impacts both SEO ranking and conversion
3. Frictionless mobile checkout (guest checkout, 1-click pay like Shop Pay/PayPal Express, minimal form fields) — 60-70% of traffic is mobile
4. High-impact product pages (benefit-driven copy, multiple photos, video, clear specs) — converts visitors once SEO gets them there
5. Trust signals sitewide (badges near Add to Cart, visible return policy, contact/chat widget) — new stores fail most often on trust
6. Social proof / reviews (UGC) via Judge.me/Loox/Yotpo — reinforces trust, doubles as fresh SEO content
7. Full analytics tracking pre-launch (GA4 + e-commerce tracking, Meta Pixel/CAPI, GTM) — needed to measure and optimize post-launch
8. Abandoned cart recovery (email/SMS sequence) — recovers otherwise-lost sales passively
9. Email/SMS capture with welcome offer — captures first-time visitors who aren't ready to buy yet
10. AOV boosters (free shipping threshold, in-cart upsells) — increases revenue per visitor

A few things that matter a lot to me for this project:

- Full ownership: I need complete ownership of the website, theme, plugins, and all files/credentials once the project is done. No lock-in.
- Full transparency: I'd like clear communication throughout — what's being installed, why, and access to everything (hosting, admin, plugin licenses, etc.) as we go, not just at the end.
- Trust: This is important to me, so I'm looking for someone reliable who works cleanly and explains me with transparency on what they do.

Could you share:
1. Examples of WooCommerce sites you've built (ideally similar product-line/e-commerce launches)
2. Your general process and timeline for a build of this scope
3. Your experience with the items listed above (SEO, checkout optimization, cart recovery, analytics, etc.)
4. How you handle ownership/transfer of credentials, licenses, and code
5. A cost estimate broken down by design, development, and setup

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Best,
Neel

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

title: WooCommerce Website Project Scope
description:
Beyond the build itself, here are the specific things I'd like included as part of this project:

1. Product schema markup + SEO-friendly URLs/meta data (per product, using my keywords) — foundation for Google discoverability
2. Fast site speed (image compression, CDN, minimal plugins) — impacts both SEO ranking and conversion
3. Frictionless mobile checkout (guest checkout, 1-click pay like Shop Pay/PayPal Express, minimal form fields) — 60-70% of traffic is mobile
4. High-impact product pages (benefit-driven copy, multiple photos, video, clear specs) — converts visitors once SEO gets them there
5. Trust signals sitewide (badges near Add to Cart, visible return policy, contact/chat widget) — new stores fail most often on trust
6. Social proof / reviews (UGC) via Judge.me/Loox/Yotpo — reinforces trust, doubles as fresh SEO content
7. Full analytics tracking pre-launch (GA4 + e-commerce tracking, Meta Pixel/CAPI, GTM) — needed to measure and optimize post-launch
8. Abandoned cart recovery (email/SMS sequence) — recovers otherwise-lost sales passively
9. Email/SMS capture with welcome offer — captures first-time visitors who aren't ready to buy yet
10. AOV boosters (free shipping threshold, in-cart upsells) — increases revenue per visitor

A few things that matter a lot to me for this project:

- Full ownership: I need complete ownership of the website, theme, plugins, and all files/credentials once the project is done. No lock-in.
- Full transparency: I'd like clear communication throughout — what's being installed, why, and access to everything (hosting, admin, plugin licenses, etc.) as we go, not just at the end.
- Trust: This is important to me, so I'm looking for someone reliable who works cleanly and explains me with transparency on what they do.

Could you share:
1. Examples of WooCommerce sites you've built (ideally similar product-line/e-commerce launches)
2. Your general process and timeline for a build of this scope
3. Your experience with the items listed above (SEO, checkout optimization, cart recovery, analytics, etc.)
4. How you handle ownership/transfer of credentials, licenses, and code
5. A cost estimate broken down by design, development, and setup

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Best,
Neel

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

object in the shared operational object model (Library/Board v1.5 §2), carrying the platform-standard identity ( uuid
VARCHAR(36) + human-readable reference_id , exactly as organizations/hotels do per migration 010), tenant scope, lifecycle,
immutable provenance, and relationship links — defined once, reused, never a parallel identity or tracking scheme. Added §11A

reactive-work performance reports alongside all operational data and rolls up toward guest-experience outcomes (OHI). Object
model, audit, and milestones updated.
Revision Note — v1.3 (notifications & delivery, reconciled to Communications Layer v4). Added §7B Notifications & delivery
— an event-based model where Requests emits its lifecycle events and subscribes to Comms intent events, never reaching into the
Comms layer (Comms v4 §23 anti-rewrite spine). Channels: live voice announce, push via the Thin Native Container (Comms
§20), in-app, email, SMS fallback — with delivery owned by Comms/the container, not Requests. Reuses Comms addressing
resolvers (presence / department / position / area / board) instead of inventing routing. Adds a configurable settings matrix (event ×
channel × role, org/property defaults, shift-aware quiet hours, escalation ladder, safety override). §9 corrected: Comms transcribes +
classifies + emits the intent event; Requests is the consumer (the one Comms v4 says is "built later in Agenda/PDEE"), with
acknowledge ↔ request correlation so a spoken "taking it" can't drift from an open request. Dependencies, milestones, audit
updated.
Revision Note — v1.2 (communication intelligence + share + view receipts). Per direction, the request's communication is
treated as a first-class data source — not just a thread to read later. Added: share (give someone visibility without making them an
owner — a viewer grant via the existing chat participant role); view receipts (delivered → viewed → acknowledged, reusing
messages_seen + last_read_at , with unviewed-by-assignee surfaced for accountability); voice notes transcribed into the
searchable thread; and Intelligence over the thread (§8) — theme/asset extraction ("TV remote again"), sentiment/guest-impact
flags, thread summaries for handoff, and resolution-knowledge capture that mines how a request was fixed and drafts it into the
Library. All advisory, tenant-scoped, and functional with Intelligence disabled.
Revision Note — v1.1 (collaboration added). A gap was caught: v1.0 covered evidence-on-close but not the live, day-to-day team
interaction on a request — comments, responses, adding people, and attaching photos/files mid-flight — which the legacy system
had. §7A is added to specify request collaboration, built entirely on existing infrastructure: the tie-message thread pattern
( message_model ), the chat participant model ( Chat_model — add/remove people, search), and the governed media spine
( Media_attachment / Media_file / Media_link ). No second chat system is built. Object model, dependencies, milestones,
and audit updated to match.
Revision Note — v1.0 (code-audit reconciliation). The develop branch was audited against this scope. Most dependencies
check out and are richer than assumed; several findings changed this document so the developer builds onto existing infrastructure
instead of reinventing it.
Confirmed present (reuse, don't rebuild): the Foundations spine — organization , hotels , hotel_branches (hotel
locations), and user_hotel_location_assignments + user_active_hotel_location for portfolio scoping; the
inventory_usage / inventory_adjustment / inventory_restock ledger (a mature subsystem); the
NotificationService library (the single notification entry point — the legacy ticket even disabled its own writes in favor of it); the
ai_governance_* layer plus ai_structured_output_model (ideal for voice → structured draft); per-user language
preferences + the translation layer; immutable audit_logs triggers.
Findings that changed the scope: (1) scoping resolves through hotel_location_id (org → hotel → location), not hotel_id
alone — corrected

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

title: REQUEST - Senior Full-Stack Developer (NON GREENFIELD)
description:
Revision Note — v1.4 (identity & tracking — a first-class citizen). Made explicit that a service_request is a first-class
object in the shared operational object model (Library/Board v1.5 §2), carrying the platform-standard identity ( uuid
VARCHAR(36) + human-readable reference_id , exactly as organizations/hotels do per migration 010), tenant scope, lifecycle,
immutable provenance, and relationship links — defined once, reused, never a parallel identity or tracking scheme. Added §11A
Tracked with everything else — toward outcomes: requests correlate to the guest stay, room/asset, property, and time so
reactive-work performance reports alongside all operational data and rolls up toward guest-experience outcomes (OHI). Object
model, audit, and milestones updated.
Revision Note — v1.3 (notifications & delivery, reconciled to Communications Layer v4). Added §7B Notifications & delivery
— an event-based model where Requests emits its lifecycle events and subscribes to Comms intent events, never reaching into the
Comms layer (Comms v4 §23 anti-rewrite spine). Channels: live voice announce, push via the Thin Native Container (Comms
§20), in-app, email, SMS fallback — with delivery owned by Comms/the container, not Requests. Reuses Comms addressing
resolvers (presence / department / position / area / board) instead of inventing routing. Adds a configurable settings matrix (event ×
channel × role, org/property defaults, shift-aware quiet hours, escalation ladder, safety override). §9 corrected: Comms transcribes +
classifies + emits the intent event; Requests is the consumer (the one Comms v4 says is "built later in Agenda/PDEE"), with
acknowledge ↔ request correlation so a spoken "taking it" can't drift from an open request. Dependencies, milestones, audit
updated.
Revision Note — v1.2 (communication intelligence + share + view receipts). Per direction, the request's communication is
treated as a first-class data source — not just a thread to read later. Added: share (give someone visibility without making them an
owner — a viewer grant via the existing chat participant role); view receipts (delivered → viewed → acknowledged, reusing
messages_seen + last_read_at , with unviewed-by-assignee surfaced for accountability); voice notes transcribed into the
searchable thread; and Intelligence over the thread (§8) — theme/asset extraction ("TV remote again"), sentiment/guest-impact
flags, thread summaries for handoff, and resolution-knowledge capture that mines how a request was fixed and drafts it into the
Library. All advisory, tenant-scoped, and functional with Intelligence disabled.
Revision Note — v1.1 (collaboration added). A gap was caught: v1.0 covered evidence-on-close but not the live, day-to-day team
interaction on a request — comments, responses, adding people, and attaching photos/files mid-flight — which the legacy system
had. §7A is added to specify request collaboration, built entirely on existing infrastructure: the tie-message thread pattern
( message_model ), the chat participant model ( Chat_model — add/remove people, search), and the governed media spine
( Media_attachment / Media_file / Media_link ). No second chat system is built. Object model, dependencies, milestones,
and audit updated to match.
Revision Note — v1.0 (code-audit reconciliation). The develop branch was audited against this scope. Most dependencies
check out and are richer than assumed; several findings changed this document so the developer builds onto existing infrastructure
instead of reinventing it.
Confirmed present (reuse, don't rebuild): the Foundations spine — organization , hotels , hotel_branches (hotel
locations), and user_hotel_location_assignments + user_active_hotel_location for portfolio scoping; the
inventory_usage / inventory_adjustment / inventory_restock ledger (a mature subsystem); the
NotificationService library (the single notification entry point — the legacy ticket even disabled its own writes in favor of it); the
ai_governance_* layer plus ai_structured_output_model (ideal for voice → structured draft); per-user language
preferences + the translation layer; immutable audit_logs triggers.
Findings that changed the scope: (1) scoping resolves through hotel_location_id (org → hotel → location), not hotel_id

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

title: Multilingual Communication Preferences & Translation Layer - Senior PHP / CodeIgniter Developer
description:
HOTELHUB / OPERATIONSHUB
Language Preferences & Translation Orchestration Layer v1.0
(Multilingual Communication Preference Infrastructure)



Built Against:
• Push-to-Talk Unified Master Scope v2.3
• Operational Accessibility Addendum v1.0
• Real-Time Translation Layer Scope v1.0
• Existing Translation Provider Abstraction Infrastructure



Purpose



This scope introduces centralized multilingual communication preference management for operational communication systems.



This layer exists to:
• personalize multilingual communication behavior
• reduce communication friction
• improve translation usability
• support multilingual frontline operations
• standardize translation behavior across communication systems



This scope is configuration and orchestration focused.
This scope does NOT introduce:
• conversational AI
• autonomous AI systems
• employee monitoring
• sentiment analysis
• workflow automation



PART I — USER LANGUAGE PREFERENCES



1.1 User Preferred Language



System must support:
• primary/preferred language selection per user



Examples:
• English
• Spanish
• Haitian Creole
• Portuguese
• French
• Arabic
• Chinese (Simplified)



Language availability must remain configurable by hotel/system settings.



1.2 Secondary Language (Optional)



System may support:
• secondary/preferred fallback language



Example:
• primary = Spanish
• secondary = English



1.3 Translation Preference Settings



Users may configure:
• auto-translate incoming communication
• show original language first
• show translated language first
• narration playback preferred language
• live captions enabled/disabled
• translated narration enabled/disabled



PART II — HOTEL LANGUAGE CONFIGURATION



2.1 Allowed Language Packs



Hotels may define:
• supported operational languages
• enabled translation languages
• narration-capable languages



2.2 Hotel Default Language



System must support:
• hotel-level default operational language



2.3 Future Expansion Reservation



Architecture must remain compatible with:
• regional language packs
• department-specific language preferences
• portfolio-wide language governance



PART III — COMMUNICATION ORCHESTRATION



3.1 Incoming Communication Behavior



System must support:
• automatic translation of incoming operational communication
• optional manual translation trigger
• translation preference persistence



3.2 Outgoing Communication Behavior



System may support:
• preferred outgoing translation handling
• automatic recipient-language translation routing



3.3 Translation Visibility



Users must always be able to:
• view original communication
• view translated communication
• identify source language
• identify translated language



Original operational communication remains source-of-truth.



PART IV — LIVE TRANSLATION SETTINGS



4.1 Real-Time Translation Preferences



Users may configure:
• live captions enabled/disabled
• translated captions enabled/disabled
• preferred live caption language



4.2 Narration Preferences



Users may configure:
• translated narration playback enabled/disabled
• narration playback language preference



Narration must remain:
• user-triggered
• non-intrusive
• operationally lightweight



PART V — ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENTS



5.1 Provider Abstraction Compliance



System MUST:
• remain provider-agnostic
• avoid provider-specific UI coupling
• avoid hardcoded provider assumptions



5.2 Shared Infrastructure Consumption



This layer MUST consume:
• existing translation infrastructure
• existing narration infrastructure
• existing provider abstraction architecture



No parallel translation infrastructure permitted.



5.3 Mobile Compatibility



All preference management MUST remain compatible with:
• handheld execution
• tablet execution
• Thin Native Container architecture



PART VI — SECURITY & ISOLATION



6.1 Tenant Isolation



All language preferences MUST remain:
• hotel-isolated
• permission-aware
• role-safe



6.2 Privacy Doctrine



Language preferences exist solely to:
• improve communication usability
• improve translation quality
• improve operational accessibility



This data MUST NOT be used for:
• employee scoring
• profiling
• behavioral analysis



PART VII — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA



Acceptance requires:
• user language preference persistence functional
• translation preference persistence functional
• multilingual communication rendering functional
• original-language visibility functional
• translation toggles functional
• narration preference handling functional
• mobile/tablet validation complete
• no cross-tenant leakage
• provider abstraction compliance verified



STRATEGIC INTENT



This layer exists to standardize multilingual operational communication behavior across HotelHub communication systems.



This functionality is intended to improve operational communication clarity and accessibility — not replace human operational judgment or introduce conversational AI dependency.

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring

A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?

Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

• preferred live caption language

• operationally lightweight

• avoid hardcoded provider assumptions

• existing translation infrastructure
• existing narration infrastructure
• existing provider abstraction architecture



No parallel translation infrastructure permitted.

All preference management MUST remain compatible with:
• handheld execution
• tablet execution
• Thin Native Container architecture



PART VI — SECURITY & ISOLATION

All language preferences MUST remain:
• hotel-isolated
• permission-aware
• role-safe



6.2 Privacy Doctrine



Language preferences exist solely to:
• improve communication usability
• improve translation quality
• improve operational accessibility



This data MUST NOT be used for:
• employee scoring
• profiling
• behavioral analysis



PART VII — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA



Acceptance requires:
• user language preference persistence functional
• translation preference persistence functional
• multilingual communication rendering functional
• original-language visibility functional
• translation toggles functional
• narration preference handling functional
• mobile/tablet validation complete
• no cross-tenant leakage
• provider abstraction compliance verified



STRATEGIC INTENT



This layer exists to standardize multilingual operational communication behavior across HotelHub communication systems.



This functionality is intended to improve operational communication clarity and accessibility — not replace human operational judgment or introduce conversational AI dependency.

title: Custom WordPress Developer for Editorial & Media Website
description:
Custom WordPress Developer for Editorial & Media Website

We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer to help us build and launch a professional, fast, and scalable website for our business.

The goal is to create a strong first version efficiently, without unnecessary complexity or over-engineering. We want someone who can understand the business objective, recommend practical technical solutions, and focus on what is actually needed for the initial launch.

What we need
WordPress development and customization.
Clean, responsive, mobile-friendly implementation.
Customization of the theme and/or existing components when appropriate.
PHP, CSS, and JavaScript as needed.
Good website structure, performance, and usability.
Basic SEO and technical best practices.
Integration of necessary WordPress plugins without relying on excessive plugins.
Testing, optimization, and bug fixing before launch.
A website that is easy to maintain and can be expanded later if the business requires it.
Content Management — Important

A key requirement of this project is that our team must be able to manage the website independently after launch, without requiring a developer for normal editorial tasks.

We need to be able to:

Create, edit, publish, and delete articles/content.
Upload and manage images and other media.
Manage categories and tags.
Add and update featured content.
Manage the relevant content fields and information from WordPress.
Make normal editorial updates without touching code.

The website should therefore be structured as a proper editorial/content management system, rather than as a collection of manually designed pages.

Normal content publishing and management should not require recurring developer intervention.

Design and Visual Direction

We already have a defined visual direction and basic brand guidelines, including the overall visual style and color palette.

We are therefore not looking to develop the brand identity from scratch.

The developer should be able to translate the existing visual direction into a clean, professional, and consistent WordPress implementation, while also providing practical recommendations when something can be improved from a usability or technical perspective.

Initial Website Scope

The initial version is expected to include approximately 5–7 core pages, based on the final website structure and business requirements.

The exact number and structure of pages will be defined during the initial planning.

We are intentionally keeping the first version focused on the essential content and functionality required to launch the business, rather than adding unnecessary pages or features.

The goal is to launch a professional and functional first version efficiently, with the possibility of adding improvements later based on actual business needs and results.

How We Want to Work
Start with a clearly defined first version/MVP.
Prioritize the highest-impact elements first.
Avoid unnecessary custom development when a reliable existing solution is sufficient.
Work in clear milestones with visible progress.
Communicate clearly about what is necessary, what is optional, and what can wait until a later stage.
We value efficiency, good judgment, and quality of execution more than simply spending more hours.
We want a developer who can identify simpler and more efficient solutions when appropriate.
We prefer a developer who can work independently and solve problems rather than requiring step-by-step instructions for every task.

Important: This is not intended to be an open-ended or indefinite project. We want to launch a strong first version within a reasonable timeframe, then evaluate future improvements based on actual business needs and results.

Ideal Developer

We are looking for an intermediate-level WordPress developer who:

Has strong practical WordPress development experience.
Understands WordPress beyond basic page builders.
Can work with PHP, CSS, and JavaScript when necessary.
Has experience structuring websites for ongoing content management.
Communicates clearly in English.
Can work independently and meet agreed milestones.
Understands the balance between quality, functionality, speed, and budget.
Please Include

When applying, please provide:

2–4 relevant WordPress projects you have developed.
A brief explanation of your role in those projects.
Whether you have experience with editorial, media, magazine, publishing, or content-heavy websites.
Your estimated timeline for this project.
Your proposed fixed price.
Any important technical recommendations you would make based on this description.

We are particularly interested in developers who can demonstrate actual development and customization work, rather than projects built primarily by installing and configuring a page builder.

A visual reference document is attached to help you understand the project's visual direction. Detailed technical specifications and website architecture will be shared with shortlisted candidates.

title: Custom WordPress Developer for Editorial & Media Website
description:

We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer to help us build and launch a professional, fast, and scalable website for our business.
