What we need
WordPress development and customization.
Clean, responsive, mobile-friendly implementation.
Customization of the theme and/or existing components when appropriate.
PHP, CSS, and JavaScript as needed.
Good website structure, performance, and usability.
Basic SEO and technical best practices.
Integration of necessary WordPress plugins without relying on excessive plugins.
Testing, optimization, and bug fixing before launch.
A website that is easy to maintain and can be expanded later if the business requires it.
Content Management — Important

A key requirement of this project is that our team must be able to manage the website independently after launch, without requiring a developer for normal editorial tasks.

We need to be able to:

Create, edit, publish, and delete articles/content.
Upload and manage images and other media.
Manage categories and tags.
Add and update featured content.
Manage the relevant content fields and information from WordPress.
Make normal editorial updates without touching code.

The website should therefore be structured as a proper editorial/content management system, rather than as a collection of manually designed pages.

Normal content publishing and management should not require recurring developer intervention.

Design and Visual Direction

We already have a defined visual direction and basic brand guidelines, including the overall visual style and color palette.

We are therefore not looking to develop the brand identity from scratch.

The developer should be able to translate the existing visual direction into a clean, professional, and consistent WordPress implementation, while also providing practical recommendations when something can be improved from a usability or technical perspective.

Initial Website Scope

The initial version is expected to include approximately 5–7 core pages, based on the final website structure and business requirements.

The exact number and structure of pages will be defined during the initial planning.

We are intentionally keeping the first version focused on the essential content and functionality required to launch the business, rather than adding unnecessary pages or features.

The goal is to launch a professional and functional first version efficiently, with the possibility of adding improvements later based on actual business needs and results.

How We Want to Work
Start with a clearly defined first version/MVP.
Prioritize the highest-impact elements first.
Avoid unnecessary custom development when a reliable existing solution is sufficient.
Work in clear milestones with visible progress.

We value efficiency, good judgment, and quality of execution more than simply spending more hours.

We prefer a developer who can work independently and solve problems rather than requiring step-by-step instructions for every task.

Ideal Developer

Has strong practical WordPress development experience.
Understands WordPress beyond basic page builders.
Can work with PHP, CSS, and JavaScript when necessary.

title: Site Migration Word Press Multi-Site to Astro Static
description:
WordPress → Astro Migration: 208-Post Legal Blog, Zero URL Loss

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

Type: Fixed price, milestone-based Duration: 3–5 weeks Skills: Astro, static site generation, WordPress migration, Cloudflare Workers/Pages, DNS, technical SEO

Overview

I publish a legal blog that has run continuously since 2010. It currently sits on a vendor-managed WordPress platform. I am moving it to a self-hosted static site built with Astro and deployed on Cloudflare Workers, at the same domain, with the same URLs.

This is a migration, not a redesign. The visual design and the content architecture are already decided and already implemented on a sister site I own. Your job is to reproduce that architecture on a new repository, load the content, generate every route, guarantee that no URL is lost, and execute the cutover.

The site's authority is the asset. A broken URL is the only failure mode that matters.

What already exists

Substantial preparatory work is done. Please price accordingly.

A working reference implementation. A sister site on the same stack — Astro 5.x, Cloudflare Workers, flat /[slug]/ routes, a content collection with a Zod-validated schema, an "authorities" collection, and a Pages CMS configuration. You will copy this forward and change site identity. You are not designing anything.
208 posts already converted to Astro-ready markdown with frontmatter (title, description, pubDate, categories, tags, legacy URL, read time, word count). Legacy slugs are preserved verbatim.
The original WordPress XML export, if you prefer to rerun conversion yourself.
The Python converter script that produced the markdown, so mappings can be changed and all 208 files regenerated.
An inventory CSV of all 208 posts with their taxonomy.
A written work plan dividing the job into phases with defined acceptance gates. You will be given it after hiring. It is the plan you will execute.
A manifest of 42 media files to preserve (court opinions and statutes hosted as PDFs, original diagrams, headshot). Roughly 280 stock images have already been stripped.
Scope of work

1. Repository and deployment skeleton. Create a new private GitHub repository seeded from the reference codebase. Change site identity, canonical host, and pillar definitions. Add two fields to the post schema. Connect to a new Cloudflare Worker. Confirm it builds and serves.

2. Content load. Load the 208 posts into the content collection. Build. Spot-check across the full date range. Eighteen posts contain tables or embeds and are flagged for manual review; confirm they render correctly.

3. Routes and archives. Generate pillar landing pages, tag archives, paginated index at /page/N/, a topics index, an RSS feed, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt. Add Pagefind for site search.

4. Redirect map. The legacy site has 37 category archives and 316 tag archives. The tag set is being reduced to roughly 24. Every retired archive URL must 301 to a surviving archive or to its pillar. Write public/_redirects.

5. Media. Download 42 files from the live site — this must happen before DNS moves, and it is irreversible if missed. Place them in public/ at their exact legacy paths so existing links resolve without edits.

6. Pages. 43 published pages require triage: convert, consolidate, or redirect. Several are empty or byte-identical duplicates. I will decide the disposition of each; you implement.

7. Parity verification. Crawl the live site's sitemap. Diff every live URL against what the staging site serves or redirects. Produce a report showing zero unaccounted-for URLs. The export is known to be an unreliable inventory — at least one page is served from a different path than the export records. Assume there are others. This is the go/no-go gate.

8. Cutover. Attach the domain and www to the Worker. Move nameservers to Cloudflare. Verify. Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console. Monitor 404s for 14 days.

Explicitly out of scope

Do not quote for these:

Content writing, editing, or rewriting of any kind
Design work — the design is fixed and already built
Taxonomy decisions. I assign posts to pillars and approve the tag consolidation. You receive approved mapping files and implement them.
Legal or professional-conduct content. Two required notices must appear sitewide; I supply the text.
SEO consulting, content strategy, link building
Technical requirements
Astro 5.x, TypeScript, content collections with Zod schema validation
Cloudflare Workers deployment with static assets; Git-triggered builds
Cloudflare DNS configuration and custom domain attachment
Comfortable working from an existing codebase and matching its conventions
Able to read a Python script and modify a mapping table
Access and security
GitHub access will be repository-scoped collaborator access to one private repository. No organization-level access.
Cloudflare access will be via scoped API token or an account containing only this project. You will not receive access to any other domain I own.
The content is a public blog. There is no confidential material in scope.
All work is delivered by pull request. I merge.
Deliverables and acceptance

Payment is milestone-based. Each milestone is accepted against an objective test.

Milestone	Acceptance test
1. Skeleton	Empty site builds and serves at a workers.dev address
2. Content	All 208 posts render; 18 flagged posts verified
3. Routes and redirects	Every legacy archive URL renders or 301s
4. Assets and pages	All 42 files present and reachable; pages dispositioned
5. Parity report	Zero unaccounted-for live URLs
6. Cutover	Domain live on new host; sitemap submitted; 14 days monitoring
To be considered, your proposal must include
A live example of a WordPress-to-static migration you have completed. Give me the URL. Tell me how many URLs it involved and how you verified none were lost.
Your method for URL parity verification. Specifically: how do you prove, before cutover, that no live URL will 404 after it? Name the tools.
Your approach to the 316 tag archives. How do you decide what redirects where, given an approved mapping file?
Your rollback plan. If the site is broken an hour after DNS moves, what happens?
Your fixed-price quote, broken out by the six milestones above, and your available start date.

Proposals that do not answer all five will not be reviewed. Please open your response with the word PARITY so I know you read this posting.

title: Multilingual Communication Preferences & Translation Layer - Senior PHP / CodeIgniter Developer
description:
HOTELHUB / OPERATIONSHUB
Language Preferences & Translation Orchestration Layer v1.0
(Multilingual Communication Preference Infrastructure)



Built Against:
• Push-to-Talk Unified Master Scope v2.3
• Operational Accessibility Addendum v1.0
• Real-Time Translation Layer Scope v1.0
• Existing Translation Provider Abstraction Infrastructure



Purpose



This scope introduces centralized multilingual communication preference management for operational communication systems.



This layer exists to:
• personalize multilingual communication behavior
• reduce communication friction
• improve translation usability
• support multilingual frontline operations
• standardize translation behavior across communication systems



This scope is configuration and orchestration focused.
This scope does NOT introduce:
• conversational AI
• autonomous AI systems
• employee monitoring
• sentiment analysis
• workflow automation



PART I — USER LANGUAGE PREFERENCES



1.1 User Preferred Language



System must support:
• primary/preferred language selection per user



Examples:
• English
• Spanish
• Haitian Creole
• Portuguese
• French
• Arabic
• Chinese (Simplified)



Language availability must remain configurable by hotel/system settings.



1.2 Secondary Language (Optional)



System may support:
• secondary/preferred fallback language



Example:
• primary = Spanish
• secondary = English



1.3 Translation Preference Settings



Users may configure:
• auto-translate incoming communication
• show original language first
• show translated language first
• narration playback preferred language
• live captions enabled/disabled
• translated narration enabled/disabled



PART II — HOTEL LANGUAGE CONFIGURATION



2.1 Allowed Language Packs



Hotels may define:
• supported operational languages
• enabled translation languages
• narration-capable languages



2.2 Hotel Default Language



System must support:
• hotel-level default operational language



2.3 Future Expansion Reservation



Architecture must remain compatible with:
• regional language packs
• department-specific language preferences
• portfolio-wide language governance



PART III — COMMUNICATION ORCHESTRATION



3.1 Incoming Communication Behavior



System must support:
• automatic translation of incoming operational communication
• optional manual translation trigger
• translation preference persistence



3.2 Outgoing Communication Behavior



System may support:
• preferred outgoing translation handling
• automatic recipient-language translation routing



3.3 Translation Visibility



Users must always be able to:
• view original communication
• view translated communication
• identify source language
• identify translated language



Original operational communication remains source-of-truth.



PART IV — LIVE TRANSLATION SETTINGS



4.1 Real-Time Translation Preferences



Users may configure:
• live captions enabled/disabled
• translated captions enabled/disabled
• preferred live caption language



4.2 Narration Preferences



Users may configure:
• translated narration playback enabled/disabled
• narration playback language preference



Narration must remain:
• user-triggered
• non-intrusive
• operationally lightweight



PART V — ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENTS



5.1 Provider Abstraction Compliance



System MUST:
• remain provider-agnostic
• avoid provider-specific UI coupling
• avoid hardcoded provider assumptions



5.2 Shared Infrastructure Consumption



This layer MUST consume:
• existing translation infrastructure
• existing narration infrastructure
• existing provider abstraction architecture



No parallel translation infrastructure permitted.



5.3 Mobile Compatibility



All preference management MUST remain compatible with:
• handheld execution
• tablet execution
• Thin Native Container architecture



PART VI — SECURITY & ISOLATION



6.1 Tenant Isolation



All language preferences MUST remain:
• hotel-isolated
• permission-aware
• role-safe



6.2 Privacy Doctrine



Language preferences exist solely to:
• improve communication usability
• improve translation quality
• improve operational accessibility



This data MUST NOT be used for:
• employee scoring
• profiling
• behavioral analysis



PART VII — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA



Acceptance requires:
• user language preference persistence functional
• translation preference persistence functional
• multilingual communication rendering functional
• original-language visibility functional
• translation toggles functional
• narration preference handling functional
• mobile/tablet validation complete
• no cross-tenant leakage
• provider abstraction compliance verified



STRATEGIC INTENT



This layer exists to standardize multilingual operational communication behavior across HotelHub communication systems.



This functionality is intended to improve operational communication clarity and accessibility — not replace human operational judgment or introduce conversational AI dependency.

title: Custom WordPress Developer for Editorial & Media Website
description:
Custom WordPress Developer for Editorial & Media Website

We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer to help us build and launch a professional, fast, and scalable website for our business.

The goal is to create a strong first version efficiently, without unnecessary complexity or over-engineering. We want someone who can understand the business objective, recommend practical technical solutions, and focus on what is actually needed for the initial launch.

What we need
WordPress development and customization.
Clean, responsive, mobile-friendly implementation.
Customization of the theme and/or existing components when appropriate.
PHP, CSS, and JavaScript as needed.
Good website structure, performance, and usability.
Basic SEO and technical best practices.
Integration of necessary WordPress plugins without relying on excessive plugins.
Testing, optimization, and bug fixing before launch.
A website that is easy to maintain and can be expanded later if the business requires it.
Content Management — Important

A key requirement of this project is that our team must be able to manage the website independently after launch, without requiring a developer for normal editorial tasks.

We need to be able to:

Create, edit, publish, and delete articles/content.
Upload and manage images and other media.
Manage categories and tags.
Add and update featured content.
Manage the relevant content fields and information from WordPress.
Make normal editorial updates without touching code.

The website should therefore be structured as a proper editorial/content management system, rather than as a collection of manually designed pages.

Normal content publishing and management should not require recurring developer intervention.

Design and Visual Direction

We already have a defined visual direction and basic brand guidelines, including the overall visual style and color palette.

We are therefore not looking to develop the brand identity from scratch.

The developer should be able to translate the existing visual direction into a clean, professional, and consistent WordPress implementation, while also providing practical recommendations when something can be improved from a usability or technical perspective.

Initial Website Scope

The initial version is expected to include approximately 5–7 core pages, based on the final website structure and business requirements.

The exact number and structure of pages will be defined during the initial planning.

We are intentionally keeping the first version focused on the essential content and functionality required to launch the business, rather than adding unnecessary pages or features.

The goal is to launch a professional and functional first version efficiently, with the possibility of adding improvements later based on actual business needs and results.

How We Want to Work
Start with a clearly defined first version/MVP.
Prioritize the highest-impact elements first.
Avoid unnecessary custom development when a reliable existing solution is sufficient.
Work in clear milestones with visible progress.
Communicate clearly about what is necessary, what is optional, and what can wait until a later stage.
We value efficiency, good judgment, and quality of execution more than simply spending more hours.
We want a developer who can identify simpler and more efficient solutions when appropriate.
We prefer a developer who can work independently and solve problems rather than requiring step-by-step instructions for every task.

Important: This is not intended to be an open-ended or indefinite project. We want to launch a strong first version within a reasonable timeframe, then evaluate future improvements based on actual business needs and results.

Ideal Developer

We are looking for an intermediate-level WordPress developer who:

Has strong practical WordPress development experience.
Understands WordPress beyond basic page builders.
Can work with PHP, CSS, and JavaScript when necessary.
Has experience structuring websites for ongoing content management.
Communicates clearly in English.
Can work independently and meet agreed milestones.
Understands the balance between quality, functionality, speed, and budget.
Please Include

When applying, please provide:

2–4 relevant WordPress projects you have developed.
A brief explanation of your role in those projects.
Whether you have experience with editorial, media, magazine, publishing, or content-heavy websites.
Your estimated timeline for this project.
Your proposed fixed price.
Any important technical recommendations you would make based on this description.

We are particularly interested in developers who can demonstrate actual development and customization work, rather than projects built primarily by installing and configuring a page builder.

A visual reference document is attached to help you understand the project's visual direction. Detailed technical specifications and website architecture will be shared with shortlisted candidates.

title: Web Developer Needed for Custom Travel Startup Website & Backend Integration
description:
I’m looking for a web developer to help build and refine the website for PlanItary, an early-stage travel technology startup focused on helping travelers better understand the places they visit while connecting them with local businesses, organizations, educators, guides, projects, and communities around the world.

The project involves developing a responsive, polished website from an established design direction and implementing the functionality behind it. This includes multiple pages and interactive forms, mobile and desktop responsiveness, navigation and UI components, form validation, backend form processing, email routing, spam protection, and deployment. The site also needs to support several different types of inquiries, including general questions, partnerships, businesses, educational contributors, community projects, transportation providers, travel providers, support requests, waitlist registrations, and community submissions.

The developer should be comfortable working with a modern web stack and integrating services such as Cloudflare/Vercel, transactional email, DNS/domain configuration, and custom form-processing logic where needed. Attention to detail is important because this website is intended to become the public foundation for a much larger platform currently in development.

I'm looking for someone who communicates well, can work independently, understands the goals behind the product rather than simply implementing individual pages, and is comfortable suggesting improvements when they see a better technical or user-experience solution.

title: Fix WordPress Plugin Conflict
description: My website breaks when both WP Rocket and Contact Form 7 are active - forms stop submitting properly. I need someone to troubleshoot and fix the compatibility issue between the caching plugin and the form plugin.

title: TutorLMS and Woocommerce Issues
description:
I have an existing live WordPress site using Tutor LMS Pro and WooCommerce. After recent updates we experienced automatic enrollment failures after successful payment, and we're now having problems with certificates using the WordPress username/display name instead of the student's actual first and last name. Tutor LMS support has been working on it for days without resolving everything.

I need someone experienced specifically with Tutor LMS + WooCommerce who can diagnose the underlying issue, including hooks, user metadata/database values and plugin conflicts—not simply change settings. Are you comfortable troubleshooting this on a staging copy and then implementing the fix on the live site?

title: Web Developer for SMS Website
description: I need a web developer to build a website where users can send text messages for a fee to a large group of users, who will reply by text. The system should then generate a report for the original message sender. The project includes setting up the website, handling SMS sending and receiving, and creating a reporting feature that tracks responses and provides a summary for each sender.

title: Multilingual Communication Preferences & Translation Layer - Senior PHP / CodeIgniter Developer
description:
HOTELHUB / OPERATIONSHUB
Language Preferences & Translation Orchestration Layer v1.0
(Multilingual Communication Preference Infrastructure)



Built Against:
• Push-to-Talk Unified Master Scope v2.3
• Operational Accessibility Addendum v1.0
• Real-Time Translation Layer Scope v1.0
• Existing Translation Provider Abstraction Infrastructure



Purpose



This scope introduces centralized multilingual communication preference management for operational communication systems.



This layer exists to:
• personalize multilingual communication behavior
• reduce communication friction
• improve translation usability
• support multilingual frontline operations
• standardize translation behavior across communication systems



This scope is configuration and orchestration focused.
This scope does NOT introduce:
• conversational AI
• autonomous AI systems
• employee monitoring
• sentiment analysis
• workflow automation



PART I — USER LANGUAGE PREFERENCES



1.1 User Preferred Language



System must support:
• primary/preferred language selection per user



Examples:
• English
• Spanish
• Haitian Creole
• Portuguese
• French
• Arabic
• Chinese (Simplified)



Language availability must remain configurable by hotel/system settings.



1.2 Secondary Language (Optional)



System may support:
• secondary/preferred fallback language



Example:
• primary = Spanish
• secondary = English



1.3 Translation Preference Settings



Users may configure:
• auto-translate incoming communication
• show original language first
• show translated language first
• narration playback preferred language
• live captions enabled/disabled
• translated narration enabled/disabled



PART II — HOTEL LANGUAGE CONFIGURATION



2.1 Allowed Language Packs



Hotels may define:
• supported operational languages
• enabled translation languages
• narration-capable languages



2.2 Hotel Default Language



System must support:
• hotel-level default operational language



2.3 Future Expansion Reservation



Architecture must remain compatible with:
• regional language packs
• department-specific language preferences
• portfolio-wide language governance



PART III — COMMUNICATION ORCHESTRATION



3.1 Incoming Communication Behavior



System must support:
• automatic translation of incoming operational communication
• optional manual translation trigger
• translation preference persistence



3.2 Outgoing Communication Behavior



System may support:
• preferred outgoing translation handling
• automatic recipient-language translation routing



3.3 Translation Visibility



Users must always be able to:
• view original communication
• view translated communication
• identify source language
• identify translated language



Original operational communication remains source-of-truth.



PART IV — LIVE TRANSLATION SETTINGS



4.1 Real-Time Translation Preferences



Users may configure:
• live captions enabled/disabled
• translated captions enabled/disabled
• preferred live caption language



4.2 Narration Preferences



Users may configure:
• translated narration playback enabled/disabled
• narration playback language preference



Narration must remain:
• user-triggered
• non-intrusive
• operationally lightweight



PART V — ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENTS



5.1 Provider Abstraction Compliance



System MUST:
• remain provider-agnostic
• avoid provider-specific UI coupling
• avoid hardcoded provider assumptions



5.2 Shared Infrastructure Consumption



This layer MUST consume:
• existing translation infrastructure
• existing narration infrastructure
• existing provider abstraction architecture



No parallel translation infrastructure permitted.



5.3 Mobile Compatibility



All preference management MUST remain compatible with:
• handheld execution
• tablet execution
• Thin Native Container architecture



PART VI — SECURITY & ISOLATION



6.1 Tenant Isolation



All language preferences MUST remain:
• hotel-isolated
• permission-aware
• role-safe



6.2 Privacy Doctrine



Language preferences exist solely to:
• improve communication usability
• improve translation quality
• improve operational accessibility



This data MUST NOT be used for:
• employee scoring
• profiling
• behavioral analysis



PART VII — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA



Acceptance requires:
• user language preference persistence functional
• translation preference persistence functional
• multilingual communication rendering functional
• original-language visibility functional
• translation toggles functional
• narration preference handling functional
• mobile/tablet validation complete
• no cross-tenant leakage
• provider abstraction compliance verified



STRATEGIC INTENT



This layer exists to standardize multilingual operational communication behavior across HotelHub communication systems.



This functionality is intended to improve operational communication clarity and accessibility — not replace human operational judgment or introduce conversational AI dependency.

title: WordPress + Stripe Developer — Finish & Launch a Subscription Directory (Italian market)
description:
PROJECT OVERVIEW
 
I run Dogsify, an Italian directory and discovery platform for dog-related businesses (breeders, vets, groomers, boarding, etc.), built on WordPress with a custom theme and custom functionality. The site is in the final pre-launch stage and I need an experienced developer to pick up an existing codebase on a staging environment and complete the critical items needed to go live cleanly.
 
This is a finish-and-launch engagement, not a build-from-scratch. Most of the work is done. A separate sysadmin handles server infrastructure and the staging-to-production push, so you focus on the application and code side. I will provide a detailed handover document and staging access to the developer I select.
 
WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT
 
- Custom search, navigation and discovery front-end
- A Stripe-native subscription system (Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal and Webhooks) with three tiers, webhook event handling, WordPress user-meta sync, downgrade-on-expiry logic, and a reminder-email cron with idempotency
- Italian B2B billing fields already present on the user profile (Ragione Sociale, Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale, SDI, PEC)
- A listing claim flow (submit, admin review, account creation)
- Custom post types and taxonomies for listings, breeds, interviews and editorial content
 
SCOPE — CRITICAL ITEMS FOR GO-LIVE
 
1. Verify custom post type registration, then a controlled plugin cleanup on staging: confirm which code registers each core CPT (services, breeds, interviews, listing_claim), then remove legacy ecommerce and marketplace plugins (WooCommerce, WCFM and related) safely, tested on staging, checking for orphaned data and broken URLs. NOTE: the multilingual WPML stack must be KEPT for launch — do not remove it.
 
2. Stripe tax_behavior fix: create new Price objects with inclusive tax behavior (VAT-inclusive 99 EUR and 199 EUR) and repoint Checkout to them.
 
3. Complete the Italian billing fields at Checkout: the fields already exist on the user profile; finish capturing them at Stripe Checkout, validate them (Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale, SDI, PEC, with an SDI-or-PEC requirement), store them to user meta, and display them in admin. Collection only — no external invoicing or SDI transmission.
 
4. Full end-to-end QA on staging against a checklist I will provide (subscription flows, tiers, downgrade-on-expiry, reminder emails, claim flow, VAT-inclusive pricing, etc.).
 
5. Support the sysadmin on the WP-CLI production push and a short post-launch stabilization period (bug-fixing of launch issues).
 
Some smaller enhancements (claim-flow polish, SEO plugin setup, multilingual-stack removal, analytics) are OUT OF SCOPE for this engagement and may be handled as separate work later.
 
REQUIRED SKILLS
 
- Strong WordPress development (custom themes, custom post types, taxonomies, ACF PRO, WP-Cron, user meta)
- Solid Stripe experience: Checkout, Customer Portal, Webhooks, Price and tax behavior, subscription lifecycle
- Comfortable safely picking up and extending an EXISTING codebase, not rebuilding
- PHP, WordPress REST API, debugging in a staging-to-production workflow
- Clear written English
 
NICE TO HAVE
 
- Familiarity with the Italian market and Italian B2B invoicing fields (Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale, SDI, PEC)

title: WordPress + Stripe Developer — Finish & Launch a Subscription Directory (Italian market)
description:
PROJECT OVERVIEW
 
I run Dogsify, an Italian directory and discovery platform for dog-related businesses (breeders, vets, groomers, boarding, etc.), built on WordPress with a custom theme and custom functionality. The site is in the final pre-launch stage and I need an experienced developer to pick up an existing codebase on a staging environment and complete the critical items needed to go live cleanly.
 
This is a finish-and-launch engagement, not a build-from-scratch. Most of the work is done. A separate sysadmin handles server infrastructure and the staging-to-production push, so you focus on the application and code side. I will provide a detailed handover document and staging access to the developer I select.
 
WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT
 
- Custom search, navigation and discovery front-end
- A Stripe-native subscription system (Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal and Webhooks) with three tiers, webhook event handling, WordPress user-meta sync, downgrade-on-expiry logic, and a reminder-email cron with idempotency
- Italian B2B billing fields already present on the user profile (Ragione Sociale, Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale, SDI, PEC)
- A listing claim flow (submit, admin review, account creation)
- Custom post types and taxonomies for listings, breeds, interviews and editorial content
 
SCOPE — CRITICAL ITEMS FOR GO-LIVE
 
1. Verify custom post type registration, then a controlled plugin cleanup on staging: confirm which code registers each core CPT (services, breeds, interviews, listing_claim), then remove legacy ecommerce and marketplace plugins (WooCommerce, WCFM and related) safely, tested on staging, checking for orphaned data and broken URLs. NOTE: the multilingual WPML stack must be KEPT for launch — do not remove it.
 
2. Stripe tax_behavior fix: create new Price objects with inclusive tax behavior (VAT-inclusive 99 EUR and 199 EUR) and repoint Checkout to them.
 
3. Complete the Italian billing fields at Checkout: the fields already exist on the user profile; finish capturing them at Stripe Checkout, validate them (Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale, SDI, PEC, with an SDI-or-PEC requirement), store them to user meta, and display them in admin. Collection only — no external invoicing or SDI transmission.
 
4. Full end-to-end QA on staging against a checklist I will provide (subscription flows, tiers, downgrade-on-expiry, reminder emails, claim flow, VAT-inclusive pricing, etc.).
 
5. Support the sysadmin on the WP-CLI production push and a short post-launch stabilization period (bug-fixing of launch issues).
 
Some smaller enhancements (claim-flow polish, SEO plugin setup, multilingual-stack removal, analytics) are OUT OF SCOPE for this engagement and may be handled as separate work later.
 
REQUIRED SKILLS
 
- Strong WordPress development (custom themes, custom post types, taxonomies, ACF PRO, WP-Cron, user meta)
- Solid Stripe experience: Checkout, Customer Portal, Webhooks, Price and tax behavior, subscription lifecycle
- Comfortable safely picking up and extending an EXISTING codebase, not rebuilding
- PHP, WordPress REST API, debugging in a staging-to-production workflow
- Clear written English
 
NICE TO HAVE
 
- Familiarity with the Italian market and Italian B2B invoicing fields (Partita IVA, Codice Fiscale, SDI, PEC)

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer for Live Product
description:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is a live product, not a prototype.

We are a Swiss software publisher. Our platform handles reservations and floor management for restaurants — real venues, real bookings, paying customers, running in production today.

We have two releases to ship: one in September, one on 1 January 2027. Both dates are firm. We are bringing in senior engineering capacity to get there, and we intend to keep working with the right person well beyond those dates.

What we offer is straightforward: a defined scope, direct contact with the decision-maker — no account manager, no committee, no three-day wait for an answer — and a codebase that already works and already earns.

What we ask is equally straightforward: that you can read someone else's code without insisting on rewriting it, that you tell us plainly when we are wrong, and that you hit dates.

If you are looking for a quick gig, this is not it. If you are looking for a client you can still be working with in two years, keep reading.


STACK

Backend — Node.js 18+, Express, MariaDB/MySQL (mysql2), JWT auth
Frontend — React + Vite
Payments — Stripe (Checkout Sessions, Customer Portal, webhooks)
Email — Nodemailer / SMTP
Hosting — Linux, SSH access, no container orchestration


FIRST ASSIGNMENT (paid, ~25-30 hours) — TECHNICAL AUDIT — STARTS THIS WEEK

We start every collaboration with one scoped, paid assignment.

Our platform has two reservation management views:
- a timeline/grid view (tables as rows, time slots as columns)
- a 2D floor-plan view (visual room layout)

The backend already exposes the required endpoints (rooms, tables, reservation move + move logs, availability slots). What we need is an honest technical assessment of the frontend and of the business logic consistency.

Deliverables:

1. Timeline view — functional audit
- Drag & drop of a reservation between tables: is the existing move endpoint actually wired to the UI?
- Overlap / double-booking detection
- Table combination (two 2-seaters merged into one 4-seater)
- Service rotation (two seatings on the same table in one evening)
- Walk-in creation from the view
- Tablet usability — this is the real-world use case, not desktop

2. 2D floor-plan view — feasibility assessment
- Do the table records currently store x/y coordinates? If not, what does the migration look like?
- What exists today vs. what needs to be built
- Realistic hour estimate for a production-ready editor

3. Written report (2-3 pages)
- What works, what is broken, what is missing
- Prioritised list: blocking / important / nice-to-have
- Your honest estimate for each

We want a real assessment, not reassurance. If the code is bad, say so.

If this goes well, we move to an ongoing engagement (20-25 h/week) through December.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Required
- 5+ years of professional full-stack JavaScript experience
- Solid SQL, comfortable with schema migrations on a live database
- Comfortable with SSH, environment variables and server-side debugging
- Experience with Stripe subscriptions
- Fluent written English
- European timezone (CET +/- 3 hours) — we want real-time overlap

Strong plus
- French (working language on our side, but English is fine)
- Experience taking over an undocumented codebase
- Multi-tenant SaaS experience

Not a fit
- Agencies subcontracting the work
- Teams operating behind a single freelancer profile
- "I can do everything" generalist proposals


HOW WE WORK

- NDA signed before any repository access
- You work on a dedicated branch; every change is reviewed before merge
- One 30-minute sync call per week, async the rest of the time
- All work is invoiced through Upwork
- Full IP assignment on all delivered work


COMMITMENT

Start date: immediately. The first assignment is ready to begin as soon as the NDA is signed — we are not waiting on internal approvals, budget cycles or anything else.

This is a deadline-driven engagement. We ship a first release in November and a second on 1 January 2027. If you cannot commit 20 h/week from now through December, please do not apply.

Rate is negotiable and based on experience. Please state your rate in your proposal.


TO APPLY

Please start your proposal with the word ORANGE, and in ONE sentence, tell us what you consider the riskiest part of the first assignment.

Proposals that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.

Do not send a generic portfolio. Tell us about one relevant project you built, and one thing that went wrong with it.

Include your hourly rate and how many hours per week you can start with this week.

title: Full-Stack Developer Needed – Private Contact Database Platform
description:
Full-Stack Developer Needed – Private Contact Database Platform with Subscriptions, Data Collection & WhatsApp

I am looking for an experienced full-stack developer to build a private, subscription-based web platform.

This will be a desktop-first web application containing a large professional contact database. Approved users will be able to search and filter contacts, create personalized message templates and quickly contact selected contacts through WhatsApp.

The exact industry and use case will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates.

I already have an example of a similar platform that I can demonstrate, which should make the required workflow very clear.

Main Functionality

1. Registration & Admin Approval

Users should be able to:

* Create an account
* Select a subscription plan
* Complete payment
* Wait for administrator approval
* Access the platform once approved and subscribed

From the admin dashboard, I need to be able to approve, reject, suspend and manage users, etc...

2. Subscription System

The platform should support recurring paid subscriptions.

Preferably through Stripe or another reliable European payment solution.

The system should automatically handle:

* Monthly/yearly subscriptions
* Different subscription tiers
* Renewals
* Cancellations
* Failed payments
* Active/inactive access

3. Large Contact Database

The core of the platform is a large private contact database.

Contacts will have multiple attributes such as:

* Name
* Organisation
* Position / role
* Country
* Phone / WhatsApp
* Email
* Category
* Other custom fields

The exact database structure will be provided privately.

4. Advanced Search & Filtering

Users should be able to quickly search through the database and combine multiple filters.

For example:

**Country + category + role + other attributes**

Search results should update quickly and the system must remain performant with a large number of contacts.

### 5. WhatsApp Desktop / Web Integration

This is an important feature.

Users should be able to create and save reusable message templates.

Templates should support variables such as:

`Hi (first_name), ...`

When viewing a contact, the user should be able to:

**Select contact → Select template → Click WhatsApp → WhatsApp Web/Desktop opens with the correct phone number and pre-filled message.**

The user will manually review and send the message.

We are **not looking for automated mass messaging**. The goal is to make individual outreach faster.

### 6. Message Template Manager

Each user should be able to:

* Create templates
* Edit templates
* Delete templates
* Insert dynamic contact information
* Select a template before opening WhatsApp

### 7. Data Collection / Scraping

An important part of the project is keeping the contact database populated and up to date.

The developer should have experience with:

* Web scraping
* APIs
* Automated data collection
* Data cleaning
* Duplicate detection
* Updating existing records
* CSV / Excel imports

The exact sources that need to be monitored or scraped will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates.

The solution should be maintainable, as sources and database fields may change over time.

8. Admin Dashboard

I need full control over the platform from an admin environment.

This should include:

* User management
* Registration approvals
* Subscription overview
* Contact management
* Add/edit/delete contacts
* Bulk imports
* Manage collected/scraped data
* Manage categories and filters
* Basic platform statistics

9. Security

The database contains valuable private business information, so security is important.

The platform should include:

* Secure authentication
* Protected database/API
* Role-based permissions
* Secure payment handling
* Password reset

Users should not simply be able to download or extract the entire database.

## Technology

I am open to recommendations regarding the technology stack.

Experience with technologies such as **React / Next.js, Node.js, Laravel, Django, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Stripe, Playwright, Puppeteer or similar technologies** is relevant.


## Timeline

**ASAP.**

Speed is very important for this project. I want to have a functional MVP online as quickly as realistically possible.

After the MVP, additional features and improvements can be developed.

## Important

I already have a **working example/reference platform** that demonstrates much of the functionality I am looking for.

I will show this privately to serious shortlisted candidates.

The selected developer will therefore have a clear reference for the expected user experience and functionality.

## When Applying

Please answer the following:

1. Have you built a similar database, CRM or subscription-based web application?
2. What technology stack would you recommend?
3. What is your experience with web scraping and automated data collection?
4. Have you implemented Stripe or another subscription system before?
5. How would you implement the WhatsApp Web/Desktop workflow?
6. How would you protect the database from users attempting to extract all contacts?
7. What would you include in the first MVP?
8. How quickly can you deliver a working first version?
9. Are you available to start immediately?

Please include relevant examples of previous work.

**Generic proposals will not be considered.**

We are a roofing contractor looking for an individual AI developer/expert, not a company, agency, or development firm, to work directly with us.

We are looking for experience with:

* OpenAI API
* Custom AI chatbots
* Knowledge bases/RAG
* WordPress integration
* Lead capture and qualification
* Human handoff/escalation
* AI voice agents and phone integrations
* Twilio or similar platforms
* APIs, webhooks, and automation tools

This is not a CRM integration project. Our focus is creating a high-quality, company-specific AI customer communication system for our website and potentially our after-hours calls.

We are looking for a hands-on individual expert who can design, build, and maintain the system long term, not an agency or firm.

Individual freelancers only. No agencies or development companies.

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer for Live Product
description:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is a live product, not a prototype.

We are a Swiss software publisher. Our platform handles reservations and floor management for restaurants — real venues, real bookings, paying customers, running in production today.

We have two releases to ship: one in September, one on 1 January 2027. Both dates are firm. We are bringing in senior engineering capacity to get there, and we intend to keep working with the right person well beyond those dates.

What we offer is straightforward: a defined scope, direct contact with the decision-maker — no account manager, no committee, no three-day wait for an answer — and a codebase that already works and already earns.

What we ask is equally straightforward: that you can read someone else's code without insisting on rewriting it, that you tell us plainly when we are wrong, and that you hit dates.

If you are looking for a quick gig, this is not it. If you are looking for a client you can still be working with in two years, keep reading.


STACK

Backend — Node.js 18+, Express, MariaDB/MySQL (mysql2), JWT auth
Frontend — React + Vite
Payments — Stripe (Checkout Sessions, Customer Portal, webhooks)
Email — Nodemailer / SMTP
Hosting — Linux, SSH access, no container orchestration


FIRST ASSIGNMENT (paid, ~25-30 hours) — TECHNICAL AUDIT — STARTS THIS WEEK

We start every collaboration with one scoped, paid assignment.

Our platform has two reservation management views:
- a timeline/grid view (tables as rows, time slots as columns)
- a 2D floor-plan view (visual room layout)

The backend already exposes the required endpoints (rooms, tables, reservation move + move logs, availability slots). What we need is an honest technical assessment of the frontend and of the business logic consistency.

Deliverables:

1. Timeline view — functional audit
- Drag & drop of a reservation between tables: is the existing move endpoint actually wired to the UI?
- Overlap / double-booking detection
- Table combination (two 2-seaters merged into one 4-seater)
- Service rotation (two seatings on the same table in one evening)
- Walk-in creation from the view
- Tablet usability — this is the real-world use case, not desktop

2. 2D floor-plan view — feasibility assessment
- Do the table records currently store x/y coordinates? If not, what does the migration look like?
- What exists today vs. what needs to be built
- Realistic hour estimate for a production-ready editor

3. Written report (2-3 pages)
- What works, what is broken, what is missing
- Prioritised list: blocking / important / nice-to-have
- Your honest estimate for each

We want a real assessment, not reassurance. If the code is bad, say so.

If this goes well, we move to an ongoing engagement (20-25 h/week) through December.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Required
- 5+ years of professional full-stack JavaScript experience
- Solid SQL, comfortable with schema migrations on a live database
- Comfortable with SSH, environment variables and server-side debugging
- Experience with Stripe subscriptions
- Fluent written English
- European timezone (CET +/- 3 hours) — we want real-time overlap

Strong plus
- French (working language on our side, but English is fine)
- Experience taking over an undocumented codebase
- Multi-tenant SaaS experience

Not a fit
- Agencies subcontracting the work
- Teams operating behind a single freelancer profile
- "I can do everything" generalist proposals


HOW WE WORK

- NDA signed before any repository access
- You work on a dedicated branch; every change is reviewed before merge
- One 30-minute sync call per week, async the rest of the time
- All work is invoiced through Upwork
- Full IP assignment on all delivered work


COMMITMENT

Start date: immediately. The first assignment is ready to begin as soon as the NDA is signed — we are not waiting on internal approvals, budget cycles or anything else.

This is a deadline-driven engagement. We ship a first release in November and a second on 1 January 2027. If you cannot commit 20 h/week from now through December, please do not apply.

Rate is negotiable and based on experience. Please state your rate in your proposal.


TO APPLY

Please start your proposal with the word ORANGE, and in ONE sentence, tell us what you consider the riskiest part of the first assignment.

Proposals that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.

Do not send a generic portfolio. Tell us about one relevant project you built, and one thing that went wrong with it.

Include your hourly rate and how many hours per week you can start with this week.

title: Full-Stack Developer Needed – Private Contact Database Platform
description:
Full-Stack Developer Needed – Private Contact Database Platform with Subscriptions, Data Collection & WhatsApp

I am looking for an experienced full-stack developer to build a private, subscription-based web platform.

This will be a desktop-first web application containing a large professional contact database. Approved users will be able to search and filter contacts, create personalized message templates and quickly contact selected contacts through WhatsApp.

The exact industry and use case will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates.

I already have an example of a similar platform that I can demonstrate, which should make the required workflow very clear.

Main Functionality

1. Registration & Admin Approval

Users should be able to:

* Create an account
* Select a subscription plan
* Complete payment
* Wait for administrator approval
* Access the platform once approved and subscribed

From the admin dashboard, I need to be able to approve, reject, suspend and manage users, etc...

2. Subscription System

The platform should support recurring paid subscriptions.

Preferably through Stripe or another reliable European payment solution.

The system should automatically handle:

* Monthly/yearly subscriptions
* Different subscription tiers
* Renewals
* Cancellations
* Failed payments
* Active/inactive access

3. Large Contact Database

The core of the platform is a large private contact database.

Contacts will have multiple attributes such as:

* Name
* Organisation
* Position / role
* Country
* Phone / WhatsApp
* Email
* Category
* Other custom fields

The exact database structure will be provided privately.

4. Advanced Search & Filtering

Users should be able to quickly search through the database and combine multiple filters.

For example:

**Country + category + role + other attributes**

Search results should update quickly and the system must remain performant with a large number of contacts.

### 5. WhatsApp Desktop / Web Integration

This is an important feature.

Users should be able to create and save reusable message templates.

Templates should support variables such as:

`Hi (first_name), ...`

When viewing a contact, the user should be able to:

**Select contact → Select template → Click WhatsApp → WhatsApp Web/Desktop opens with the correct phone number and pre-filled message.**

The user will manually review and send the message.

We are **not looking for automated mass messaging**. The goal is to make individual outreach faster.

### 6. Message Template Manager

Each user should be able to:

* Create templates
* Edit templates
* Delete templates
* Insert dynamic contact information
* Select a template before opening WhatsApp

### 7. Data Collection / Scraping

An important part of the project is keeping the contact database populated and up to date.

The developer should have experience with:

* Web scraping
* APIs
* Automated data collection
* Data cleaning
* Duplicate detection
* Updating existing records
* CSV / Excel imports

The exact sources that need to be monitored or scraped will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates.

The solution should be maintainable, as sources and database fields may change over time.

8. Admin Dashboard

I need full control over the platform from an admin environment.

This should include:

* User management
* Registration approvals
* Subscription overview
* Contact management
* Add/edit/delete contacts
* Bulk imports
* Manage collected/scraped data
* Manage categories and filters
* Basic platform statistics

9. Security

The database contains valuable private business information, so security is important.

The platform should include:

* Secure authentication
* Protected database/API
* Role-based permissions
* Secure payment handling
* Password reset

Users should not simply be able to download or extract the entire database.

## Technology

I am open to recommendations regarding the technology stack.

Experience with technologies such as **React / Next.js, Node.js, Laravel, Django, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Stripe, Playwright, Puppeteer or similar technologies** is relevant.


## Timeline

**ASAP.**

Speed is very important for this project. I want to have a functional MVP online as quickly as realistically possible.

After the MVP, additional features and improvements can be developed.

## Important

I already have a **working example/reference platform** that demonstrates much of the functionality I am looking for.

I will show this privately to serious shortlisted candidates.

The selected developer will therefore have a clear reference for the expected user experience and functionality.

## When Applying

Please answer the following:

1. Have you built a similar database, CRM or subscription-based web application?
2. What technology stack would you recommend?
3. What is your experience with web scraping and automated data collection?
4. Have you implemented Stripe or another subscription system before?
5. How would you implement the WhatsApp Web/Desktop workflow?
6. How would you protect the database from users attempting to extract all contacts?
7. What would you include in the first MVP?
8. How quickly can you deliver a working first version?
9. Are you available to start immediately?

Please include relevant examples of previous work.

**Generic proposals will not be considered.**

title: LifterLMS Member Area Expert — Deep Technical Ownership incl. Elementor, Lifter LMS for Longterm
description:

We're an internationally operating business running 7 WordPress properties, including a custom-built member platform connected to a PrestaShop store. We work with short, direct communication, and we value a pragmatic approach — smallest effort, biggest impact.

The project:
We're building a custom WordPress / LifterLMS member area — a hierarchical Collections and Bundle structure with automatic course enrollment, a tile-based dashboard, and a clean, API-ready architecture. 

A companion mobile app is the next phase once the member area is live.
The core plugin foundation is already built and working. 
What we need now is someone to take ownership of the rest and bring it to completion.

(1) The core plugin foundation — custom ID system, enrollment logic, PrestaShop integration — is completed. 
(2) The frontend/dashboard build (Elementor templates, lesson templates) is developed and pending final migration and verification on the live site.
What's still needed to be done and finish:
(3) Migrating and verifying the current build on our live site. 
(4) GetResponse integration, custom login flow, and email templates. 
(5) Performance optimization, multilingual setup, and user migration from Old memberarea 

What we're looking for:
- Absolute deep-dive, hands-on expertise in Elementor, WordPress, and specifically LifterLMS. 
- Solid understanding of enrollment logic, hooks and filters, memberships, and REST API integration. 
- Someone who thinks around corners, works innovatively, but also delivers correct, clean work — able to close out milestones properly, one at a time, and document them cleanly. 
- Someone who can look at an existing system, understand it properly, and keep building on it with precision — this is not a plugin-installation job.

++ Experience with mobile app / API development is a strong plus, since that's the planned next phase.


Long-term potential:
If this goes well, there's more beyond this one project — a developer who proves reliable here becomes our long-term go-to for LifterLMS and related WordPress work across our properties.

How this works:
Tell us:
(1) Your specific experience with LifterLMS, and project examples you've worked on. 
(2) Whether you have experience in app development / API work. (
3) Why you're the right candidate for this job.
Please also include your hourly rate for this initial stage. 

Shortlisted candidates will receive full technical documentation and the current project status, and will be asked to submit a fixed-price proposal per milestone – backend could also be provided.

title: Looking for Agentic AI Integration Engineer
description:
If this task can be successfully completed, along with payment I will provide a very positive review, as well as the potential for future work with much higher budgets, ideally leading to a long-term client relationship.

We are looking for someone experienced in AI-driven software development and autonomous coding agents.
Modern AI development tools can now handle much of an application build automatically — including backend setup, databases, API discovery, live-data connections, and user functionality.

Manus is one example. It can be given a concept such as an Inflation Monitor and handle much of the build itself, including finding relevant public data sources, connecting them, and creating the supporting backend.

Our objective is to use that same level of automation for products where most of the groundwork is already done. We would typically already have:
- The completed frontend/UI
- Clear specifications for what data each section needs
- Shared account, billing, authentication, and premium-access infrastructure
- Existing backend/database services where applicable

The remaining task is primarily to use AI tools to complete the backend and data integrations — identifying the appropriate sources, connecting them to our existing systems, and feeding the required data into the application.

We are looking for someone who knows how to guide and supervise AI tools to accomplish this efficiently, rather than manually building everything from scratch.

title: Senior AI SaaS Developer - AIMER Production Build
description:
We are building AIMER, a multi-industry SaaS platform focused on AI Employees, customer communication, booking systems, business management, subscriptions, and third-party integrations.

The UI/UX, technical blueprint, approximately 30 screens, backend logic, workflows, and product structure are already prepared. We are looking for a senior full-stack developer to turn the existing specification into a secure, scalable, production-ready SaaS.

Core requirements include:
- AI Employees and AI-powered workflows using OpenAI/LLMs
- Multi-channel customer communication
- Booking and calendar systems
- WhatsApp Business integration
- Shopify integration
- Google and Microsoft calendar integrations
- Stripe subscriptions and billing
- Multi-tenant architecture with proper data isolation
- Authentication, roles and permissions
- Admin dashboard and business management
- APIs and third-party integrations
- Notifications and automated workflows
- Secure database architecture and audit logging
- Production deployment, testing and error handling

The developer should be comfortable with modern full-stack technologies such as Next.js, React, Node.js/NestJS, PostgreSQL/Supabase, APIs, AI integrations, Stripe and cloud deployment.

Security, privacy, scalability and reliability are important. The system should be built properly for real customers, not as a demo or temporary MVP.

I already have the detailed specifications and visual references and will provide them to the selected developer.

I prefer a milestone-based fixed-price contract. Please review the requirements carefully and provide:
1. Your proposed architecture and technology choices.
2. Estimated timeline.
3. Fixed-price estimate and milestone breakdown.
4. Relevant examples of similar AI SaaS projects you have built.
5. Any technical risks or questions you identify before development starts.

We are looking for a long-term technical partner, not just someone to write code.

title: AI Full-Stack Developer – LLM, RAG & AI Integration
description:
We are looking for an experienced AI Full-Stack Developer to build and integrate AI-powered features into a modern web application.

The project involves developing AI functionality using LLMs, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), AI APIs, and intelligent automation, along with the supporting backend and frontend components.

Responsibilities:

* Develop AI-powered features using OpenAI and other LLM APIs
* Build RAG-based systems for searching and retrieving information from documents/data
* Develop AI chatbots and intelligent assistants
* Integrate AI capabilities into existing web applications
* Build backend APIs and services using Node.js / NestJS
* Develop frontend interfaces using React / Next.js
* Work with databases such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or Supabase
* Implement secure, scalable, and production-ready AI workflows
* Optimize AI responses, performance, and API usage
* Integrate third-party APIs and cloud services
* Deploy and maintain the application in a cloud environment

Required Skills:

* Strong experience with AI/LLM application development
* OpenAI API or similar LLM APIs
* RAG and vector/semantic search
* AI chatbot or AI agent development
* Node.js / TypeScript
* React / Next.js
* REST APIs
* PostgreSQL or similar databases
* Cloud platforms such as AWS
* Experience integrating AI into production applications

Project Goal:

Build a reliable, scalable AI-powered application that can understand user queries, retrieve relevant information, generate accurate responses, and integrate seamlessly with the existing web application.

Experience with AI agents, LangChain/LangGraph, vector databases, document processing, and AI automation is a plus.

title: AI Agents Developer
description:
Senior AI Voice & Automation Developer — Natural Conversational AI

We are looking for an experienced **AI Voice and Automation Developer** to help improve and expand an existing AI-powered voice system.

This is **not** a basic chatbot project and not simply an automated answering service.

Our highest priority is creating a voice AI experience that feels **natural, responsive, intelligent, and conversational** — not robotic, scripted, or frustrating.

The right developer should understand that excellent voice AI requires much more than connecting an LLM to a phone number. We are looking for someone who understands the entire system: voice, latency, prompting, memory, interruptions, tool calling, CRM integration, automation, and reliability.

## What We Need

The AI voice system should be able to:

* Carry on natural, fluid conversations.
* Listen and respond to what the caller actually says.
* Ask one question at a time instead of reading a questionnaire.
* Remember information already provided during the conversation.
* Avoid repeating questions unnecessarily.
* Handle interruptions and barge-in naturally.
* Handle pauses, hesitation, incomplete answers, and changes in direction.
* Maintain context throughout longer conversations.
* Respond correctly when callers provide information out of order.
* Keep responses concise and conversational.
* Minimize awkward delays between the caller and the AI.
* Trigger external actions based on what happens during the conversation.
* Save information into a CRM.
* Send text messages and trigger automations.
* Transfer or escalate calls when appropriate.
* Recognize when it should stop handling something and involve a human.
* Operate reliably in a real production environment.

Our goal is **not to deceive people into believing the AI is human**.

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer for Live Product
description:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is a live product, not a prototype.

We are a Swiss software publisher. Our platform handles reservations and floor management for restaurants — real venues, real bookings, paying customers, running in production today.

We have two releases to ship: one in September, one on 1 January 2027. Both dates are firm. We are bringing in senior engineering capacity to get there, and we intend to keep working with the right person well beyond those dates.

What we offer is straightforward: a defined scope, direct contact with the decision-maker — no account manager, no committee, no three-day wait for an answer — and a codebase that already works and already earns.

What we ask is equally straightforward: that you can read someone else's code without insisting on rewriting it, that you tell us plainly when we are wrong, and that you hit dates.

If you are looking for a quick gig, this is not it. If you are looking for a client you can still be working with in two years, keep reading.


STACK

Backend — Node.js 18+, Express, MariaDB/MySQL (mysql2), JWT auth
Frontend — React + Vite
Payments — Stripe (Checkout Sessions, Customer Portal, webhooks)
Email — Nodemailer / SMTP
Hosting — Linux, SSH access, no container orchestration


FIRST ASSIGNMENT (paid, ~25-30 hours) — TECHNICAL AUDIT — STARTS THIS WEEK

We start every collaboration with one scoped, paid assignment.

Our platform has two reservation management views:
- a timeline/grid view (tables as rows, time slots as columns)
- a 2D floor-plan view (visual room layout)

The backend already exposes the required endpoints (rooms, tables, reservation move + move logs, availability slots). What we need is an honest technical assessment of the frontend and of the business logic consistency.

Deliverables:

1. Timeline view — functional audit
- Drag & drop of a reservation between tables: is the existing move endpoint actually wired to the UI?
- Overlap / double-booking detection
- Table combination (two 2-seaters merged into one 4-seater)
- Service rotation (two seatings on the same table in one evening)
- Walk-in creation from the view
- Tablet usability — this is the real-world use case, not desktop

2. 2D floor-plan view — feasibility assessment
- Do the table records currently store x/y coordinates? If not, what does the migration look like?
- What exists today vs. what needs to be built
- Realistic hour estimate for a production-ready editor

3. Written report (2-3 pages)
- What works, what is broken, what is missing
- Prioritised list: blocking / important / nice-to-have
- Your honest estimate for each

We want a real assessment, not reassurance. If the code is bad, say so.

If this goes well, we move to an ongoing engagement (20-25 h/week) through December.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Required
- 5+ years of professional full-stack JavaScript experience
- Solid SQL, comfortable with schema migrations on a live database
- Comfortable with SSH, environment variables and server-side debugging
- Experience with Stripe subscriptions
- Fluent written English
- European timezone (CET +/- 3 hours) — we want real-time overlap

Strong plus
- French (working language on our side, but English is fine)
- Experience taking over an undocumented codebase
- Multi-tenant SaaS experience

Not a fit
- Agencies subcontracting the work
- Teams operating behind a single freelancer profile
- "I can do everything" generalist proposals


HOW WE WORK

- NDA signed before any repository access
- You work on a dedicated branch; every change is reviewed before merge
- One 30-minute sync call per week, async the rest of the time
- All work is invoiced through Upwork
- Full IP assignment on all delivered work


COMMITMENT

Start date: immediately. The first assignment is ready to begin as soon as the NDA is signed — we are not waiting on internal approvals, budget cycles or anything else.

This is a deadline-driven engagement. We ship a first release in November and a second on 1 January 2027. If you cannot commit 20 h/week from now through December, please do not apply.

Rate is negotiable and based on experience. Please state your rate in your proposal.


TO APPLY

Please start your proposal with the word ORANGE, and in ONE sentence, tell us what you consider the riskiest part of the first assignment.

Proposals that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.

Do not send a generic portfolio. Tell us about one relevant project you built, and one thing that went wrong with it.

Include your hourly rate and how many hours per week you can start with this week.
