title: AI-Native Full-Stack Dev (PHP/WordPress + React/TypeScript)
description:
Who we are

Gnostis is a digital media company running a network of roughly 50 review and comparison sites across Scandinavia and Europe - Denmark, Sweden, Finland and other markets. We publish product reviews, rankings and comparison content, monetized through affiliate partnerships. Small team, high rate of change: we're pushing edits and features across many sites every single day.

The stack you'd be inheriting

WordPress - but not the kind of WordPress you usually see on Upwork. Custom themes, custom post types, affiliate and pricing API integrations pulling live data into our comparison tables, and a long tail of plugins we've bent to purposes they weren't designed for. Deployment and debugging over SSH. Real SQL when the WordPress abstractions get in the way, which is often.

Day one to roughly month six, this is the work: fixing things, building features, integrating APIs, and keeping 50 sites healthy without breaking them one at a time.

Where this is going

We're moving off WordPress and onto our own platform. The likely shape: headless architecture, Next.js front-end in React/TypeScript, paired with either a headless CMS or a backend we build ourselves.

That isn't a vague someday - it's the reason this posting exists. We want the person who maintains the current system to be one of the people who builds its replacement. We're hiring for the second job as much as the first.

The honest version

You'd be doing WordPress and PHP work for a while before you touch the new platform. If that sounds like a bait-and-switch, don't apply. If maintaining WordPress indefinitely sounds perfectly fine and you have no interest in what comes after, also don't apply - you'd be bored and we'd have hired the wrong person.

The fit we're looking for is someone who can do the PHP work competently and without drama, while being visibly capable of the React/TypeScript work that's coming.

What we need you to already have
Strong PHP fundamentals. This is the entry ticket. Not "I can edit a theme" - actual language competence, able to read someone else's messy codebase and work out what it's doing.
Database comfort. SQL, indexes, query performance, and the ability to think about data structure rather than assuming WP_Query will solve it.
API integration experience. Both consuming third-party REST APIs (with the usual joys: rate limits, flaky responses, caching, stale pricing data) and building your own.
AI tools as part of your daily loop. Cursor, Copilot, Claude, whatever you've settled on. See below.
Terminal fluency. SSH, Linux basics, log reading, deployment. You shouldn't need a GUI to find out why a site is down.
Independence. You'll get context and access, not a spec written in Jira. We need someone who diagnoses, decides, and tells us what they found.
The thing we're actually screening for

Hands-on exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js.

This is the differentiator, and we'd rather be blunt about it than waste your time. We are not asking for five years of production React. Side projects count. A repo counts. Something you built for yourself and abandoned counts, as long as you can talk about it.

What doesn't work: "I've only ever done PHP because that's what my clients needed." We understand how that happens, and it's not a criticism - but it's not who we're hiring. PHP is the entry ticket. JavaScript is the actual reason we'd pick you over the next candidate.

On AI tools

We're not asking whether you've tried ChatGPT. We're asking whether AI-assisted development is genuinely how you work - in your editor, in your daily loop, meaningfully changing your throughput - and whether you have the judgment to catch it when it's confidently wrong. We'll ask about this specifically, and vague answers are easy to spot.

Please don't apply if you are
An entry-level WordPress/Elementor site-builder
An SEO generalist who does "some development"
A developer with zero exposure to and zero interest in modern JS frameworks
An agency sending a proposal on behalf of an unnamed team member
How this starts

A small, paid test task on a real, live project from our network. Scoped up front -  you get paid for it regardless of whether we continue.

If it goes well: ongoing hourly work with hours ramping up, and a long-term relationship that we'd like to turn into full-time. We're not looking for a one-off contractor. We're looking for the developer who's still here when the new platform ships.

Practical details
Working language is English.
We need a minimum of 4 hours of daily overlap with Central European Time - we're not asking you to relocate your sleep schedule, but we do need to be able to reach you.
Long-term, ideally full-time. Say so if that's not what you want.

How to apply

Answer the screening questions properly. Short and specific beats long and polished - we'd rather have three sentences that show you've done the work than three paragraphs about your commitment to quality. Links to code or live projects are worth more than any adjective you could use about yourself.

Proposals that are obviously templates get rejected without a reply. Start your proposal with the word headless so we know you read to the end.

--------------------------------------------------

Question 1 - JS/React exposure (the differentiator)

Link us to something you've built with JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js - a repo, a live site, a side project, anything real. Tell us in a few sentences what it does, what you found hardest about it, and what you'd build differently now. If it's a side project or unfinished, say so; that's fine.

-----------------------

Question 2 - AI fluency

Describe how AI tools actually fit into your development work. Which tools, in which parts of your workflow, and what do you deliberately not use them for? Then give us one concrete example of AI output you accepted and later regretted, or caught before it shipped - what was wrong with it and how did you notice?

------------------------

Question 3 - PHP/WordPress depth + API reality

Tell us about a time you integrated a third-party API into WordPress where the data mattered - pricing, inventory, anything that goes stale or breaks. How did you handle caching, rate limits, and failures? And how did you avoid taking the site down when the API had a bad day?

-------------------------

Question 4 - Terminal competence and independence

One of our 50 sites starts returning 500s. You have SSH access and no other information. Walk us through your first 15 minutes - the actual commands and the order you'd run them in

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer for Live Product
description:
ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is a live product, not a prototype.

We are a Swiss software publisher. Our platform handles reservations and floor management for restaurants — real venues, real bookings, paying customers, running in production today.

We have two releases to ship: one in September, one on 1 January 2027. Both dates are firm. We are bringing in senior engineering capacity to get there, and we intend to keep working with the right person well beyond those dates.

What we offer is straightforward: a defined scope, direct contact with the decision-maker — no account manager, no committee, no three-day wait for an answer — and a codebase that already works and already earns.

What we ask is equally straightforward: that you can read someone else's code without insisting on rewriting it, that you tell us plainly when we are wrong, and that you hit dates.

If you are looking for a quick gig, this is not it. If you are looking for a client you can still be working with in two years, keep reading.


STACK

Backend — Node.js 18+, Express, MariaDB/MySQL (mysql2), JWT auth
Frontend — React + Vite
Payments — Stripe (Checkout Sessions, Customer Portal, webhooks)
Email — Nodemailer / SMTP
Hosting — Linux, SSH access, no container orchestration


FIRST ASSIGNMENT (paid, ~25-30 hours) — TECHNICAL AUDIT — STARTS THIS WEEK

We start every collaboration with one scoped, paid assignment.

Our platform has two reservation management views:
- a timeline/grid view (tables as rows, time slots as columns)
- a 2D floor-plan view (visual room layout)

The backend already exposes the required endpoints (rooms, tables, reservation move + move logs, availability slots). What we need is an honest technical assessment of the frontend and of the business logic consistency.

Deliverables:

1. Timeline view — functional audit
- Drag & drop of a reservation between tables: is the existing move endpoint actually wired to the UI?
- Overlap / double-booking detection
- Table combination (two 2-seaters merged into one 4-seater)
- Service rotation (two seatings on the same table in one evening)
- Walk-in creation from the view
- Tablet usability — this is the real-world use case, not desktop

2. 2D floor-plan view — feasibility assessment
- Do the table records currently store x/y coordinates? If not, what does the migration look like?
- What exists today vs. what needs to be built
- Realistic hour estimate for a production-ready editor

3. Written report (2-3 pages)
- What works, what is broken, what is missing
- Prioritised list: blocking / important / nice-to-have
- Your honest estimate for each

We want a real assessment, not reassurance. If the code is bad, say so.

If this goes well, we move to an ongoing engagement (20-25 h/week) through December.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Required
- 5+ years of professional full-stack JavaScript experience
- Solid SQL, comfortable with schema migrations on a live database
- Comfortable with SSH, environment variables and server-side debugging
- Experience with Stripe subscriptions
- Fluent written English
- European timezone (CET +/- 3 hours) — we want real-time overlap

Strong plus
- French (working language on our side, but English is fine)
- Experience taking over an undocumented codebase
- Multi-tenant SaaS experience

Not a fit
- Agencies subcontracting the work
- Teams operating behind a single freelancer profile
- "I can do everything" generalist proposals


HOW WE WORK

- NDA signed before any repository access
- You work on a dedicated branch; every change is reviewed before merge
- One 30-minute sync call per week, async the rest of the time
- All work is invoiced through Upwork
- Full IP assignment on all delivered work


COMMITMENT

Start date: immediately. The first assignment is ready to begin as soon as the NDA is signed — we are not waiting on internal approvals, budget cycles or anything else.

This is a deadline-driven engagement. We ship a first release in November and a second on 1 January 2027. If you cannot commit 20 h/week from now through December, please do not apply.

Rate is negotiable and based on experience. Please state your rate in your proposal.


TO APPLY

Please start your proposal with the word ORANGE, and in ONE sentence, tell us what you consider the riskiest part of the first assignment.

Proposals that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.

Do not send a generic portfolio. Tell us about one relevant project you built, and one thing that went wrong with it.

Include your hourly rate and how many hours per week you can start with this week.

title: Full-Stack Developer Needed – Private Contact Database Platform
description:
Full-Stack Developer Needed – Private Contact Database Platform with Subscriptions, Data Collection & WhatsApp

I am looking for an experienced full-stack developer to build a private, subscription-based web platform.

This will be a desktop-first web application containing a large professional contact database. Approved users will be able to search and filter contacts, create personalized message templates and quickly contact selected contacts through WhatsApp.

The exact industry and use case will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates.

I already have an example of a similar platform that I can demonstrate, which should make the required workflow very clear.

Main Functionality

1. Registration & Admin Approval

Users should be able to:

* Create an account
* Select a subscription plan
* Complete payment
* Wait for administrator approval
* Access the platform once approved and subscribed

From the admin dashboard, I need to be able to approve, reject, suspend and manage users, etc...

2. Subscription System

The platform should support recurring paid subscriptions.

Preferably through Stripe or another reliable European payment solution.

The system should automatically handle:

* Monthly/yearly subscriptions
* Different subscription tiers
* Renewals
* Cancellations
* Failed payments
* Active/inactive access

3. Large Contact Database

The core of the platform is a large private contact database.

Contacts will have multiple attributes such as:

* Name
* Organisation
* Position / role
* Country
* Phone / WhatsApp
* Email
* Category
* Other custom fields

The exact database structure will be provided privately.

4. Advanced Search & Filtering

Users should be able to quickly search through the database and combine multiple filters.

For example:

**Country + category + role + other attributes**

Search results should update quickly and the system must remain performant with a large number of contacts.

### 5. WhatsApp Desktop / Web Integration

This is an important feature.

Users should be able to create and save reusable message templates.

Templates should support variables such as:

`Hi (first_name), ...`

When viewing a contact, the user should be able to:

**Select contact → Select template → Click WhatsApp → WhatsApp Web/Desktop opens with the correct phone number and pre-filled message.**

The user will manually review and send the message.

We are **not looking for automated mass messaging**. The goal is to make individual outreach faster.

### 6. Message Template Manager

Each user should be able to:

* Create templates
* Edit templates
* Delete templates
* Insert dynamic contact information
* Select a template before opening WhatsApp

### 7. Data Collection / Scraping

An important part of the project is keeping the contact database populated and up to date.

The developer should have experience with:

* Web scraping
* APIs
* Automated data collection
* Data cleaning
* Duplicate detection
* Updating existing records
* CSV / Excel imports

The exact sources that need to be monitored or scraped will be shared privately with shortlisted candidates.

The solution should be maintainable, as sources and database fields may change over time.

8. Admin Dashboard

I need full control over the platform from an admin environment.

This should include:

* User management
* Registration approvals
* Subscription overview
* Contact management
* Add/edit/delete contacts
* Bulk imports
* Manage collected/scraped data
* Manage categories and filters
* Basic platform statistics

9. Security

The database contains valuable private business information, so security is important.

The platform should include:

* Secure authentication
* Protected database/API
* Role-based permissions
* Secure payment handling
* Password reset

Users should not simply be able to download or extract the entire database.

## Technology

I am open to recommendations regarding the technology stack.

Experience with technologies such as **React / Next.js, Node.js, Laravel, Django, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Stripe, Playwright, Puppeteer or similar technologies** is relevant.


## Timeline

**ASAP.**

Speed is very important for this project. I want to have a functional MVP online as quickly as realistically possible.

After the MVP, additional features and improvements can be developed.

## Important

I already have a **working example/reference platform** that demonstrates much of the functionality I am looking for.

I will show this privately to serious shortlisted candidates.

The selected developer will therefore have a clear reference for the expected user experience and functionality.

## When Applying

Please answer the following:

1. Have you built a similar database, CRM or subscription-based web application?
2. What technology stack would you recommend?
3. What is your experience with web scraping and automated data collection?
4. Have you implemented Stripe or another subscription system before?
5. How would you implement the WhatsApp Web/Desktop workflow?
6. How would you protect the database from users attempting to extract all contacts?
7. What would you include in the first MVP?
8. How quickly can you deliver a working first version?
9. Are you available to start immediately?

Please include relevant examples of previous work.

**Generic proposals will not be considered.**

title: AI-Native Full-Stack Dev (PHP/WordPress + React/TypeScript)
description:
Who we are

Gnostis is a digital media company running a network of roughly 50 review and comparison sites across Scandinavia and Europe - Denmark, Sweden, Finland and other markets. We publish product reviews, rankings and comparison content, monetized through affiliate partnerships. Small team, high rate of change: we're pushing edits and features across many sites every single day.

The stack you'd be inheriting

WordPress - but not the kind of WordPress you usually see on Upwork. Custom themes, custom post types, affiliate and pricing API integrations pulling live data into our comparison tables, and a long tail of plugins we've bent to purposes they weren't designed for. Deployment and debugging over SSH. Real SQL when the WordPress abstractions get in the way, which is often.

Day one to roughly month six, this is the work: fixing things, building features, integrating APIs, and keeping 50 sites healthy without breaking them one at a time.

Where this is going

We're moving off WordPress and onto our own platform. The likely shape: headless architecture, Next.js front-end in React/TypeScript, paired with either a headless CMS or a backend we build ourselves.

That isn't a vague someday - it's the reason this posting exists. We want the person who maintains the current system to be one of the people who builds its replacement. We're hiring for the second job as much as the first.

The honest version

You'd be doing WordPress and PHP work for a while before you touch the new platform. If that sounds like a bait-and-switch, don't apply. If maintaining WordPress indefinitely sounds perfectly fine and you have no interest in what comes after, also don't apply - you'd be bored and we'd have hired the wrong person.

The fit we're looking for is someone who can do the PHP work competently and without drama, while being visibly capable of the React/TypeScript work that's coming.

What we need you to already have
Strong PHP fundamentals. This is the entry ticket. Not "I can edit a theme" - actual language competence, able to read someone else's messy codebase and work out what it's doing.
Database comfort. SQL, indexes, query performance, and the ability to think about data structure rather than assuming WP_Query will solve it.
API integration experience. Both consuming third-party REST APIs (with the usual joys: rate limits, flaky responses, caching, stale pricing data) and building your own.
AI tools as part of your daily loop. Cursor, Copilot, Claude, whatever you've settled on. See below.
Terminal fluency. SSH, Linux basics, log reading, deployment. You shouldn't need a GUI to find out why a site is down.
Independence. You'll get context and access, not a spec written in Jira. We need someone who diagnoses, decides, and tells us what they found.
The thing we're actually screening for

Hands-on exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js.

This is the differentiator, and we'd rather be blunt about it than waste your time. We are not asking for five years of production React. Side projects count. A repo counts. Something you built for yourself and abandoned counts, as long as you can talk about it.

What doesn't work: "I've only ever done PHP because that's what my clients needed." We understand how that happens, and it's not a criticism - but it's not who we're hiring. PHP is the entry ticket. JavaScript is the actual reason we'd pick you over the next candidate.

On AI tools

We're not asking whether you've tried ChatGPT. We're asking whether AI-assisted development is genuinely how you work - in your editor, in your daily loop, meaningfully changing your throughput - and whether you have the judgment to catch it when it's confidently wrong. We'll ask about this specifically, and vague answers are easy to spot.

Please don't apply if you are
An entry-level WordPress/Elementor site-builder
An SEO generalist who does "some development"
A developer with zero exposure to and zero interest in modern JS frameworks
An agency sending a proposal on behalf of an unnamed team member
How this starts

A small, paid test task on a real, live project from our network. Scoped up front -  you get paid for it regardless of whether we continue.

If it goes well: ongoing hourly work with hours ramping up, and a long-term relationship that we'd like to turn into full-time. We're not looking for a one-off contractor. We're looking for the developer who's still here when the new platform ships.

Practical details
Working language is English.
We need a minimum of 4 hours of daily overlap with Central European Time - we're not asking you to relocate your sleep schedule, but we do need to be able to reach you.
Long-term, ideally full-time. Say so if that's not what you want.

How to apply

Answer the screening questions properly. Short and specific beats long and polished - we'd rather have three sentences that show you've done the work than three paragraphs about your commitment to quality. Links to code or live projects are worth more than any adjective you could use about yourself.

Start your proposal with the word "HEADLESS" so we know you read to the end.

Senior Lead Laravel Developer & Database Architect with experience in integration and backend development of enterprise ERP platform and building robust, bi-directional integrations with Sage 50 Accounts & Sage 50 Payroll.

Our core platform is built on Laravel (10/11), FilamentPHP (v3/v4), and SaaSykit Tenancy. We need a sharp-minded, highly autonomous engineer who can take full ownership of database architecture, complex SQL performance tuning, multi-tenant logic, and fault-tolerant financial sync engines.

If you are a master of Laravel queues, complex relational databases (MySQL/MariaDB), and have real-world experience integrating web applications with Sage 50 Accounts and Payroll, this project is for you.


Key Responsibilities:
Laravel & Database Architecture: Design normalized, high-concurrency database schemas, optimize complex SQL queries (CTEs, execution plans, indexing), and balance Eloquent ORM with raw Query Builder for performance-critical tasks.

FilamentPHP & SaaSykit Ecosystem: Extend Filament admin panels—building custom resources, dynamic tables, relation managers, custom actions, and leveraging SaaSykit's multi-tenant tenant isolation mechanics.

Sage 50 Accounts & Payroll Integration: Architect bi-directional sync pipelines for:

Accounts: Invoices, credit notes, customer/supplier ledgers, nominal codes, general ledger journals, bank receipts, and VAT returns.

Payroll: Ingesting timesheets, overtime rates, and bonuses into Sage 50 Payroll; extracting gross-to-net summaries, tax/NI deductions, and posting journals back to Sage Accounts.

Queue & Idempotency Management: Build resilient Laravel Queue/Worker pipelines (Redis, Horizon, database locks) with strict idempotency keys to ensure no financial record or payroll line is ever duplicated or lost.

Deep SQL & MySQL/MariaDB Mastery: Expert in query optimization (EXPLAIN), indexing strategies, raw SQL, CTEs, window functions, and row-level locking.

FilamentPHP (v3/v4) & SaaSykit / Multi-Tenancy: Hands-on experience customizing Filament resources, forms, tables, and working within multi-tenant SaaS architectures.

Sage 50 Integration Experience: Proven commercial experience integrating Laravel apps with Sage 50 Accounts AND Sage 50 Payroll via Sage SDK, Sage Data Objects (SDO), Sage 50cloud REST APIs, or ODBC drivers.

FinTech & Accounting Knowledge: Solid understanding of double-entry bookkeeping, general ledgers, nominal codes, VAT rules, invoicing, and UK payroll logic (Tax, NI, Pensions, P45/P60).

PHP 8.2+ | Laravel 10/11 | FilamentPHP | SaaSykit | MySQL / MariaDB | Redis / Horizon | Sage 50 Accounts | Sage 50 Payroll | Git | REST APIs

title: Plugin Development
description:
Here is a clean, modular **Scope of Work (SOW)** template tailored for custom WordPress plugin development. You can adapt the items in brackets to match your project's exact features.

---

## **Scope of Work: Custom WordPress Plugin Development**

### **1. Project Overview & Goals**

Develop a custom, lightweight, and secure WordPress plugin to provide `[Core Purpose, e.g., automated employee reward tracking / specialized custom post type query]`. The plugin will integrate seamlessly with the existing WordPress architecture without altering core theme files.

---

### **2. Core Features & Functional Requirements**

* **Plugin Setup & Architecture:**
* Standard WordPress plugin structure compliant with WP coding standards.
* Activation/Deactivation hooks with proper database setup and cleanup routines.
* Role-based permissions (Restricted to `Administrator` or custom user roles).


* **Admin Dashboard / Settings Page:**
* Custom admin menu item under `[e.g., Settings / Tools / Custom Top Level]`.
* Options page for configuring `[e.g., API keys, default post counts, display preferences]`.
* Sanitized input handling and nonce validation on all form submissions.


* **Front-End Integration:**
* **Shortcodes & Blocks:** Creation of `[ [custom_display_shortcode] ]` or custom Gutenberg Block to render output on any page/post.
* **Styling & Assets:** Enqueued CSS/JS files scoped strictly to pages using the plugin features (ensuring zero impact on sitewide page load speeds).


* **Data & Backend Management:**
* *Database:* `[Option A: Custom database table created on activation / Option B: WP Options API / Option C: Custom Post Types & Meta]`.
* *AJAX/REST API:* Asynchronous requests handled via `wp_ajax_*` or standard WP REST API endpoints for seamless UI updates.



---

### **3. Technical & Performance Standards**

* **Security:** Full implementation of Nonces, Input Sanitization (`sanitize_text_field`), and Output Escaping (`esc_html`, `esc_attr`).
* **Performance:** Optimized SQL queries, leveraging WordPress Transients/Caching where applicable.
* **Compatibility:** Compatible with WordPress 6.x+, PHP 8.1+, and major page builders (if applicable).

---

### **4. Out of Scope (Explicit Exclusions)**

* Modification or styling of existing theme templates outside plugin shortcodes/blocks.
* Third-party plugin conflict resolution for non-standard or deprecated plugins.
* Ongoing monthly maintenance or feature additions post-delivery (unless covered under a separate SLA).

---

### **5. Deliverables & Milestones**

| Milestone | Deliverable | Target Timeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Architecture & Setup** | Functional skeleton plugin, DB migrations, and admin settings page. | `[e.g., 3 Days]` |
| **2. Feature Logic** | Core front-end shortcodes/blocks, backend logic, and API/Database integration. | `[e.g., 1 Week]` |
| **3. Testing & Handover** | QA testing, bug fixes, zip file deliverable, and basic installation docs. | `[e.g., 2 Days]` |

---

title: AI-Native Full-Stack Dev (PHP/WordPress + React/TypeScript)
description:
Who we are

Gnostis is a digital media company running a network of roughly 50 review and comparison sites across Scandinavia and Europe - Denmark, Sweden, Finland and other markets. We publish product reviews, rankings and comparison content, monetized through affiliate partnerships. Small team, high rate of change: we're pushing edits and features across many sites every single day.

The stack you'd be inheriting

WordPress - but not the kind of WordPress you usually see on Upwork. Custom themes, custom post types, affiliate and pricing API integrations pulling live data into our comparison tables, and a long tail of plugins we've bent to purposes they weren't designed for. Deployment and debugging over SSH. Real SQL when the WordPress abstractions get in the way, which is often.

Day one to roughly month six, this is the work: fixing things, building features, integrating APIs, and keeping 50 sites healthy without breaking them one at a time.

Where this is going

We're moving off WordPress and onto our own platform. The likely shape: headless architecture, Next.js front-end in React/TypeScript, paired with either a headless CMS or a backend we build ourselves.

That isn't a vague someday - it's the reason this posting exists. We want the person who maintains the current system to be one of the people who builds its replacement. We're hiring for the second job as much as the first.

The honest version

You'd be doing WordPress and PHP work for a while before you touch the new platform. If that sounds like a bait-and-switch, don't apply. If maintaining WordPress indefinitely sounds perfectly fine and you have no interest in what comes after, also don't apply - you'd be bored and we'd have hired the wrong person.

The fit we're looking for is someone who can do the PHP work competently and without drama, while being visibly capable of the React/TypeScript work that's coming.

What we need you to already have
Strong PHP fundamentals. This is the entry ticket. Not "I can edit a theme" - actual language competence, able to read someone else's messy codebase and work out what it's doing.
Database comfort. SQL, indexes, query performance, and the ability to think about data structure rather than assuming WP_Query will solve it.
API integration experience. Both consuming third-party REST APIs (with the usual joys: rate limits, flaky responses, caching, stale pricing data) and building your own.
AI tools as part of your daily loop. Cursor, Copilot, Claude, whatever you've settled on. See below.
Terminal fluency. SSH, Linux basics, log reading, deployment. You shouldn't need a GUI to find out why a site is down.
Independence. You'll get context and access, not a spec written in Jira. We need someone who diagnoses, decides, and tells us what they found.
The thing we're actually screening for

Hands-on exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js.

This is the differentiator, and we'd rather be blunt about it than waste your time. We are not asking for five years of production React. Side projects count. A repo counts. Something you built for yourself and abandoned counts, as long as you can talk about it.

What doesn't work: "I've only ever done PHP because that's what my clients needed." We understand how that happens, and it's not a criticism - but it's not who we're hiring. PHP is the entry ticket. JavaScript is the actual reason we'd pick you over the next candidate.

On AI tools

We're not asking whether you've tried ChatGPT. We're asking whether AI-assisted development is genuinely how you work - in your editor, in your daily loop, meaningfully changing your throughput - and whether you have the judgment to catch it when it's confidently wrong. We'll ask about this specifically, and vague answers are easy to spot.

Please don't apply if you are
An entry-level WordPress/Elementor site-builder
An SEO generalist who does "some development"
A developer with zero exposure to and zero interest in modern JS frameworks
An agency sending a proposal on behalf of an unnamed team member
How this starts

A small, paid test task on a real, live project from our network. Scoped up front -  you get paid for it regardless of whether we continue.

If it goes well: ongoing hourly work with hours ramping up, and a long-term relationship that we'd like to turn into full-time. We're not looking for a one-off contractor. We're looking for the developer who's still here when the new platform ships.

Practical details
Working language is English.
We need a minimum of 4 hours of daily overlap with Central European Time - we're not asking you to relocate your sleep schedule, but we do need to be able to reach you.
Long-term, ideally full-time. Say so if that's not what you want.

How to apply

Answer the screening questions properly. Short and specific beats long and polished - we'd rather have three sentences that show you've done the work than three paragraphs about your commitment to quality. Links to code or live projects are worth more than any adjective you could use about yourself.

Start your proposal with the word "HEADLESS" so we know you read to the end.

title: Senior Lead Laravel Developer with Sage 50 (Accounts & Payroll) Integration Experience
description:
Senior Lead Laravel Developer with Sage 50 (Accounts & Payroll) Integration Experience.

Laravel and Sage 50 Integration experience is MUST.

Senior Lead Laravel Developer & Database Architect with experience in integration and backend development of enterprise ERP platform and building robust, bi-directional integrations with Sage 50 Accounts & Sage 50 Payroll.

Our core platform is built on Laravel (10/11), FilamentPHP (v3/v4), and SaaSykit Tenancy. We need a sharp-minded, highly autonomous engineer who can take full ownership of database architecture, complex SQL performance tuning, multi-tenant logic, and fault-tolerant financial sync engines.

If you are a master of Laravel queues, complex relational databases (MySQL/MariaDB), and have real-world experience integrating web applications with Sage 50 Accounts and Payroll, this project is for you.


Key Responsibilities:
Laravel & Database Architecture: Design normalized, high-concurrency database schemas, optimize complex SQL queries (CTEs, execution plans, indexing), and balance Eloquent ORM with raw Query Builder for performance-critical tasks.

FilamentPHP & SaaSykit Ecosystem: Extend Filament admin panels—building custom resources, dynamic tables, relation managers, custom actions, and leveraging SaaSykit's multi-tenant tenant isolation mechanics.

Sage 50 Accounts & Payroll Integration: Architect bi-directional sync pipelines for:

Accounts: Invoices, credit notes, customer/supplier ledgers, nominal codes, general ledger journals, bank receipts, and VAT returns.

Payroll: Ingesting timesheets, overtime rates, and bonuses into Sage 50 Payroll; extracting gross-to-net summaries, tax/NI deductions, and posting journals back to Sage Accounts.

Queue & Idempotency Management: Build resilient Laravel Queue/Worker pipelines (Redis, Horizon, database locks) with strict idempotency keys to ensure no financial record or payroll line is ever duplicated or lost.

🎯 Required Skills & Experience:
5+ Years Senior Laravel/PHP Experience: Advanced mastery of Laravel 10/11, custom service providers, event sourcing, middleware, queues, jobs, and database transactions.

Deep SQL & MySQL/MariaDB Mastery: Expert in query optimization (EXPLAIN), indexing strategies, raw SQL, CTEs, window functions, and row-level locking.

FilamentPHP (v3/v4) & SaaSykit / Multi-Tenancy: Hands-on experience customizing Filament resources, forms, tables, and working within multi-tenant SaaS architectures.

Sage 50 Integration Experience: Proven commercial experience integrating Laravel apps with Sage 50 Accounts AND Sage 50 Payroll via Sage SDK, Sage Data Objects (SDO), Sage 50cloud REST APIs, or ODBC drivers.

FinTech & Accounting Knowledge: Solid understanding of double-entry bookkeeping, general ledgers, nominal codes, VAT rules, invoicing, and UK payroll logic (Tax, NI, Pensions, P45/P60).

🛠️ Tech Stack:
PHP 8.2+ | Laravel 10/11 | FilamentPHP | SaaSykit | MySQL / MariaDB | Redis / Horizon | Sage 50 Accounts | Sage 50 Payroll | Git | REST APIs

title: Plugin Development
description:
Here is a clean, modular **Scope of Work (SOW)** template tailored for custom WordPress plugin development. You can adapt the items in brackets to match your project's exact features.

---

## **Scope of Work: Custom WordPress Plugin Development**

### **1. Project Overview & Goals**

Develop a custom, lightweight, and secure WordPress plugin to provide `[Core Purpose, e.g., automated employee reward tracking / specialized custom post type query]`. The plugin will integrate seamlessly with the existing WordPress architecture without altering core theme files.

---

### **2. Core Features & Functional Requirements**

* **Plugin Setup & Architecture:**
* Standard WordPress plugin structure compliant with WP coding standards.
* Activation/Deactivation hooks with proper database setup and cleanup routines.
* Role-based permissions (Restricted to `Administrator` or custom user roles).


* **Admin Dashboard / Settings Page:**
* Custom admin menu item under `[e.g., Settings / Tools / Custom Top Level]`.
* Options page for configuring `[e.g., API keys, default post counts, display preferences]`.
* Sanitized input handling and nonce validation on all form submissions.


* **Front-End Integration:**
* **Shortcodes & Blocks:** Creation of `[ [custom_display_shortcode] ]` or custom Gutenberg Block to render output on any page/post.
* **Styling & Assets:** Enqueued CSS/JS files scoped strictly to pages using the plugin features (ensuring zero impact on sitewide page load speeds).


* **Data & Backend Management:**
* *Database:* `[Option A: Custom database table created on activation / Option B: WP Options API / Option C: Custom Post Types & Meta]`.
* *AJAX/REST API:* Asynchronous requests handled via `wp_ajax_*` or standard WP REST API endpoints for seamless UI updates.



---

### **3. Technical & Performance Standards**

* **Security:** Full implementation of Nonces, Input Sanitization (`sanitize_text_field`), and Output Escaping (`esc_html`, `esc_attr`).
* **Performance:** Optimized SQL queries, leveraging WordPress Transients/Caching where applicable.
* **Compatibility:** Compatible with WordPress 6.x+, PHP 8.1+, and major page builders (if applicable).

---

### **4. Out of Scope (Explicit Exclusions)**

* Modification or styling of existing theme templates outside plugin shortcodes/blocks.
* Third-party plugin conflict resolution for non-standard or deprecated plugins.
* Ongoing monthly maintenance or feature additions post-delivery (unless covered under a separate SLA).

---

### **5. Deliverables & Milestones**

| Milestone | Deliverable | Target Timeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Architecture & Setup** | Functional skeleton plugin, DB migrations, and admin settings page. | `[e.g., 3 Days]` |
| **2. Feature Logic** | Core front-end shortcodes/blocks, backend logic, and API/Database integration. | `[e.g., 1 Week]` |
| **3. Testing & Handover** | QA testing, bug fixes, zip file deliverable, and basic installation docs. | `[e.g., 2 Days]` |

title: Senior Product Engineer (Laravel / AI) — Dashlink
description:
The vision
Dashlink is a no-code platform for building dashboards — marketing, logistics, accounting, finance, you name it. Our integration layer plugs straight into our customers' APIs, turning scattered data into a clean, real-time command center with no glue code.

This is live in production today, serving everyone from lean SMBs to some of the largest enterprises in global payments and logistics. The hard part is done. Now comes the ambitious part: turning a great product into the default platform teams reach for when they need to see their business clearly.

We're hiring one builder to help drive that leap — someone who sees a half-finished thing, says "why not make this exceptional," and then does it.

What you'll do
Own real surface area. Take our Laravel + Livewire apps to the next level — architecture, performance, UX. You'll have the keys, not a permission slip.
Build AI into the product and into how we ship. Equal weight: LLM-powered features for customers, and AI-assisted workflows that let a tiny team move like a big one.
Own the runtime, not just the code. Configure, harden, and maintain the servers; keep queues healthy with Horizon + Redis; run things in Docker; treat security as first-class.
Make architectural calls and live with them. Decide what we build, what we don't, where the boundaries go. Take measured risks, ship, adjust.
Set the bar for a small team. Work alongside 2+ engineers — lead by example, mentor, shape how we hire and grow.
What we're looking for
Non-negotiable:

Deep, demonstrable Laravel expertise — you've built, scaled, and fixed serious systems and can show it. Livewire a strong plus.
You own the whole stack: Horizon + Redis in production · Docker day-to-day · server config, hardening & maintenance · Laravel's security stack (auth, encryption, secrets, dependency hygiene).
Real architecture instinct — you know the difference between clever and maintainable.
Hands-on AI fluency — you actively build and ship with LLMs/agents.
A can-do / why-not wiring — you take ownership, take measured risks, and you finish.
You want a small team — high trust, high autonomy, building something and making it big.
Bonus: no-code/low-code or multi-tenant SaaS · API-integration-heavy products · e-commerce, payments, shipping, or fulfillment · taking a product from "first version" to "platform."

Why it's worth your time
You get to build something real and make it big. The foundation is laid, the customers are serious, the ceiling is high. You bring startup speed; Itembase brings the backing and stability so you're not gambling your runway every quarter.

Remote-first, with EU-hours overlap.
Real ownership of product and architecture.
Senior compensation, discussed openly based on your experience.
Not for you if…
…you want a tightly-scoped lane and a handed-down backlog, you treat AI as someone else's job, you ship code but expect someone else to run the servers, or you need three approvals to change a file.

How to apply
Skip the cover letter. Send us:

Your best Laravel work (repo, project, or a short paragraph).
One thing you shipped with AI recently.
One sentence on something you'd make great that others accepted as "good enough."
We read every one properly, and we move fast.

Gnostis is a digital media company running a network of roughly 50 review and comparison sites across Scandinavia and Europe - Denmark, Sweden, Finland and other markets. We publish product reviews, rankings and comparison content, monetized through affiliate partnerships. Small team, high rate of change: we're pushing edits and features across many sites every single day.

The stack you'd be inheriting

WordPress - but not the kind of WordPress you usually see on Upwork. Custom themes, custom post types, affiliate and pricing API integrations pulling live data into our comparison tables, and a long tail of plugins we've bent to purposes they weren't designed for. Deployment and debugging over SSH. Real SQL when the WordPress abstractions get in the way, which is often.

Day one to roughly month six, this is the work: fixing things, building features, integrating APIs, and keeping 50 sites healthy without breaking them one at a time.

Where this is going

We're moving off WordPress and onto our own platform. The likely shape: headless architecture, Next.js front-end in React/TypeScript, paired with either a headless CMS or a backend we build ourselves.

That isn't a vague someday - it's the reason this posting exists. We want the person who maintains the current system to be one of the people who builds its replacement. We're hiring for the second job as much as the first.

The honest version

You'd be doing WordPress and PHP work for a while before you touch the new platform. If that sounds like a bait-and-switch, don't apply. If maintaining WordPress indefinitely sounds perfectly fine and you have no interest in what comes after, also don't apply - you'd be bored and we'd have hired the wrong person.

The fit we're looking for is someone who can do the PHP work competently and without drama, while being visibly capable of the React/TypeScript work that's coming.

What we need you to already have
Strong PHP fundamentals. This is the entry ticket. Not "I can edit a theme" - actual language competence, able to read someone else's messy codebase and work out what it's doing.
Database comfort. SQL, indexes, query performance, and the ability to think about data structure rather than assuming WP_Query will solve it.
API integration experience. Both consuming third-party REST APIs (with the usual joys: rate limits, flaky responses, caching, stale pricing data) and building your own.
AI tools as part of your daily loop. Cursor, Copilot, Claude, whatever you've settled on. See below.
Terminal fluency. SSH, Linux basics, log reading, deployment. You shouldn't need a GUI to find out why a site is down.
Independence. You'll get context and access, not a spec written in Jira. We need someone who diagnoses, decides, and tells us what they found.
The thing we're actually screening for

Hands-on exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js.

This is the differentiator, and we'd rather be blunt about it than waste your time. We are not asking for five years of production React. Side projects count. A repo counts. Something you built for yourself and abandoned counts, as long as you can talk about it.

What doesn't work: "I've only ever done PHP because that's what my clients needed." We understand how that happens, and it's not a criticism - but it's not who we're hiring. PHP is the entry ticket. JavaScript is the actual reason we'd pick you over the next candidate.

On AI tools

We're not asking whether you've tried ChatGPT. We're asking whether AI-assisted development is genuinely how you work - in your editor, in your daily loop, meaningfully changing your throughput - and whether you have the judgment to catch it when it's confidently wrong. We'll ask about this specifically, and vague answers are easy to spot.

Please don't apply if you are
An entry-level WordPress/Elementor site-builder
An SEO generalist who does "some development"
A developer with zero exposure to and zero interest in modern JS frameworks
An agency sending a proposal on behalf of an unnamed team member
How this starts

A small, paid test task on a real, live project from our network. Scoped up front -  you get paid for it regardless of whether we continue.

If it goes well: ongoing hourly work with hours ramping up, and a long-term relationship that we'd like to turn into full-time. We're not looking for a one-off contractor. We're looking for the developer who's still here when the new platform ships.

Practical details
Working language is English.
We need a minimum of 4 hours of daily overlap with Central European Time - we're not asking you to relocate your sleep schedule, but we do need to be able to reach you.
Long-term, ideally full-time. Say so if that's not what you want.

How to apply

Answer the screening questions properly. Short and specific beats long and polished - we'd rather have three sentences that show you've done the work than three paragraphs about your commitment to quality. Links to code or live projects are worth more than any adjective you could use about yourself.

Start your proposal with the word "HEADLESS" so we know you read to the end.

title: Senior Lead Laravel Developer with Sage 50 (Accounts & Payroll) Integration Experience
description:
Senior Lead Laravel Developer with Sage 50 (Accounts & Payroll) Integration Experience.

Laravel and Sage 50 Integration experience is MUST.

Senior Lead Laravel Developer & Database Architect with experience in integration and backend development of enterprise ERP platform and building robust, bi-directional integrations with Sage 50 Accounts & Sage 50 Payroll.

Our core platform is built on Laravel (10/11), FilamentPHP (v3/v4), and SaaSykit Tenancy. We need a sharp-minded, highly autonomous engineer who can take full ownership of database architecture, complex SQL performance tuning, multi-tenant logic, and fault-tolerant financial sync engines.

If you are a master of Laravel queues, complex relational databases (MySQL/MariaDB), and have real-world experience integrating web applications with Sage 50 Accounts and Payroll, this project is for you.


Key Responsibilities:
Laravel & Database Architecture: Design normalized, high-concurrency database schemas, optimize complex SQL queries (CTEs, execution plans, indexing), and balance Eloquent ORM with raw Query Builder for performance-critical tasks.

FilamentPHP & SaaSykit Ecosystem: Extend Filament admin panels—building custom resources, dynamic tables, relation managers, custom actions, and leveraging SaaSykit's multi-tenant tenant isolation mechanics.

Sage 50 Accounts & Payroll Integration: Architect bi-directional sync pipelines for:

Accounts: Invoices, credit notes, customer/supplier ledgers, nominal codes, general ledger journals, bank receipts, and VAT returns.

Payroll: Ingesting timesheets, overtime rates, and bonuses into Sage 50 Payroll; extracting gross-to-net summaries, tax/NI deductions, and posting journals back to Sage Accounts.

Queue & Idempotency Management: Build resilient Laravel Queue/Worker pipelines (Redis, Horizon, database locks) with strict idempotency keys to ensure no financial record or payroll line is ever duplicated or lost.

🎯 Required Skills & Experience:
5+ Years Senior Laravel/PHP Experience: Advanced mastery of Laravel 10/11, custom service providers, event sourcing, middleware, queues, jobs, and database transactions.

Deep SQL & MySQL/MariaDB Mastery: Expert in query optimization (EXPLAIN), indexing strategies, raw SQL, CTEs, window functions, and row-level locking.

FilamentPHP (v3/v4) & SaaSykit / Multi-Tenancy: Hands-on experience customizing Filament resources, forms, tables, and working within multi-tenant SaaS architectures.

Sage 50 Integration Experience: Proven commercial experience integrating Laravel apps with Sage 50 Accounts AND Sage 50 Payroll via Sage SDK, Sage Data Objects (SDO), Sage 50cloud REST APIs, or ODBC drivers.

FinTech & Accounting Knowledge: Solid understanding of double-entry bookkeeping, general ledgers, nominal codes, VAT rules, invoicing, and UK payroll logic (Tax, NI, Pensions, P45/P60).

🛠️ Tech Stack:
PHP 8.2+ | Laravel 10/11 | FilamentPHP | SaaSykit | MySQL / MariaDB | Redis / Horizon | Sage 50 Accounts | Sage 50 Payroll | Git | REST APIs

title: Laravel + PostGIS Property Data Site with Calculators & Lead Routing
description:
I'm building a UK property information website for homeowners and buyers. I have a complete written specification ready, around 55 pages covering database schema, data sources, page structure, design system and performance requirements. The chosen developer gets the full document. Greenfield build, no legacy code.

WHAT IT DOES

The site combines UK open property data with editorial content and cost tools. Postcode-level sold price data, street sale history and planning application records, all ingested and normalised from free government and open sources. Location-aware cost calculators for home improvements and energy installations. Editorial content in a CMS with location-specific data blocks embedded in articles. User accounts with saved areas and email alerts when new data appears. Enquiry forms routed to third-party partners, plus a paid directory for local businesses. A separate paid toolset for estate agents including image processing and PDF generation. Admin panel for managing all data, content, settings and partners.

There are two AI features, both using the Gemini API through a swappable driver interface. The first runs at ingest and rewrites impenetrable council planning descriptions into one plain-English line, stored once and never regenerated, with hard spend caps and graceful failure so it never blocks the import. The second is a drafting tool for estate agents that generates listing descriptions from structured inputs, with strict prompt constraints for UK advertising compliance. Both are metered per call and logged with token counts and cost. This is API integration work with careful cost control, not model training.

STACK, FIXED AND NOT OPEN TO SUBSTITUTION

Laravel 12, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Livewire and Alpine, Tailwind, Statamic, Filament, Meilisearch, Redis with Horizon, Stripe, Cloudflare, Gemini API, fal.ai.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU

Strong Laravel including queues, scheduled jobs and service-layer architecture. PostGIS and geospatial querying, which is central here rather than incidental. Real experience ingesting and normalising large datasets, since the main sold-price file is around 30 million rows with monthly deltas and there is fuzzy address matching between two separate sources. Server-rendered frontend skills, because there is no SPA framework and the site must work with JavaScript disabled while meeting a hard performance budget of under 2 seconds LCP on data pages. A clean minimalist frontend built from a design direction I provide, not a purchased theme. Technical SEO at scale, meaning programmatic page generation, structured data, sitemaps and meta templating. And an understanding of why a site like this must never create junk database rows, and how to prevent that.

DESIGN AND QUALITY BAR

Clean and fast is the whole point. The visual reference is a modern restrained dashboard aesthetic, neutral, card-based, one accent colour. Mobile-first, WCAG 2.2 AA, tested on real devices.

SCOPE

Single delivery, not phased releases. The spec includes a 20-step dependency order. Roughly half the work sits in the data layer before any user-facing feature becomes meaningful.

WHEN YOU APPLY, PLEASE TELL ME

One, a project where you used PostGIS or handled geospatial data, and what the hard part was. Two, the largest dataset you have imported into a production Laravel app, and how you handled updates. Three, whether you would build fuzzy address matching between two datasets differently to a normalised hash key, and why.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Laravel / AI) — Dashlink
description:
The vision
Dashlink is a no-code platform for building dashboards — marketing, logistics, accounting, finance, you name it. Our integration layer plugs straight into our customers' APIs, turning scattered data into a clean, real-time command center with no glue code.

This is live in production today, serving everyone from lean SMBs to some of the largest enterprises in global payments and logistics. The hard part is done. Now comes the ambitious part: turning a great product into the default platform teams reach for when they need to see their business clearly.

We're hiring one builder to help drive that leap — someone who sees a half-finished thing, says "why not make this exceptional," and then does it.

What you'll do
Own real surface area. Take our Laravel + Livewire apps to the next level — architecture, performance, UX. You'll have the keys, not a permission slip.
Build AI into the product and into how we ship. Equal weight: LLM-powered features for customers, and AI-assisted workflows that let a tiny team move like a big one.
Own the runtime, not just the code. Configure, harden, and maintain the servers; keep queues healthy with Horizon + Redis; run things in Docker; treat security as first-class.
Make architectural calls and live with them. Decide what we build, what we don't, where the boundaries go. Take measured risks, ship, adjust.
Set the bar for a small team. Work alongside 2+ engineers — lead by example, mentor, shape how we hire and grow.
What we're looking for
Non-negotiable:

Deep, demonstrable Laravel expertise — you've built, scaled, and fixed serious systems and can show it. Livewire a strong plus.
You own the whole stack: Horizon + Redis in production · Docker day-to-day · server config, hardening & maintenance · Laravel's security stack (auth, encryption, secrets, dependency hygiene).
Real architecture instinct — you know the difference between clever and maintainable.
Hands-on AI fluency — you actively build and ship with LLMs/agents.
A can-do / why-not wiring — you take ownership, take measured risks, and you finish.
You want a small team — high trust, high autonomy, building something and making it big.
Bonus: no-code/low-code or multi-tenant SaaS · API-integration-heavy products · e-commerce, payments, shipping, or fulfillment · taking a product from "first version" to "platform."

Why it's worth your time
You get to build something real and make it big. The foundation is laid, the customers are serious, the ceiling is high. You bring startup speed; Itembase brings the backing and stability so you're not gambling your runway every quarter.

Remote-first, with EU-hours overlap.
Real ownership of product and architecture.
Senior compensation, discussed openly based on your experience.
Not for you if…
…you want a tightly-scoped lane and a handed-down backlog, you treat AI as someone else's job, you ship code but expect someone else to run the servers, or you need three approvals to change a file.

How to apply
Skip the cover letter. Send us:

Your best Laravel work (repo, project, or a short paragraph).
One thing you shipped with AI recently.
One sentence on something you'd make great that others accepted as "good enough."
We read every one properly, and we move fast.

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer for Marketplace
description:
We’re looking for a Senior Full-Stack Developer to take full ownership of a growing WordPress/WooCommerce multi-vendor marketplace. This is a long-term opportunity with potential for ongoing maintenance and development.

Responsibilities:

• Audit WordPress, WooCommerce, custom plugins, PHP, and MySQL.
• Identify security issues, technical debt, slow queries, and bottlenecks.

Engagement: 30+ hrs/week, bi-weekly milestones, sync updates, and a weekly video call, with potential for ongoing work.

title: Laravel + PostGIS Property Data Site with Calculators & Lead Routing
description:
I'm building a UK property information website for homeowners and buyers. I have a complete written specification ready, around 55 pages covering database schema, data sources, page structure, design system and performance requirements. The chosen developer gets the full document. Greenfield build, no legacy code.

WHAT IT DOES

The site combines UK open property data with editorial content and cost tools. Postcode-level sold price data, street sale history and planning application records, all ingested and normalised from free government and open sources. Location-aware cost calculators for home improvements and energy installations. Editorial content in a CMS with location-specific data blocks embedded in articles. User accounts with saved areas and email alerts when new data appears. Enquiry forms routed to third-party partners, plus a paid directory for local businesses. A separate paid toolset for estate agents including image processing and PDF generation. Admin panel for managing all data, content, settings and partners.

There are two AI features, both using the Gemini API through a swappable driver interface. The first runs at ingest and rewrites impenetrable council planning descriptions into one plain-English line, stored once and never regenerated, with hard spend caps and graceful failure so it never blocks the import. The second is a drafting tool for estate agents that generates listing descriptions from structured inputs, with strict prompt constraints for UK advertising compliance. Both are metered per call and logged with token counts and cost. This is API integration work with careful cost control, not model training.

STACK, FIXED AND NOT OPEN TO SUBSTITUTION

Laravel 12, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Livewire and Alpine, Tailwind, Statamic, Filament, Meilisearch, Redis with Horizon, Stripe, Cloudflare, Gemini API, fal.ai.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU

Strong Laravel including queues, scheduled jobs and service-layer architecture. PostGIS and geospatial querying, which is central here rather than incidental. Real experience ingesting and normalising large datasets, since the main sold-price file is around 30 million rows with monthly deltas and there is fuzzy address matching between two separate sources. Server-rendered frontend skills, because there is no SPA framework and the site must work with JavaScript disabled while meeting a hard performance budget of under 2 seconds LCP on data pages. A clean minimalist frontend built from a design direction I provide, not a purchased theme. Technical SEO at scale, meaning programmatic page generation, structured data, sitemaps and meta templating. And an understanding of why a site like this must never create junk database rows, and how to prevent that.

DESIGN AND QUALITY BAR

Clean and fast is the whole point. The visual reference is a modern restrained dashboard aesthetic, neutral, card-based, one accent colour. Mobile-first, WCAG 2.2 AA, tested on real devices.

SCOPE

Single delivery, not phased releases. The spec includes a 20-step dependency order. Roughly half the work sits in the data layer before any user-facing feature becomes meaningful.

WHEN YOU APPLY, PLEASE TELL ME

One, a project where you used PostGIS or handled geospatial data, and what the hard part was. Two, the largest dataset you have imported into a production Laravel app, and how you handled updates. Three, whether you would build fuzzy address matching between two datasets differently to a normalised hash key, and why.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Laravel / AI) — Dashlink
description:
The vision
Dashlink is a no-code platform for building dashboards — marketing, logistics, accounting, finance, you name it. Our integration layer plugs straight into our customers' APIs, turning scattered data into a clean, real-time command center with no glue code.

This is live in production today, serving everyone from lean SMBs to some of the largest enterprises in global payments and logistics. The hard part is done. Now comes the ambitious part: turning a great product into the default platform teams reach for when they need to see their business clearly.

We're hiring one builder to help drive that leap — someone who sees a half-finished thing, says "why not make this exceptional," and then does it.

What you'll do
Own real surface area. Take our Laravel + Livewire apps to the next level — architecture, performance, UX. You'll have the keys, not a permission slip.
Build AI into the product and into how we ship. Equal weight: LLM-powered features for customers, and AI-assisted workflows that let a tiny team move like a big one.
Own the runtime, not just the code. Configure, harden, and maintain the servers; keep queues healthy with Horizon + Redis; run things in Docker; treat security as first-class.
Make architectural calls and live with them. Decide what we build, what we don't, where the boundaries go. Take measured risks, ship, adjust.
Set the bar for a small team. Work alongside 2+ engineers — lead by example, mentor, shape how we hire and grow.
What we're looking for
Non-negotiable:

Deep, demonstrable Laravel expertise — you've built, scaled, and fixed serious systems and can show it. Livewire a strong plus.
You own the whole stack: Horizon + Redis in production · Docker day-to-day · server config, hardening & maintenance · Laravel's security stack (auth, encryption, secrets, dependency hygiene).
Real architecture instinct — you know the difference between clever and maintainable.
Hands-on AI fluency — you actively build and ship with LLMs/agents.
A can-do / why-not wiring — you take ownership, take measured risks, and you finish.
You want a small team — high trust, high autonomy, building something and making it big.
Bonus: no-code/low-code or multi-tenant SaaS · API-integration-heavy products · e-commerce, payments, shipping, or fulfillment · taking a product from "first version" to "platform."

Why it's worth your time
You get to build something real and make it big. The foundation is laid, the customers are serious, the ceiling is high. You bring startup speed; Itembase brings the backing and stability so you're not gambling your runway every quarter.

Remote-first, with EU-hours overlap.
Real ownership of product and architecture.
Senior compensation, discussed openly based on your experience.
Not for you if…
…you want a tightly-scoped lane and a handed-down backlog, you treat AI as someone else's job, you ship code but expect someone else to run the servers, or you need three approvals to change a file.

How to apply
Skip the cover letter. Send us:

Your best Laravel work (repo, project, or a short paragraph).
One thing you shipped with AI recently.
One sentence on something you'd make great that others accepted as "good enough."
We read every one properly, and we move fast.

title: AI-Native Full-Stack Dev (PHP/WordPress + React/TypeScript)
description:
Who we are

Gnostis is a digital media company running a network of roughly 50 review and comparison sites across Scandinavia and Europe - Denmark, Sweden, Finland and other markets. We publish product reviews, rankings and comparison content, monetized through affiliate partnerships. Small team, high rate of change: we're pushing edits and features across many sites every single day.

The stack you'd be inheriting

WordPress - but not the kind of WordPress you usually see on Upwork. Custom themes, custom post types, affiliate and pricing API integrations pulling live data into our comparison tables, and a long tail of plugins we've bent to purposes they weren't designed for. Deployment and debugging over SSH. Real SQL when the WordPress abstractions get in the way, which is often.

Day one to roughly month six, this is the work: fixing things, building features, integrating APIs, and keeping 50 sites healthy without breaking them one at a time.

Where this is going

We're moving off WordPress and onto our own platform. The likely shape: headless architecture, Next.js front-end in React/TypeScript, paired with either a headless CMS or a backend we build ourselves.

That isn't a vague someday - it's the reason this posting exists. We want the person who maintains the current system to be one of the people who builds its replacement. We're hiring for the second job as much as the first.

The honest version

You'd be doing WordPress and PHP work for a while before you touch the new platform. If that sounds like a bait-and-switch, don't apply. If maintaining WordPress indefinitely sounds perfectly fine and you have no interest in what comes after, also don't apply - you'd be bored and we'd have hired the wrong person.

The fit we're looking for is someone who can do the PHP work competently and without drama, while being visibly capable of the React/TypeScript work that's coming.

What we need you to already have
Strong PHP fundamentals. This is the entry ticket. Not "I can edit a theme" - actual language competence, able to read someone else's messy codebase and work out what it's doing.
Database comfort. SQL, indexes, query performance, and the ability to think about data structure rather than assuming WP_Query will solve it.
API integration experience. Both consuming third-party REST APIs (with the usual joys: rate limits, flaky responses, caching, stale pricing data) and building your own.
AI tools as part of your daily loop. Cursor, Copilot, Claude, whatever you've settled on. See below.
Terminal fluency. SSH, Linux basics, log reading, deployment. You shouldn't need a GUI to find out why a site is down.
Independence. You'll get context and access, not a spec written in Jira. We need someone who diagnoses, decides, and tells us what they found.
The thing we're actually screening for

Hands-on exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js.

This is the differentiator, and we'd rather be blunt about it than waste your time. We are not asking for five years of production React. Side projects count. A repo counts. Something you built for yourself and abandoned counts, as long as you can talk about it.

What doesn't work: "I've only ever done PHP because that's what my clients needed." We understand how that happens, and it's not a criticism - but it's not who we're hiring. PHP is the entry ticket. JavaScript is the actual reason we'd pick you over the next candidate.

On AI tools

We're not asking whether you've tried ChatGPT. We're asking whether AI-assisted development is genuinely how you work - in your editor, in your daily loop, meaningfully changing your throughput - and whether you have the judgment to catch it when it's confidently wrong. We'll ask about this specifically, and vague answers are easy to spot.

Please don't apply if you are
An entry-level WordPress/Elementor site-builder
An SEO generalist who does "some development"
A developer with zero exposure to and zero interest in modern JS frameworks
An agency sending a proposal on behalf of an unnamed team member
How this starts

A small, paid test task on a real, live project from our network. Scoped up front -  you get paid for it regardless of whether we continue.

If it goes well: ongoing hourly work with hours ramping up, and a long-term relationship that we'd like to turn into full-time. We're not looking for a one-off contractor. We're looking for the developer who's still here when the new platform ships.

Practical details
Working language is English.
We need a minimum of 4 hours of daily overlap with Central European Time - we're not asking you to relocate your sleep schedule, but we do need to be able to reach you.
Long-term, ideally full-time. Say so if that's not what you want.

How to apply

Answer the screening questions properly. Short and specific beats long and polished - we'd rather have three sentences that show you've done the work than three paragraphs about your commitment to quality. Links to code or live projects are worth more than any adjective you could use about yourself.

Start your proposal with the word "HEADLESS" so we know you read to the end.

Accounts: Invoices, credit notes, customer/supplier ledgers, nominal codes, general ledger journals, bank receipts, and VAT returns.

Payroll: Ingesting timesheets, overtime rates, and bonuses into Sage 50 Payroll; extracting gross-to-net summaries, tax/NI deductions, and posting journals back to Sage Accounts.

🎯 Required Skills & Experience:
5+ Years Senior Laravel/PHP Experience: Advanced mastery of Laravel 10/11, custom service providers, event sourcing, middleware, queues, jobs, and database transactions.

Deep SQL & MySQL/MariaDB Mastery: Expert in query optimization (EXPLAIN), indexing strategies, raw SQL, CTEs, window functions, and row-level locking.

FilamentPHP (v3/v4) & SaaSykit / Multi-Tenancy: Hands-on experience customizing Filament resources, forms, tables, and working within multi-tenant SaaS architectures.

Sage 50 Integration Experience: Proven commercial experience integrating Laravel apps with Sage 50 Accounts AND Sage 50 Payroll via Sage SDK, Sage Data Objects (SDO), Sage 50cloud REST APIs, or ODBC drivers.

FinTech & Accounting Knowledge: Solid understanding of double-entry bookkeeping, general ledgers, nominal codes, VAT rules, invoicing, and UK payroll logic (Tax, NI, Pensions, P45/P60).

description:
Full-Stack Developer for UK EdTech Learning Platform

I am looking for a full-stack developer to help build the next stage of Teachers That Tutor, an existing UK education business.

We currently have an established website and a YouTube channel with 7,000+ subscribers, which will provide an existing audience for launching and testing the new platform.

What I want to build

I want to transform Teachers That Tutor into a modern, subscription-based educational web application for UK primary pupils and their parents.

The initial MVP will focus mainly on Years 3–6, with particular emphasis on Year 6 SATs.

The platform will have seven main areas:

Dashboard – overview of a child's learning, activity and recommended next steps
Learn – curriculum content organised by Year → Subject → Topic → Lesson
Practice – teacher-written interactive questions with automatic marking and explanations
Studio – searchable educational video library linked to curriculum topics
Insights – progress tracking and parent-friendly learning analytics
Ask TTT – AI-powered educational support and personalised practice
Papers – SATs papers, mark schemes and other assessment resources

Parents should be able to create an account, add child profiles and monitor their children's learning and progress.

What I need from you

I am looking for someone capable of helping develop the platform from MVP through to a functioning subscription product.

Relevant experience would include:

React / Next.js
TypeScript / JavaScript
Node.js or similar backend technology
Database design
User authentication
API integration
Stripe/subscription payments
AI API integration
Responsive web applications
SaaS/dashboard development
Secure handling of user data

I am open to your recommendations regarding the exact technology stack.

Content Management

An important requirement is that I can manage the educational content myself.

I need an admin/CMS area that eventually allows me to add and edit:

Year groups and subjects
Curriculum topics
Lessons
Questions and answers
Teacher explanations
Videos
Practice sets
SATs/resources

I do not want routine educational content updates to require developer involvement.

How I want to build it

I do not want the entire platform built at once.

My preference is to develop an MVP incrementally through clearly defined milestones.

For example:

Stage 1: User accounts, child profiles, curriculum structure and dashboard

Stage 2: Learn and Studio

Stage 3: Question database, Practice and automatic marking

Stage 4: Progress tracking and Insights

Stage 5: Ask TTT / AI integration

Stage 6: Subscriptions and further development

The exact order can be discussed with the successful developer.

My initial development budget is approximately £1,000 per month, and I am looking for an ongoing relationship of 6+ months rather than a one-off website build.

If the platform gains traction, I would expect development to continue and the scope/budget to grow accordingly.

About me

I will provide the educational and product expertise, including:

UK primary curriculum knowledge
Educational content
Questions and answers
Video content
Product direction
User testing
Existing audience for beta testing and marketing

I am therefore looking for someone who can bring the technical/product development expertise to complement this.

Good communication is extremely important to me.

I would like someone who is happy to discuss ideas, suggest better technical solutions where appropriate, explain technical decisions clearly and build the product collaboratively.

When applying

Please include:

A brief introduction.
Examples of SaaS/web applications you have personally built.
Your experience with React/Next.js or similar technologies.
Any experience with Stripe subscriptions.
Any experience integrating AI/LLM APIs.
Your recommended technology stack for this project.
Your hourly rate and approximate availability each month.
What you think should be included in the first MVP milestone.
Any initial concerns or suggestions about the proposed platform.

Please don't send a generic proposal. I am particularly interested in hearing how you would approach this specific product.

Ownership

The successful developer must be comfortable with the Teachers That Tutor business retaining ownership and administrative access to the source code/repository, hosting, database, domain, payment accounts and other core infrastructure.

I am looking for the right developer to potentially work with Teachers That Tutor for the long term rather than simply someone to build a website and move on. (please see image attached of the platform dashboard concept).
