description:
Full-Stack Developer for UK EdTech Learning Platform

I am looking for a full-stack developer to help build the next stage of Teachers That Tutor, an existing UK education business.

We currently have an established website and a YouTube channel with 7,000+ subscribers, which will provide an existing audience for launching and testing the new platform.

What I want to build

I want to transform Teachers That Tutor into a modern, subscription-based educational web application for UK primary pupils and their parents.

The initial MVP will focus mainly on Years 3–6, with particular emphasis on Year 6 SATs.

The platform will have seven main areas:

Dashboard – overview of a child's learning, activity and recommended next steps
Learn – curriculum content organised by Year → Subject → Topic → Lesson
Practice – teacher-written interactive questions with automatic marking and explanations
Studio – searchable educational video library linked to curriculum topics
Insights – progress tracking and parent-friendly learning analytics
Ask TTT – AI-powered educational support and personalised practice
Papers – SATs papers, mark schemes and other assessment resources

Parents should be able to create an account, add child profiles and monitor their children's learning and progress.

What I need from you

I am looking for someone capable of helping develop the platform from MVP through to a functioning subscription product.

Relevant experience would include:

React / Next.js
TypeScript / JavaScript
Node.js or similar backend technology
Database design
User authentication
API integration
Stripe/subscription payments
AI API integration
Responsive web applications
SaaS/dashboard development
Secure handling of user data

I am open to your recommendations regarding the exact technology stack.

Content Management

An important requirement is that I can manage the educational content myself.

I need an admin/CMS area that eventually allows me to add and edit:

Year groups and subjects
Curriculum topics
Lessons
Questions and answers
Teacher explanations
Videos
Practice sets
SATs/resources

I do not want routine educational content updates to require developer involvement.

How I want to build it

I do not want the entire platform built at once.

My preference is to develop an MVP incrementally through clearly defined milestones.

For example:

Stage 1: User accounts, child profiles, curriculum structure and dashboard

Stage 2: Learn and Studio

Stage 3: Question database, Practice and automatic marking

Stage 4: Progress tracking and Insights

Stage 5: Ask TTT / AI integration

Stage 6: Subscriptions and further development

The exact order can be discussed with the successful developer.

My initial development budget is approximately £1,000 per month, and I am looking for an ongoing relationship of 6+ months rather than a one-off website build.

If the platform gains traction, I would expect development to continue and the scope/budget to grow accordingly.

About me

I will provide the educational and product expertise, including:

UK primary curriculum knowledge
Educational content
Questions and answers
Video content
Product direction
User testing
Existing audience for beta testing and marketing

I am therefore looking for someone who can bring the technical/product development expertise to complement this.

Good communication is extremely important to me.

I would like someone who is happy to discuss ideas, suggest better technical solutions where appropriate, explain technical decisions clearly and build the product collaboratively.

When applying

Please include:

A brief introduction.
Examples of SaaS/web applications you have personally built.
Your experience with React/Next.js or similar technologies.
Any experience with Stripe subscriptions.
Any experience integrating AI/LLM APIs.
Your recommended technology stack for this project.
Your hourly rate and approximate availability each month.
What you think should be included in the first MVP milestone.
Any initial concerns or suggestions about the proposed platform.

Please don't send a generic proposal. I am particularly interested in hearing how you would approach this specific product.

Ownership

The successful developer must be comfortable with the Teachers That Tutor business retaining ownership and administrative access to the source code/repository, hosting, database, domain, payment accounts and other core infrastructure.

I am looking for the right developer to potentially work with Teachers That Tutor for the long term rather than simply someone to build a website and move on. (please see image attached of the platform dashboard concept).

title: Laravel + PostGIS Property Data Site with Calculators & Lead Routing
description:
I'm building a UK property information website for homeowners and buyers. I have a complete written specification ready, around 55 pages covering database schema, data sources, page structure, design system and performance requirements. The chosen developer gets the full document. Greenfield build, no legacy code.

WHAT IT DOES

The site combines UK open property data with editorial content and cost tools. Postcode-level sold price data, street sale history and planning application records, all ingested and normalised from free government and open sources. Location-aware cost calculators for home improvements and energy installations. Editorial content in a CMS with location-specific data blocks embedded in articles. User accounts with saved areas and email alerts when new data appears. Enquiry forms routed to third-party partners, plus a paid directory for local businesses. A separate paid toolset for estate agents including image processing and PDF generation. Admin panel for managing all data, content, settings and partners.

There are two AI features, both using the Gemini API through a swappable driver interface. The first runs at ingest and rewrites impenetrable council planning descriptions into one plain-English line, stored once and never regenerated, with hard spend caps and graceful failure so it never blocks the import. The second is a drafting tool for estate agents that generates listing descriptions from structured inputs, with strict prompt constraints for UK advertising compliance. Both are metered per call and logged with token counts and cost. This is API integration work with careful cost control, not model training.

STACK, FIXED AND NOT OPEN TO SUBSTITUTION

Laravel 12, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Livewire and Alpine, Tailwind, Statamic, Filament, Meilisearch, Redis with Horizon, Stripe, Cloudflare, Gemini API, fal.ai.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU

Strong Laravel including queues, scheduled jobs and service-layer architecture. PostGIS and geospatial querying, which is central here rather than incidental. Real experience ingesting and normalising large datasets, since the main sold-price file is around 30 million rows with monthly deltas and there is fuzzy address matching between two separate sources. Server-rendered frontend skills, because there is no SPA framework and the site must work with JavaScript disabled while meeting a hard performance budget of under 2 seconds LCP on data pages. A clean minimalist frontend built from a design direction I provide, not a purchased theme. Technical SEO at scale, meaning programmatic page generation, structured data, sitemaps and meta templating. And an understanding of why a site like this must never create junk database rows, and how to prevent that.

DESIGN AND QUALITY BAR

Clean and fast is the whole point. The visual reference is a modern restrained dashboard aesthetic, neutral, card-based, one accent colour. Mobile-first, WCAG 2.2 AA, tested on real devices.

SCOPE

Single delivery, not phased releases. The spec includes a 20-step dependency order. Roughly half the work sits in the data layer before any user-facing feature becomes meaningful.

WHEN YOU APPLY, PLEASE TELL ME

One, a project where you used PostGIS or handled geospatial data, and what the hard part was. Two, the largest dataset you have imported into a production Laravel app, and how you handled updates. Three, whether you would build fuzzy address matching between two datasets differently to a normalised hash key, and why.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Laravel / AI) — Dashlink
description:
The vision
Dashlink is a no-code platform for building dashboards — marketing, logistics, accounting, finance, you name it. Our integration layer plugs straight into our customers' APIs, turning scattered data into a clean, real-time command center with no glue code.

This is live in production today, serving everyone from lean SMBs to some of the largest enterprises in global payments and logistics. The hard part is done. Now comes the ambitious part: turning a great product into the default platform teams reach for when they need to see their business clearly.

We're hiring one builder to help drive that leap — someone who sees a half-finished thing, says "why not make this exceptional," and then does it.

What you'll do
Own real surface area. Take our Laravel + Livewire apps to the next level — architecture, performance, UX. You'll have the keys, not a permission slip.
Build AI into the product and into how we ship. Equal weight: LLM-powered features for customers, and AI-assisted workflows that let a tiny team move like a big one.
Own the runtime, not just the code. Configure, harden, and maintain the servers; keep queues healthy with Horizon + Redis; run things in Docker; treat security as first-class.
Make architectural calls and live with them. Decide what we build, what we don't, where the boundaries go. Take measured risks, ship, adjust.
Set the bar for a small team. Work alongside 2+ engineers — lead by example, mentor, shape how we hire and grow.
What we're looking for
Non-negotiable:

Deep, demonstrable Laravel expertise — you've built, scaled, and fixed serious systems and can show it. Livewire a strong plus.
You own the whole stack: Horizon + Redis in production · Docker day-to-day · server config, hardening & maintenance · Laravel's security stack (auth, encryption, secrets, dependency hygiene).
Real architecture instinct — you know the difference between clever and maintainable.
Hands-on AI fluency — you actively build and ship with LLMs/agents.
A can-do / why-not wiring — you take ownership, take measured risks, and you finish.
You want a small team — high trust, high autonomy, building something and making it big.
Bonus: no-code/low-code or multi-tenant SaaS · API-integration-heavy products · e-commerce, payments, shipping, or fulfillment · taking a product from "first version" to "platform."

Why it's worth your time
You get to build something real and make it big. The foundation is laid, the customers are serious, the ceiling is high. You bring startup speed; Itembase brings the backing and stability so you're not gambling your runway every quarter.

Remote-first, with EU-hours overlap.
Real ownership of product and architecture.
Senior compensation, discussed openly based on your experience.
Not for you if…
…you want a tightly-scoped lane and a handed-down backlog, you treat AI as someone else's job, you ship code but expect someone else to run the servers, or you need three approvals to change a file.

How to apply
Skip the cover letter. Send us:

Your best Laravel work (repo, project, or a short paragraph).
One thing you shipped with AI recently.
One sentence on something you'd make great that others accepted as "good enough."
We read every one properly, and we move fast.

title: AI-Native Full-Stack Dev (PHP/WordPress + React/TypeScript)
description:
Who we are

Gnostis is a digital media company running a network of roughly 50 review and comparison sites across Scandinavia and Europe - Denmark, Sweden, Finland and other markets. We publish product reviews, rankings and comparison content, monetized through affiliate partnerships. Small team, high rate of change: we're pushing edits and features across many sites every single day.

The stack you'd be inheriting

WordPress - but not the kind of WordPress you usually see on Upwork. Custom themes, custom post types, affiliate and pricing API integrations pulling live data into our comparison tables, and a long tail of plugins we've bent to purposes they weren't designed for. Deployment and debugging over SSH. Real SQL when the WordPress abstractions get in the way, which is often.

Day one to roughly month six, this is the work: fixing things, building features, integrating APIs, and keeping 50 sites healthy without breaking them one at a time.

Where this is going

We're moving off WordPress and onto our own platform. The likely shape: headless architecture, Next.js front-end in React/TypeScript, paired with either a headless CMS or a backend we build ourselves.

That isn't a vague someday - it's the reason this posting exists. We want the person who maintains the current system to be one of the people who builds its replacement. We're hiring for the second job as much as the first.

The honest version

You'd be doing WordPress and PHP work for a while before you touch the new platform. If that sounds like a bait-and-switch, don't apply. If maintaining WordPress indefinitely sounds perfectly fine and you have no interest in what comes after, also don't apply - you'd be bored and we'd have hired the wrong person.

The fit we're looking for is someone who can do the PHP work competently and without drama, while being visibly capable of the React/TypeScript work that's coming.

What we need you to already have
Strong PHP fundamentals. This is the entry ticket. Not "I can edit a theme" - actual language competence, able to read someone else's messy codebase and work out what it's doing.
Database comfort. SQL, indexes, query performance, and the ability to think about data structure rather than assuming WP_Query will solve it.
API integration experience. Both consuming third-party REST APIs (with the usual joys: rate limits, flaky responses, caching, stale pricing data) and building your own.
AI tools as part of your daily loop. Cursor, Copilot, Claude, whatever you've settled on. See below.
Terminal fluency. SSH, Linux basics, log reading, deployment. You shouldn't need a GUI to find out why a site is down.
Independence. You'll get context and access, not a spec written in Jira. We need someone who diagnoses, decides, and tells us what they found.
The thing we're actually screening for

Hands-on exposure to JavaScript/TypeScript and React or Next.js.

This is the differentiator, and we'd rather be blunt about it than waste your time. We are not asking for five years of production React. Side projects count. A repo counts. Something you built for yourself and abandoned counts, as long as you can talk about it.

What doesn't work: "I've only ever done PHP because that's what my clients needed." We understand how that happens, and it's not a criticism - but it's not who we're hiring. PHP is the entry ticket. JavaScript is the actual reason we'd pick you over the next candidate.

On AI tools

We're not asking whether you've tried ChatGPT. We're asking whether AI-assisted development is genuinely how you work - in your editor, in your daily loop, meaningfully changing your throughput - and whether you have the judgment to catch it when it's confidently wrong. We'll ask about this specifically, and vague answers are easy to spot.

Please don't apply if you are
An entry-level WordPress/Elementor site-builder
An SEO generalist who does "some development"
A developer with zero exposure to and zero interest in modern JS frameworks
An agency sending a proposal on behalf of an unnamed team member
How this starts

A small, paid test task on a real, live project from our network. Scoped up front -  you get paid for it regardless of whether we continue.

If it goes well: ongoing hourly work with hours ramping up, and a long-term relationship that we'd like to turn into full-time. We're not looking for a one-off contractor. We're looking for the developer who's still here when the new platform ships.

Practical details
Working language is English.
We need a minimum of 4 hours of daily overlap with Central European Time - we're not asking you to relocate your sleep schedule, but we do need to be able to reach you.
Long-term, ideally full-time. Say so if that's not what you want.

How to apply

Answer the screening questions properly. Short and specific beats long and polished - we'd rather have three sentences that show you've done the work than three paragraphs about your commitment to quality. Links to code or live projects are worth more than any adjective you could use about yourself.

Start your proposal with the word "HEADLESS" so we know you read to the end.

title: Laravel + PostGIS Property Data Site with Calculators & Lead Routing
description:
I'm building a UK property information website for homeowners and buyers. I have a complete written specification ready, around 55 pages covering database schema, data sources, page structure, design system and performance requirements. The chosen developer gets the full document. Greenfield build, no legacy code.

WHAT IT DOES

The site combines UK open property data with editorial content and cost tools. Postcode-level sold price data, street sale history and planning application records, all ingested and normalised from free government and open sources. Location-aware cost calculators for home improvements and energy installations. Editorial content in a CMS with location-specific data blocks embedded in articles. User accounts with saved areas and email alerts when new data appears. Enquiry forms routed to third-party partners, plus a paid directory for local businesses. A separate paid toolset for estate agents including image processing and PDF generation. Admin panel for managing all data, content, settings and partners.

There are two AI features, both using the Gemini API through a swappable driver interface. The first runs at ingest and rewrites impenetrable council planning descriptions into one plain-English line, stored once and never regenerated, with hard spend caps and graceful failure so it never blocks the import. The second is a drafting tool for estate agents that generates listing descriptions from structured inputs, with strict prompt constraints for UK advertising compliance. Both are metered per call and logged with token counts and cost. This is API integration work with careful cost control, not model training.

STACK, FIXED AND NOT OPEN TO SUBSTITUTION

Laravel 12, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Livewire and Alpine, Tailwind, Statamic, Filament, Meilisearch, Redis with Horizon, Stripe, Cloudflare, Gemini API, fal.ai.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU

Strong Laravel including queues, scheduled jobs and service-layer architecture. PostGIS and geospatial querying, which is central here rather than incidental. Real experience ingesting and normalising large datasets, since the main sold-price file is around 30 million rows with monthly deltas and there is fuzzy address matching between two separate sources. Server-rendered frontend skills, because there is no SPA framework and the site must work with JavaScript disabled while meeting a hard performance budget of under 2 seconds LCP on data pages. A clean minimalist frontend built from a design direction I provide, not a purchased theme. Technical SEO at scale, meaning programmatic page generation, structured data, sitemaps and meta templating. And an understanding of why a site like this must never create junk database rows, and how to prevent that.

DESIGN AND QUALITY BAR

Clean and fast is the whole point. The visual reference is a modern restrained dashboard aesthetic, neutral, card-based, one accent colour. Mobile-first, WCAG 2.2 AA, tested on real devices.

SCOPE

Single delivery, not phased releases. The spec includes a 20-step dependency order. Roughly half the work sits in the data layer before any user-facing feature becomes meaningful.

WHEN YOU APPLY, PLEASE TELL ME

One, a project where you used PostGIS or handled geospatial data, and what the hard part was. Two, the largest dataset you have imported into a production Laravel app, and how you handled updates. Three, whether you would build fuzzy address matching between two datasets differently to a normalised hash key, and why.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Laravel / AI) — Dashlink
description:
The vision
Dashlink is a no-code platform for building dashboards — marketing, logistics, accounting, finance, you name it. Our integration layer plugs straight into our customers' APIs, turning scattered data into a clean, real-time command center with no glue code.

This is live in production today, serving everyone from lean SMBs to some of the largest enterprises in global payments and logistics. The hard part is done. Now comes the ambitious part: turning a great product into the default platform teams reach for when they need to see their business clearly.

We're hiring one builder to help drive that leap — someone who sees a half-finished thing, says "why not make this exceptional," and then does it.

What you'll do
Own real surface area. Take our Laravel + Livewire apps to the next level — architecture, performance, UX. You'll have the keys, not a permission slip.
Build AI into the product and into how we ship. Equal weight: LLM-powered features for customers, and AI-assisted workflows that let a tiny team move like a big one.
Own the runtime, not just the code. Configure, harden, and maintain the servers; keep queues healthy with Horizon + Redis; run things in Docker; treat security as first-class.
Make architectural calls and live with them. Decide what we build, what we don't, where the boundaries go. Take measured risks, ship, adjust.
Set the bar for a small team. Work alongside 2+ engineers — lead by example, mentor, shape how we hire and grow.
What we're looking for
Non-negotiable:

Deep, demonstrable Laravel expertise — you've built, scaled, and fixed serious systems and can show it. Livewire a strong plus.
You own the whole stack: Horizon + Redis in production · Docker day-to-day · server config, hardening & maintenance · Laravel's security stack (auth, encryption, secrets, dependency hygiene).
Real architecture instinct — you know the difference between clever and maintainable.
Hands-on AI fluency — you actively build and ship with LLMs/agents.
A can-do / why-not wiring — you take ownership, take measured risks, and you finish.
You want a small team — high trust, high autonomy, building something and making it big.
Bonus: no-code/low-code or multi-tenant SaaS · API-integration-heavy products · e-commerce, payments, shipping, or fulfillment · taking a product from "first version" to "platform."

Why it's worth your time
You get to build something real and make it big. The foundation is laid, the customers are serious, the ceiling is high. You bring startup speed; Itembase brings the backing and stability so you're not gambling your runway every quarter.

Remote-first, with EU-hours overlap.
Real ownership of product and architecture.
Senior compensation, discussed openly based on your experience.
Not for you if…
…you want a tightly-scoped lane and a handed-down backlog, you treat AI as someone else's job, you ship code but expect someone else to run the servers, or you need three approvals to change a file.

How to apply
Skip the cover letter. Send us:

Your best Laravel work (repo, project, or a short paragraph).
One thing you shipped with AI recently.
One sentence on something you'd make great that others accepted as "good enough."
We read every one properly, and we move fast.

description:
The vision
Dashlink is a no-code platform for building dashboards — marketing, logistics, accounting, finance, you name it. Our integration layer plugs straight into our customers' APIs, turning scattered data into a clean, real-time command center with no glue code.

This is live in production today, serving everyone from lean SMBs to some of the largest enterprises in global payments and logistics. The hard part is done. Now comes the ambitious part: turning a great product into the default platform teams reach for when they need to see their business clearly.

We're hiring one builder to help drive that leap — someone who sees a half-finished thing, says "why not make this exceptional," and then does it.

What you'll do
Own real surface area. Take our Laravel + Livewire apps to the next level — architecture, performance, UX. You'll have the keys, not a permission slip.
Build AI into the product and into how we ship. Equal weight: LLM-powered features for customers, and AI-assisted workflows that let a tiny team move like a big one.
Own the runtime, not just the code. Configure, harden, and maintain the servers; keep queues healthy with Horizon + Redis; run things in Docker; treat security as first-class.

title: I am looking to build a project management platform
description:
# Full-Stack Developer – Construction Operations Platform

## Project Overview

We are looking for an experienced **full-stack software developer** to help build and refine **ModWorks**, a mobile-first construction operations platform designed around modular construction, logistics, project management, and field execution.

The platform connects construction companies, project administrators, field personnel, manufacturers, subcontractors, and other project participants within a shared system. It is intended to manage the operational lifecycle of a modular construction project—from company and project setup through module transportation, delivery, installation, task management, and reporting.

This is not a simple prototype or CRUD application. We are looking for someone capable of working within a production-oriented architecture and helping develop a polished web and mobile product that can eventually support many companies, projects, users, and field assets.

## Core Platform

ModWorks is organized around several primary entities:

**Companies**

* Create and manage companies
* Company locations
* Company administrators and members
* Service/trade classifications
* Company-level project visibility
* Users may belong to and administer multiple companies

**Projects**

* Create and configure construction projects
* Assign project administrators
* Add participating companies
* Manage project teams and permissions
* Project dashboards
* Project profiles and operational information
* Asset/module tracking
* Tasks and field workflows
* Reports and project history

**Users & Permissions**

* User accounts and invitations
* Company-level and project-level roles
* Administrative permissions
* Users can participate in multiple companies and projects
* Role/ACL-based access control
* Account settings and profile management

The permissions model is important. A user should not require a separate account simply because they perform multiple roles—for example, the same person may be a Project Administrator and also manage company-level operations.

## Task & Workflow Management

The platform includes a project task system supporting:

* Project tasks
* Task statuses and lifecycle stages
* User assignments
* Company assignments
* File attachments
* Module/asset-related tasks
* Operational workflow steps
* Field completion and status tracking
* Automated task creation based on operational events

Tasks need to work effectively on both desktop and mobile devices, with the mobile experience optimized for field personnel.

## Modular Construction & Asset Tracking

A major differentiator of ModWorks is that it is designed specifically around **modular construction logistics**.

Individual building modules/assets can be tracked through their lifecycle, including statuses such as:

**Manufacturer → In Transit → Storage → Project Site → Set/Installed**

The platform integrates with physical GPS/IoT tracking devices installed on modules.

Geofencing and tracker events can automatically update module status and trigger downstream workflows.

For example:

* A module leaving the manufacturer's geofence can automatically become **In Transit**.
* Arrival at a storage facility can change its status to **At Storage**.
* Arrival at the construction project can change it to **Arrived on Site**.
* Movement into the building/set-area geofence can help identify that the module has been **Set/Installed**.
* These events can generate tasks, notifications, timestamps, and project history.

Manual overrides must also be supported for field conditions where automated tracking is not sufficient.

The system should ultimately be capable of supporting **hundreds to thousands of GPS-tracked assets** across multiple projects.

## Reporting

The platform includes operational reporting capabilities such as:

* Daily project reports
* Module/asset status
* Task completion
* Project activity
* Company/team participation
* Automated report generation
* Scheduled email distribution
* Historical reporting

Reporting should be designed so additional report types can be added as the platform grows.

## Web & Mobile Applications

The system consists of both a responsive web application and a native/mobile application.

The current preferred architecture is:

### Web

* Next.js
* React
* TypeScript
* Tailwind CSS
* shadcn/ui / Radix-based components
* TanStack Query
* Zustand where appropriate

### Mobile

* React Native
* Expo / Expo Router
* TypeScript
* Shared API/types where practical

### Backend

* NestJS / Node.js
* TypeScript
* REST APIs
* PostgreSQL
* Shared Zod schemas/types
* Structured service architecture

The project is structured as a **TypeScript monorepo**, with shared packages for types, API clients, themes, icons, and utilities.

## AWS Infrastructure

The application is intended to operate primarily within AWS.

Experience with services such as the following is valuable:

* ECS / Fargate
* RDS or Aurora PostgreSQL
* S3
* CloudFront
* Route 53
* SES
* CloudWatch
* Secrets Manager
* IAM
* Application Load Balancers
* VPC/networking
* CI/CD deployment into AWS

We want infrastructure that is reliable and production-ready without introducing unnecessary complexity or cost.

## External Integrations

The system also needs to support integrations with external services, particularly GPS/IoT providers.

Current asset tracking utilizes **Jimi IoT / Concox GPS devices**, with ModWorks consuming tracker/geofence events through provider APIs.

The architecture should make it possible to support additional hardware providers in the future without rewriting the core asset-tracking system.

## UI/UX Expectations

We are looking for more than someone who can simply make functionality work.

The platform needs a clean, modern interface appropriate for a professional construction SaaS product.

Important UX considerations include:

* Mobile-first field workflows
* Fast project navigation
* Large datasets without cumbersome pagination
* Virtualized tables where appropriate
* Clear status indicators
* Consistent design system
* Responsive layouts
* Efficient workflows requiring as few interactions as practical
* Good loading, empty, success, and error states
* Interfaces usable by both technically sophisticated administrators and field personnel

## What We're Looking For

The ideal developer is comfortable owning features from database through UI and has strong experience with:

* TypeScript
* React
* Next.js
* React Native / Expo
* Node.js / NestJS
* PostgreSQL
* REST API design
* AWS
* Authentication and authorization
* Multi-tenant SaaS architecture
* Responsive/mobile-first UI
* Git/GitHub workflows
* Automated testing
* Production deployments

Experience with **construction technology, logistics, IoT/GPS systems, mapping/geofencing, or field-service applications** would be particularly valuable.

## Engineering Expectations

We want someone who thinks beyond individual tickets.

You should be comfortable:

* Understanding an existing codebase before making major changes
* Identifying architectural problems instead of building around them
* Keeping web, mobile, API, and shared packages consistent
* Writing maintainable and strongly typed code
* Creating reusable components rather than duplicating functionality
* Handling edge cases and failure states
* Reviewing your own implementation before submitting work
* Writing tests for critical business logic
* Working through GitHub pull requests
* Communicating assumptions and technical tradeoffs
* Testing complete user flows rather than only individual components

AI-assisted development tools such as **Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar agentic development tools** are welcome. We care about the quality, maintainability, and correctness of the resulting code—not whether AI was used to accelerate development.

## Initial Work

Initial work will involve reviewing the existing ModWorks platform and codebase, understanding the architecture and business workflows, and then working through remaining functionality, QA/QC findings, UI improvements, and production readiness.

A successful developer may continue working with us as ModWorks expands into additional areas of construction operations, logistics automation, IoT asset management, and project intelligence.

## When Applying

Please include:

1. Examples of production applications you have personally built or substantially contributed to.
2. Your experience with Next.js, React Native/Expo, NestJS, PostgreSQL, and AWS.
3. Any experience building multi-tenant SaaS applications.
4. Any experience with IoT, GPS tracking, geofencing, logistics, construction, or field-service applications.
5. Your experience working with existing production codebases.
6. Your preferred development and Git/PR workflow.
7. How you use AI-assisted development tools, if applicable.
8. Your availability and preferred working hours/time zone.

Please **do not send a generic agency proposal**. We are particularly interested in developers who can understand a complex business workflow, independently reason through problems, and take ownership of delivering production-quality features.

AI-Powered Quotation Automation System for Engineering Company

We are an engineering company specializing in industrial buildings and technical solutions (www.ct-technologies.dk). We are looking for an experienced AI developer to build an intelligent quotation generation system that can reduce the time spent preparing customer quotations while improving consistency and quality.

The system should be able to generate high-quality quotation drafts based on historical quotations, standard material price lists, and project requirements.

Microsoft Copilot Agents
Claude-based solutions
OpenAI / ChatGPT-based solutions
Custom AI applications
Hybrid solutions combining AI and traditional software development.


Today, our quotations are prepared manually by reviewing previous projects and selecting suitable products and materials.

We would like to automate much of this process by leveraging our existing quotation database and product knowledge.

The goal is for the system to:

- Analyze customer requirements.
- Identify similar historical quotations/projects.
- Suggest appropriate products and materials.
- Generate a professional quotation draft including price, payment terms, etc. 
- Automatically create persuasive sales text explaining why the recommended solution is suitable for the customer's specific needs.

It should be easy  to use and available for our sales people to be able to do first draft quotations for our customers while they have customer meetings. 

The solution should be able to utilize:

- Historical quotations (our existing quotation database, which is quite big)
- Material and product price lists
- Product specifications and technical documentation
- Business rules and engineering requirements

If the AI selects a specific product (e.g. sandwich panel), it should explain why, such as:

Fire safety performance
Thermal insulation performance
Corrosion resistance
Durability
Cost effectiveness
Compliance with relevant standards

The generated text should sound professional and sales-oriented rather than generic AI output.

User Experience

Preferred workflow:

- User (sales managers and quotation manager) enters project details and customer requirements.
- AI System searches historical projects/quotations and our standard price lists.
- AI Recommends solution.
- AI Generates quotation draft.
- User reviews and edits.
- Final quotation is exported to Word/PDF.

Please include:

- Similar projects you have built.
- Recommended technical architecture.
- Expected approach for using historical quotations and price lists.
- Which AI platform you would recommend and why.
- Estimated development phases and total price
- How much maintenance is needed afterwards and how you will support that.

**Companies**

* Create and manage companies
* Company locations
* Company administrators and members
* Service/trade classifications
* Company-level project visibility
* Users may belong to and administer multiple companies

**Projects**

* Create and configure construction projects
* Assign project administrators
* Add participating companies
* Manage project teams and permissions
* Project dashboards
* Project profiles and operational information
* Asset/module tracking
* Tasks and field workflows
* Reports and project history

**Users & Permissions**

* User accounts and invitations
* Company-level and project-level roles
* Administrative permissions
* Users can participate in multiple companies and projects
* Role/ACL-based access control
* Account settings and profile management

The permissions model is important. A user should not require a separate account simply because they perform multiple roles—for example, the same person may be a Project Administrator and also manage company-level operations.

## Task & Workflow Management

The platform includes a project task system supporting:

* Project tasks
* Task statuses and lifecycle stages
* User assignments
* Company assignments
* File attachments
* Module/asset-related tasks
* Operational workflow steps
* Field completion and status tracking
* Automated task creation based on operational events

Tasks need to work effectively on both desktop and mobile devices, with the mobile experience optimized for field personnel.

## Modular Construction & Asset Tracking

A major differentiator of ModWorks is that it is designed specifically around **modular construction logistics**.

Individual building modules/assets can be tracked through their lifecycle, including statuses such as:

**Manufacturer → In Transit → Storage → Project Site → Set/Installed**

The platform integrates with physical GPS/IoT tracking devices installed on modules.

Geofencing and tracker events can automatically update module status and trigger downstream workflows.

For example:

* A module leaving the manufacturer's geofence can automatically become **In Transit**.
* Arrival at a storage facility can change its status to **At Storage**.
* Arrival at the construction project can change it to **Arrived on Site**.
* Movement into the building/set-area geofence can help identify that the module has been **Set/Installed**.
* These events can generate tasks, notifications, timestamps, and project history.

Manual overrides must also be supported for field conditions where automated tracking is not sufficient.

The system should ultimately be capable of supporting **hundreds to thousands of GPS-tracked assets** across multiple projects.

## Reporting

The platform includes operational reporting capabilities such as:

* Daily project reports
* Module/asset status
* Task completion
* Project activity
* Company/team participation
* Automated report generation
* Scheduled email distribution
* Historical reporting

Reporting should be designed so additional report types can be added as the platform grows.

## Web & Mobile Applications

The system consists of both a responsive web application and a native/mobile application.

The current preferred architecture is:

### Web

* Next.js
* React
* TypeScript
* Tailwind CSS
* shadcn/ui / Radix-based components
* TanStack Query
* Zustand where appropriate

### Mobile

* React Native
* Expo / Expo Router
* TypeScript
* Shared API/types where practical

### Backend

* NestJS / Node.js
* TypeScript
* REST APIs
* PostgreSQL
* Shared Zod schemas/types
* Structured service architecture

The project is structured as a **TypeScript monorepo**, with shared packages for types, API clients, themes, icons, and utilities.

## AWS Infrastructure

The application is intended to operate primarily within AWS.

Experience with services such as the following is valuable:

* ECS / Fargate
* RDS or Aurora PostgreSQL
* S3
* CloudFront
* Route 53
* SES
* CloudWatch
* Secrets Manager
* IAM
* Application Load Balancers
* VPC/networking
* CI/CD deployment into AWS

We want infrastructure that is reliable and production-ready without introducing unnecessary complexity or cost.

## External Integrations

The system also needs to support integrations with external services, particularly GPS/IoT providers.

Current asset tracking utilizes **Jimi IoT / Concox GPS devices**, with ModWorks consuming tracker/geofence events through provider APIs.

The architecture should make it possible to support additional hardware providers in the future without rewriting the core asset-tracking system.

## UI/UX Expectations

We are looking for more than someone who can simply make functionality work.

The platform needs a clean, modern interface appropriate for a professional construction SaaS product.

Important UX considerations include:

* Mobile-first field workflows
* Fast project navigation
* Large datasets without cumbersome pagination
* Virtualized tables where appropriate
* Clear status indicators
* Consistent design system
* Responsive layouts
* Efficient workflows requiring as few interactions as practical
* Good loading, empty, success, and error states
* Interfaces usable by both technically sophisticated administrators and field personnel

## What We're Looking For

The ideal developer is comfortable owning features from database through UI and has strong experience with:

* TypeScript
* React
* Next.js
* React Native / Expo
* Node.js / NestJS
* PostgreSQL
* REST API design
* AWS
* Authentication and authorization
* Multi-tenant SaaS architecture
* Responsive/mobile-first UI
* Git/GitHub workflows
* Automated testing
* Production deployments

Experience with **construction technology, logistics, IoT/GPS systems, mapping/geofencing, or field-service applications** would be particularly valuable.

## Engineering Expectations

We want someone who thinks beyond individual tickets.

You should be comfortable:

* Understanding an existing codebase before making major changes
* Identifying architectural problems instead of building around them
* Keeping web, mobile, API, and shared packages consistent
* Writing maintainable and strongly typed code
* Creating reusable components rather than duplicating functionality
* Handling edge cases and failure states
* Reviewing your own implementation before submitting work
* Writing tests for critical business logic
* Working through GitHub pull requests
* Communicating assumptions and technical tradeoffs
* Testing complete user flows rather than only individual components

AI-assisted development tools such as **Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar agentic development tools** are welcome. We care about the quality, maintainability, and correctness of the resulting code—not whether AI was used to accelerate development.

## Initial Work

Initial work will involve reviewing the existing ModWorks platform and codebase, understanding the architecture and business workflows, and then working through remaining functionality, QA/QC findings, UI improvements, and production readiness.

A successful developer may continue working with us as ModWorks expands into additional areas of construction operations, logistics automation, IoT asset management, and project intelligence.

## When Applying

Please include:

1. Examples of production applications you have personally built or substantially contributed to.
2. Your experience with Next.js, React Native/Expo, NestJS, PostgreSQL, and AWS.
3. Any experience building multi-tenant SaaS applications.
4. Any experience with IoT, GPS tracking, geofencing, logistics, construction, or field-service applications.
5. Your experience working with existing production codebases.
6. Your preferred development and Git/PR workflow.
7. How you use AI-assisted development tools, if applicable.
8. Your availability and preferred working hours/time zone.

Please **do not send a generic agency proposal**. We are particularly interested in developers who can understand a complex business workflow, independently reason through problems, and take ownership of delivering production-quality features.

title: AI Quotation generator
description:
AI-Powered Quotation Automation System for Engineering Company

We are an engineering company specializing in industrial buildings and technical solutions (www.ct-technologies.dk). We are looking for an experienced AI developer to build an intelligent quotation generation system that can reduce the time spent preparing customer quotations while improving consistency and quality.

The system should be able to generate high-quality quotation drafts based on historical quotations, standard material price lists, and project requirements.

We are open to different technology approaches, including:

Microsoft Copilot Agents
Claude-based solutions
OpenAI / ChatGPT-based solutions
Custom AI applications
Hybrid solutions combining AI and traditional software development.


Today, our quotations are prepared manually by reviewing previous projects and selecting suitable products and materials.

We would like to automate much of this process by leveraging our existing quotation database and product knowledge.

The goal is for the system to:

- Analyze customer requirements.
- Identify similar historical quotations/projects.
- Suggest appropriate products and materials.
- Generate a professional quotation draft including price, payment terms, etc. 
- Automatically create persuasive sales text explaining why the recommended solution is suitable for the customer's specific needs.

It should be easy  to use and available for our sales people to be able to do first draft quotations for our customers while they have customer meetings. 

The solution should be able to utilize:

- Historical quotations (our existing quotation database, which is quite big)
- Material and product price lists
- Product specifications and technical documentation
- Business rules and engineering requirements

If the AI selects a specific product (e.g. sandwich panel), it should explain why, such as:

Fire safety performance
Thermal insulation performance
Corrosion resistance
Durability
Cost effectiveness
Compliance with relevant standards

The generated text should sound professional and sales-oriented rather than generic AI output.

User Experience

Preferred workflow:

- User (sales managers and quotation manager) enters project details and customer requirements.
- AI System searches historical projects/quotations and our standard price lists.
- AI Recommends solution.
- AI Generates quotation draft.
- User reviews and edits.
- Final quotation is exported to Word/PDF.

Please include:

- Similar projects you have built.
- Recommended technical architecture.
- Expected approach for using historical quotations and price lists.
- Which AI platform you would recommend and why.
- Estimated development phases and total price
- How much maintenance is needed afterwards and how you will support that.

title: Full-Stack Laravel Developer Needed – Yoti Age Verification + Front-End/UI
description:
We are looking for an experienced **Full-Stack Laravel Developer** to assist with an existing, live website, with our immediate priority being the completion and troubleshooting of our **Yoti age verification integration**.

Our website is already built and operational. We are not looking for someone to rebuild the site. We need an experienced developer who can work within our existing Laravel codebase, understand what has already been implemented, and help us finish and improve specific areas of the site.

### Immediate Priority: Yoti Age Verification

We already have a **Yoti business account** and have begun implementing age verification. We need someone who can review the existing implementation and help us properly complete the integration.

Ideally, you have direct experience with:

* Laravel / PHP
* Yoti Age Verification or Yoti APIs/SDKs
* API integrations and webhooks
* Age-gating / age-assurance systems
* Authentication, sessions, and user flows
* Troubleshooting existing third-party integrations

**Previous Yoti experience would be a major plus**, but we are open to a strong Laravel developer with significant third-party API integration experience.

### Additional Development

Although age verification is our immediate need, we would ideally like to find someone we can continue working with as our website grows.

Additional skills we're looking for include:

* Strong full-stack Laravel/PHP development
* Front-end development
* UI/UX experience
* Responsive/mobile design
* HTML, CSS and JavaScript
* Database/backend troubleshooting
* Payment and third-party API integrations
* Improving existing features and user flows
* Ability to work safely within an established production website

This is an **adult-oriented website**, so you must be 18+ and comfortable working with a legal adult-content business and website.

### When Applying

Please tell us:

1. How many years of Laravel/PHP experience you have.
2. Whether you've integrated **Yoti** before. If yes, please describe what you implemented.
3. What other identity, age-verification, KYC, or similar API integrations you've worked with.
4. Your experience with front-end/UI development.
5. Whether you're comfortable working with an adult-oriented website.
6. Your current availability and hourly rate.

We are looking for someone who communicates well, can explain technical issues in understandable terms, and is comfortable reviewing and improving an existing codebase rather than starting from scratch.

There is potential for **ongoing development work** for the right person.

title: Agent for Portfolio Monitoring Automation
description:
Assist me in creating a portfolio monitoring agent, that identifies and aggregates portfolios of investors in one consolidated database and subsequently sends out a weekly mail with changes in the investor portfolios or on significant news in the respective portfolio company. 

Flow: 
Weekly Mail - Triggered by all (a) news in the portfolios of the selected investors and (b) news in the respective portfolio company - if no news available then simply mail with update no news.

The investor database should be build by simply submitting a name to a chat interface on a website. i.e. copying in 20 names of investors. The portfolio companies of set investors should then be scraped and mapped automatically from the respective investor websites. Further information on the respective portfolio company should be drawn from its website.

Then on a weekly basis an update is send with the news. Relevant news are: funding rounds, M&A, leadership changes, layoffs, general press. 

Further one should be able to intelligently research the database of investors. I.e. looking for an investor with XYZ portfolio company. 

Aim is to build a very MVP version first to align on the draft and then build a final version that is presentable / usable by a team. 

The final version is a chat interface a la chat GPT, where i can submit new investors and inquire about the database. The database will most likely have approx 500-1000 investors, with each between 10-20 portfolio firms (i.e. around 10k companies need to be reviewed every week).

I.e. one should be able to answer the following question: Provide an overview of industries and their respective niches that have gained particular high investor interest in the USA in recent times (last 24 months).

If this is something for you, i’d be glad to quickly get to know oneanother and discuss the following:
- Project timing
- Expected complexities
- Suggested tools, potential downside of tools
- Estimated cost, tool cost, operating cost

Please direct your proposal to Lemon. Though i encourage AI simply write 2-3 sentence about you, why you are the optimal fit for the project and potentially any questions you may have. Ideally looking for a German native speaker in the western time zone.

title: Full-Stack / Azure Engineer — Review AI Agent Platform + Build Dashboards & UI
description:
Dear Freelancers, 

We're a European real estate investment and development firm building an internal AI agent platform on a Microsoft 365 / Azure stack. The core retrieval and agent logic is already in place and we're now looking for an experienced engineer to (1) conduct an independent architecture and security review of the existing setup, and (2) design and build a set of dashboards plus a polished user interface on top of it.

The existing setup (high level)

Multi-agent fleet architecture (business-level and project-level agents), where "project" is a runtime parameter rather than hard-coded per agent
Azure OpenAI for generation; SharePoint / Microsoft Graph as the retrieval and permissions source of truth
Azure Functions back-end with an on-behalf-of (OBO) identity model and a web-app front-end
Entra ID for authentication, security groups, and access control
Document ingestion with a managed metadata layer (tagging, sensitivity classification, status tracking)

What we need

Independent review — assess the current architecture, retrieval approach, identity/permission model, and security posture. Deliver a written findings report with prioritized recommendations (correctness, security, performance, maintainability).
Dashboards — build operational dashboards covering things like agent/fleet status, evaluation results, ingestion and onboarding progress across multiple data rooms, document counts, and tagging/metadata coverage.
User interface — design and implement a clean, responsive front-end for end users to query the agents and view results with source citations, respecting the existing OBO permission model (users only see what they're entitled to see).

Required skills

Strong React / TypeScript, with real data-visualization / dashboard experience
Azure: Functions, App Service, Azure OpenAI, Key Vault / managed identity
Microsoft Graph API and SharePoint integration
Entra ID authentication (MSAL, OBO / delegated flows)
Experience with LLM / RAG applications
Security-conscious mindset around access control and data handling

Nice to have

Experience with regulated or confidentiality-sensitive environments
German language (working proficiency) — not required but a plus
Familiarity with evaluation/observability for LLM systems

Deliverables

Architecture & security review document with prioritized findings
Working dashboard(s) deployed to our environment
User-facing query UI, documented and handed over with source code

title: Senior AI and Integration Engineer for a multi-system business build (Australia, long-term)
description:
We're building an AI operating layer for an established Australian trades and services business, and we're looking for an experienced engineer to build it.

The core of the work is connecting the software the business already runs (HubSpot, ServiceM8, Xero, WhatsApp Business and a few others) so that one job flows through all of them as a single record, instead of being re-entered by hand in each system. On top of that sits a knowledge base the tools search to answer technical questions, with strict rules: every answer names its source, and if the tool isn't certain it hands over to a qualified person rather than guessing.

This is a real, multi-month build working with sensitive business data. It is not a quick automation job. It will be delivered piece by piece, with each part going live as it's finished. The code lives in a repository we own, the data stays in Australia, and there's a security review before any real data is touched.

What you'd be doing:

- Connecting several live business systems into one reliable data layer, including two systems that are mid-migration
- Building a searchable knowledge base that cites its sources and safely handles "I don't know"
- Building AI-assisted tools on top of that layer, such as design checks, a field tool, a finance layer and a dashboard
- Setting up testing, logging and cost tracking so the system is dependable and its running cost is known per job

Who we're looking for:

- Strong backend engineering (for example Python or TypeScript, databases, cloud hosting)
- Real experience integrating live business systems through their APIs (please name which ones)
- Experience building production AI or retrieval systems with grounding and citations, not just chatbots or demos
- Awareness of data privacy and security, ideally with Australian data residency in mind
- A track record of finishing substantial, multi-month builds
- Clear, responsive communication, as you'll work closely with us, not directly with the end client

Nice to have:

- Direct experience with HubSpot, ServiceM8, Xero or the WhatsApp Business API
- A habit of recommending an alternative, simpler or cheaper approach when one exists

To apply:

- A confidentiality agreement is signed before the full scope is shared
- Please share examples of live systems you've built, whether integrations, AI retrieval work, or both
- Answer the two screening questions

- Project timing

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
## The role

We are looking for a strong, versatile senior software engineer to help turn a substantial body of existing software, prototypes, integrations, and internal tools into reliable production systems.

This is fundamentally a software-engineering role. We care most about whether you can understand an unfamiliar codebase, make sound architectural decisions, write maintainable code, debug difficult problems, ship complete systems, and keep those systems dependable after launch.

The work spans backend and full-stack development, data systems, APIs and third-party integrations, workflow automation, communication platforms, cloud infrastructure, security, testing, observability, and AI-enabled applications. Some projects involve persistent agents, browser or desktop automation, media pipelines, and organizational knowledge systems. You do not need to be a specialist in every area, but you should be able to take broad technical ownership and become effective quickly in unfamiliar parts of the stack.

We use AI coding agents extensively. You will be expected to use them well, just as you would be expected to use version control, tests, debuggers, documentation, and observability tools well. Agent fluency matters, but it is not a substitute for engineering ability. We are not hiring a prompt engineer whose code must be rescued by someone else.

## Current technical environment

The current estate is polyglot. Python and TypeScript are the dominant application languages, while Rust appears in the lower-level agent, desktop, installer, terminal, and computer-control layers. The exact architecture will continue to evolve, but an engineer joining today should expect to work with:

- **Python 3.10/3.11+:** FastAPI, Starlette, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Psycopg, LangGraph, OpenAI and other model APIs, Slack and Discord SDKs, JSON Schema, PyYAML, pytest, `uv`, Hatch, and setuptools.
- **TypeScript and JavaScript on modern Node.js:** Next.js, React, Vite, Express, Electron, Tailwind CSS, Zod, Drizzle ORM, Supabase, Playwright, Vitest, `pnpm`, and `npm`.
- **Rust:** Cargo workspaces and asynchronous systems built with Tokio, Serde, Reqwest, Tauri, tracing, and cross-platform process or terminal primitives.
- **Data and protocols:** PostgreSQL, SQLite, structured JSON/YAML contracts, REST APIs, webhooks, append-only event and message records, idempotent workers, queues, authentication, permissions, and audit trails.
- **Agent and automation interfaces:** tool calling, MCP and related agent protocols, persistent task state, retrieval, evaluations, coding-agent adapters, browser automation, desktop control, and human approval workflows.
- **Infrastructure and delivery:** Docker and Compose, Linux services, cloud-hosted APIs, Vercel-style web deployment, CI/CD, secrets management, logging, metrics, traces, backups, and incident recovery.
- **Native and cross-platform surfaces:** Electron and Tauri desktop applications, PTYs and terminal interfaces, browser automation, and a smaller Swift/AppKit/ScreenCaptureKit macOS helper.

This is not a requirement to have used every named library. It is a requirement to be comfortable moving through a mixed Python, TypeScript, and Rust system and to understand the engineering concepts underneath the frameworks.

## What you will own

### Build and maintain production software

- Design, implement, test, deploy, and operate software across backend services, internal tools, and full-stack applications.
- Take features and systems from an approved requirement through implementation, integration, release, monitoring, and maintenance.
- Read and improve existing code before proposing a rewrite.
- Make pragmatic architectural and build-versus-integrate decisions based on reliability, security, cost, and maintainability.
- Define clear interfaces, schemas, failure behavior, and migration paths.
- Keep codebases understandable and leave systems in a condition that another engineer can safely continue.

### Build integrations and workflow infrastructure

- Build and maintain integrations with communication platforms, repositories, email, cloud services, publishing systems, analytics tools, CRMs, and other approved external services.
- Extend shared workflows across platforms such as Slack and Discord while preserving consistent identity, permissions, task state, and audit history.
- Design reliable webhook handlers, background jobs, queues, scheduled work, retries, idempotency, and recovery behavior.
- Build operator interfaces for reviewing work, resolving exceptions, approving actions, and understanding system state.
- Use APIs where practical and controlled browser, desktop, or mobile automation when an adequate API is unavailable.
- Design automations to tolerate interface changes, expired sessions, partial failures, duplicate events, and rate limits.

### Build data and organizational knowledge systems

- Ingest authorized communications and records from approved sources such as Slack, Discord, email, documents, meetings, and repositories.
- Build durable storage, retrieval, search, and briefing systems with appropriate provenance and access control.
- Preserve who said what, when it was said, and where it came from; distinguish a direct statement from an automated inference or summary.
- Support corrections, superseded information, retention rules, deletion, and audit requirements.
- Build relationship and communication workflows that can track interaction history, open loops, drafts, approvals, and reminders.
- Prevent private information from leaking between projects, users, agents, or public outputs.

### Build and integrate AI-enabled systems

- Implement applications and workflows that use language models, coding agents, research agents, computer-use agents, retrieval, tool calling, and structured outputs.
- Connect agents to real systems through explicit, testable interfaces rather than fragile prompt-only behavior.
- Design durable task state, checkpoints, queues, retries, timeouts, escalation, and recovery for long-running agent work.
- Build evaluations and regression tests for nondeterministic components.
- Instrument agent runs so engineers can inspect inputs, tool use, costs, failures, outputs, and approval state.
- Establish clear boundaries between observing, recommending, drafting, staging, and taking an authorized external action.
- Prevent one model's confidence or self-assessment from being treated as proof that a result is correct.

### Build secure automation and account access

- Implement least-privilege access, secret management, environment isolation, audit logging, revocation, and approval gates.
- Protect systems that can read private data, execute code, operate browsers, or act through external accounts.
- Account for prompt injection, malicious external content, confused-deputy behavior, credential exposure, and cross-project data leakage.
- Separate development, staging, and production access and make consequential actions attributable.
- Work with the relevant security owner on threat modeling, design review, incident response, and remediation.
- Treat browser and desktop control as high-permission production infrastructure, not a demo shortcut.

### Own engineering quality and operations

- Write meaningful unit, integration, end-to-end, security, and regression tests.
- Build deployment automation and maintain appropriate environments, backups, recovery procedures, and operational runbooks.
- Instrument services with useful logs, metrics, traces, alerts, cost visibility, and failure diagnostics.
- Investigate production problems, identify root causes, and make the system more resilient afterward.
- Review human- and agent-generated code for correctness, security, dependency risk, brittle assumptions, and unnecessary complexity.
- Distinguish proposed, mocked, locally demonstrated, staging-qualified, and production behavior.
- Require reproducible evidence before declaring technical work complete.

### Improve how engineering work gets done

- Work with product managers to turn approved requirements and acceptance criteria into sound technical plans.
- Surface unclear requirements, hidden dependencies, security concerns, and technically risky assumptions early.
- Break larger implementations into work that engineers and agents can execute without losing architectural coherence.
- Keep technical decisions, active work, blockers, and release evidence visible to the team.
- Turn recurring implementation problems into reusable libraries, tests, automation, documentation, or engineering standards.
- Help a small team operate multiple systems without accumulating an unmanageable collection of one-off frameworks.

## How we use AI agents

We expect senior engineers here to use agents as a normal part of their engineering practice. Depending on the task, that may include coding agents, research agents, browser agents, custom automations, local models, orchestration tools, or parallel development workflows.

Strong use of agents might involve:

- giving an agent the relevant code, architecture, constraints, and definition of done;
- delegating bounded implementation, investigation, test-writing, migration, or documentation work;
- coordinating parallel work without conflicting changes or duplicated systems;
- preserving task state and decisions outside a private chat transcript;
- reviewing diffs, tests, traces, and running behavior rather than trusting an agent's summary;
- detecting when an agent is confidently wrong, stuck, missing context, or exceeding its authority; and
- improving the workflow after a failed or low-quality run.

You do not need to use a particular agent product or framework. We do want to understand which tools you use, what you trust them to do, how you verify their work, and where you keep a human in the loop.

The engineer remains accountable for the architecture, code, security, testing, and production result. “The agent wrote it” is never an explanation for poor engineering.

## Scope boundaries

This role does **not** own:

- product strategy, customer discovery, market selection, or roadmap prioritization;
- deciding which products or features the company should pursue;
- writing product requirements or serving as the product manager;
- trading strategy, investment signals, market calls, portfolio management, or trade execution;
- custody of funds or speculative financial activity;
- token economics, reward design, financial promises, or other economic policy; or
- final marketing, editorial, legal, or public-communications decisions.

You may implement approved software used by product, operations, content, community, or other teams. That does not transfer those teams' decision rights to engineering.

You are expected to challenge requirements that are technically incoherent, unsafe, or unverifiable and to propose better implementation options. The relevant product or functional owner remains responsible for the underlying business decision.

## Initial priorities

The exact sequence will be set with the product managers and engineering lead, but early work is likely to include:

- Audit relevant repositories, services, deployments, integrations, and unfinished implementations to determine what actually works.
- Establish a current technical map that distinguishes production systems, prototypes, stale assumptions, and missing infrastructure.
- Extend a shared organizational workflow across multiple communication platforms.
- Build a recurring, permission-aware communication-ingestion and retrieval pipeline with clear provenance.
- Improve the reliability and observability of long-running agent and automation workflows.
- Establish security controls for agents, external accounts, credentials, browser or desktop sessions, and sensitive communications.
- Build one approval-gated communication or content workflow from authorized source material through exact-artifact review and preview output.
- Consolidate common identity, event, permission, audit, and integration primitives where they are currently duplicated.
- Improve automated testing, deployment evidence, monitoring, and recovery for existing systems.

## What success looks like

- Develop an evidence-based understanding of the relevant systems and their current production state.
- Become productive in the existing stack without requiring a clean-room rewrite.
- Take ownership of a bounded technical milestone and ship a working, tested result.
- Repair or qualify at least one important existing workflow.
- Identify the highest-priority reliability, security, and maintainability risks and propose a practical sequence for addressing them.
- Establish an effective working pattern with the product managers, other engineers, QA, and the agents you use.
- Ship and operate at least one substantial cross-system workflow.
- Improve the visibility of system state, failures, approvals, costs, and outcomes.
- Establish reusable patterns for integrations, security, testing, observability, deployment, and recovery.
- Demonstrate that a second workflow can reuse those patterns with materially less engineering effort.
- Reduce the founder and engineering lead intervention required to keep technical work moving.
- Leave behind production evidence: deployed behavior, tests, traces, runbooks, and a clear maintenance path.

## What we are looking for

You are likely a strong fit if:

- You have substantial professional software-engineering experience and have personally shipped and operated production systems.
- You have production-level proficiency in both **Python** and **TypeScript/JavaScript**, including typed interfaces, dependency management, testing, debugging, and deployment.
- You have working proficiency in **Rust**: you can read an unfamiliar crate, trace ownership and async behavior, diagnose compiler or runtime failures, make a bounded production change, and verify it with tests. Deep Rust specialization is welcome but not required.
- You have built backend services using FastAPI, Starlette, Express, or a comparable framework and understand API design, authentication, validation, background work, and failure handling.
- You have built modern web applications using React and a framework such as Next.js or Vite, and can work productively across browser code, server code, and typed API boundaries.
- You can design and operate systems using PostgreSQL or SQLite, including schemas, migrations, transactions, indexing, concurrency, retention, and recovery.
- You understand APIs, webhooks, authentication, queues, background jobs, idempotency, distributed failure modes, cloud deployment, and observability.
- You are comfortable with Docker, Linux development and operations, CI/CD, secrets management, and at least one production cloud or application-hosting environment.
- You can write and maintain unit, integration, and end-to-end tests using tools such as pytest, Vitest, and Playwright or their equivalents.
- You can work across backend, infrastructure, integrations, and enough frontend code to own a result end to end.
- You write clear, maintainable code and exercise sound judgment about abstractions, dependencies, performance, and operational complexity.
- You can diagnose difficult problems using code, logs, metrics, traces, tests, and production evidence.
- You understand security fundamentals, especially around credentials, private data, access boundaries, and high-permission automation.
- You can take an ambiguous technical problem, investigate it, propose a bounded plan, and close the loop without constant supervision.
- You communicate clearly in writing and leave useful technical plans, decision records, documentation, runbooks, and postmortems.
- You use AI coding or engineering agents productively and review their work with the same rigor you would apply to a human contributor's work.
- You care more about dependable outcomes than impressive demos, framework novelty, or raw lines of generated code.

Useful but not required experience includes:

- FastAPI, Starlette, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Psycopg, LangGraph, and modern Python packaging with `uv`;
- Next.js, React, Vite, Express, Electron, Tailwind, Zod, Drizzle, Supabase, and modern Node.js tooling;
- Tokio, Serde, Reqwest, Tauri, terminal or PTY programming, and structured tracing in Rust;
- LLM applications, multi-agent systems, MCP, durable workflows, or event-driven orchestration;
- Slack Bolt/SDK, Discord.py, email, publishing, messaging, analytics, or CRM integrations;
- browser automation, computer use, desktop applications, mobile testing, or virtualized devices;
- event sourcing, knowledge graphs, provenance systems, search, or temporal data models;
- security engineering for multi-tenant or high-permission systems;
- developer tools, internal platforms, and shared-service infrastructure;
- media generation, deterministic rendering, or content-operation pipelines; and
- evaluating or observing nondeterministic software;
- Swift, AppKit, ScreenCaptureKit, macOS permissions, signing, or notarization; or
- Azure, AWS, Vercel, Railway, GitHub Actions, or comparable deployment systems.

You do not need experience in all of these areas. Strong general engineering ability, production judgment, and the capacity to learn matter more than matching every keyword.

## This role is probably not for you if

- Your experience is primarily prototypes, hackathons, or model demos that somebody else productionized.
- You prefer narrowly assigned tickets and do not want responsibility for integration, deployment, diagnosis, or maintenance.
- You want to rewrite unfamiliar systems before understanding why they exist.
- You consider a merged pull request sufficient evidence that a feature works.
- You treat testing, security, observability, or documentation as someone else's job.
- You use AI-generated code that you cannot explain, debug, or maintain.
- You optimize for the number of agents, models, or frameworks involved rather than the quality of the resulting system.
- You want to own product strategy or trading activity rather than implement approved technical work.

## Scope and decision rights

You will have broad authority to investigate technical systems, propose architecture, implement approved work, improve engineering workflows, delegate scoped tasks to agents, and make reversible technical decisions within agreed boundaries.

Production releases, material infrastructure spending, access to sensitive communications, new third-party accounts, and consequential external actions require the applicable approval. Delegating an action to an agent does not expand your authority.

The founder retains final authority over company direction, capital allocation, and material risk. Product, security, QA, legal, marketing, and operations owners retain their respective decision and approval gates.

## How to apply

Please send:

1. A short explanation of why this senior engineering role fits you.
2. Two examples of production software or infrastructure you personally shipped and operated. Explain the system, your exact contribution, the hardest technical tradeoff, and what happened after launch.
3. A link to code or a technically detailed artifact you produced. Private work may be described or demonstrated in redacted form.
4. A description of a difficult production incident or engineering failure you helped resolve. How did you diagnose it, what was the root cause, and what changed afterward?
5. A short technical walkthrough of a system you designed or substantially improved: its architecture, data model, important failure modes, security boundaries, and how you knew it was operating correctly.
6. A concise account of your experience with Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Rust. Name the frameworks and production systems you used, identify your strongest and weakest of the three, and explain one meaningful contribution you made in each language.
7. A description of the AI agents you currently use for engineering. Name the products, coding agents, models, frameworks, custom tools, or automations where possible. Walk through one real task: what you delegated, what context and permissions the agent received, how you verified its work, where it failed or needed correction, and what you deliberately kept under human control.
8. Your location, working hours, availability, and preferred engagement model.

We care more about evidence of strong engineering judgment, ownership, and dependable production work than pedigree, titles, or familiarity with any single AI framework.
