title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
## The role

We are looking for a strong, versatile senior software engineer to help turn a substantial body of existing software, prototypes, integrations, and internal tools into reliable production systems.

This is fundamentally a software-engineering role. We care most about whether you can understand an unfamiliar codebase, make sound architectural decisions, write maintainable code, debug difficult problems, ship complete systems, and keep those systems dependable after launch.

The work spans backend and full-stack development, data systems, APIs and third-party integrations, workflow automation, communication platforms, cloud infrastructure, security, testing, observability, and AI-enabled applications. Some projects involve persistent agents, browser or desktop automation, media pipelines, and organizational knowledge systems. You do not need to be a specialist in every area, but you should be able to take broad technical ownership and become effective quickly in unfamiliar parts of the stack.

We use AI coding agents extensively. You will be expected to use them well, just as you would be expected to use version control, tests, debuggers, documentation, and observability tools well. Agent fluency matters, but it is not a substitute for engineering ability. We are not hiring a prompt engineer whose code must be rescued by someone else.

## Current technical environment

The current estate is polyglot. Python and TypeScript are the dominant application languages, while Rust appears in the lower-level agent, desktop, installer, terminal, and computer-control layers. The exact architecture will continue to evolve, but an engineer joining today should expect to work with:

- **Python 3.10/3.11+:** FastAPI, Starlette, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Psycopg, LangGraph, OpenAI and other model APIs, Slack and Discord SDKs, JSON Schema, PyYAML, pytest, `uv`, Hatch, and setuptools.
- **TypeScript and JavaScript on modern Node.js:** Next.js, React, Vite, Express, Electron, Tailwind CSS, Zod, Drizzle ORM, Supabase, Playwright, Vitest, `pnpm`, and `npm`.
- **Rust:** Cargo workspaces and asynchronous systems built with Tokio, Serde, Reqwest, Tauri, tracing, and cross-platform process or terminal primitives.
- **Data and protocols:** PostgreSQL, SQLite, structured JSON/YAML contracts, REST APIs, webhooks, append-only event and message records, idempotent workers, queues, authentication, permissions, and audit trails.
- **Agent and automation interfaces:** tool calling, MCP and related agent protocols, persistent task state, retrieval, evaluations, coding-agent adapters, browser automation, desktop control, and human approval workflows.
- **Infrastructure and delivery:** Docker and Compose, Linux services, cloud-hosted APIs, Vercel-style web deployment, CI/CD, secrets management, logging, metrics, traces, backups, and incident recovery.
- **Native and cross-platform surfaces:** Electron and Tauri desktop applications, PTYs and terminal interfaces, browser automation, and a smaller Swift/AppKit/ScreenCaptureKit macOS helper.

This is not a requirement to have used every named library. It is a requirement to be comfortable moving through a mixed Python, TypeScript, and Rust system and to understand the engineering concepts underneath the frameworks.

## What you will own

### Build and maintain production software

- Design, implement, test, deploy, and operate software across backend services, internal tools, and full-stack applications.
- Take features and systems from an approved requirement through implementation, integration, release, monitoring, and maintenance.
- Read and improve existing code before proposing a rewrite.
- Make pragmatic architectural and build-versus-integrate decisions based on reliability, security, cost, and maintainability.
- Define clear interfaces, schemas, failure behavior, and migration paths.
- Keep codebases understandable and leave systems in a condition that another engineer can safely continue.

### Build integrations and workflow infrastructure

- Build and maintain integrations with communication platforms, repositories, email, cloud services, publishing systems, analytics tools, CRMs, and other approved external services.
- Extend shared workflows across platforms such as Slack and Discord while preserving consistent identity, permissions, task state, and audit history.
- Design reliable webhook handlers, background jobs, queues, scheduled work, retries, idempotency, and recovery behavior.
- Build operator interfaces for reviewing work, resolving exceptions, approving actions, and understanding system state.
- Use APIs where practical and controlled browser, desktop, or mobile automation when an adequate API is unavailable.
- Design automations to tolerate interface changes, expired sessions, partial failures, duplicate events, and rate limits.

### Build data and organizational knowledge systems

- Ingest authorized communications and records from approved sources such as Slack, Discord, email, documents, meetings, and repositories.
- Build durable storage, retrieval, search, and briefing systems with appropriate provenance and access control.
- Preserve who said what, when it was said, and where it came from; distinguish a direct statement from an automated inference or summary.
- Support corrections, superseded information, retention rules, deletion, and audit requirements.
- Build relationship and communication workflows that can track interaction history, open loops, drafts, approvals, and reminders.
- Prevent private information from leaking between projects, users, agents, or public outputs.

### Build and integrate AI-enabled systems

- Implement applications and workflows that use language models, coding agents, research agents, computer-use agents, retrieval, tool calling, and structured outputs.
- Connect agents to real systems through explicit, testable interfaces rather than fragile prompt-only behavior.
- Design durable task state, checkpoints, queues, retries, timeouts, escalation, and recovery for long-running agent work.
- Build evaluations and regression tests for nondeterministic components.
- Instrument agent runs so engineers can inspect inputs, tool use, costs, failures, outputs, and approval state.
- Establish clear boundaries between observing, recommending, drafting, staging, and taking an authorized external action.
- Prevent one model's confidence or self-assessment from being treated as proof that a result is correct.

### Build secure automation and account access

- Implement least-privilege access, secret management, environment isolation, audit logging, revocation, and approval gates.
- Protect systems that can read private data, execute code, operate browsers, or act through external accounts.
- Account for prompt injection, malicious external content, confused-deputy behavior, credential exposure, and cross-project data leakage.
- Separate development, staging, and production access and make consequential actions attributable.
- Work with the relevant security owner on threat modeling, design review, incident response, and remediation.
- Treat browser and desktop control as high-permission production infrastructure, not a demo shortcut.

### Own engineering quality and operations

- Write meaningful unit, integration, end-to-end, security, and regression tests.
- Build deployment automation and maintain appropriate environments, backups, recovery procedures, and operational runbooks.
- Instrument services with useful logs, metrics, traces, alerts, cost visibility, and failure diagnostics.
- Investigate production problems, identify root causes, and make the system more resilient afterward.
- Review human- and agent-generated code for correctness, security, dependency risk, brittle assumptions, and unnecessary complexity.
- Distinguish proposed, mocked, locally demonstrated, staging-qualified, and production behavior.
- Require reproducible evidence before declaring technical work complete.

### Improve how engineering work gets done

- Work with product managers to turn approved requirements and acceptance criteria into sound technical plans.
- Surface unclear requirements, hidden dependencies, security concerns, and technically risky assumptions early.
- Break larger implementations into work that engineers and agents can execute without losing architectural coherence.
- Keep technical decisions, active work, blockers, and release evidence visible to the team.
- Turn recurring implementation problems into reusable libraries, tests, automation, documentation, or engineering standards.
- Help a small team operate multiple systems without accumulating an unmanageable collection of one-off frameworks.

## How we use AI agents

We expect senior engineers here to use agents as a normal part of their engineering practice. Depending on the task, that may include coding agents, research agents, browser agents, custom automations, local models, orchestration tools, or parallel development workflows.

Strong use of agents might involve:

- giving an agent the relevant code, architecture, constraints, and definition of done;
- delegating bounded implementation, investigation, test-writing, migration, or documentation work;
- coordinating parallel work without conflicting changes or duplicated systems;
- preserving task state and decisions outside a private chat transcript;
- reviewing diffs, tests, traces, and running behavior rather than trusting an agent's summary;
- detecting when an agent is confidently wrong, stuck, missing context, or exceeding its authority; and
- improving the workflow after a failed or low-quality run.

You do not need to use a particular agent product or framework. We do want to understand which tools you use, what you trust them to do, how you verify their work, and where you keep a human in the loop.

The engineer remains accountable for the architecture, code, security, testing, and production result. “The agent wrote it” is never an explanation for poor engineering.

## Scope boundaries

This role does **not** own:

- product strategy, customer discovery, market selection, or roadmap prioritization;
- deciding which products or features the company should pursue;
- writing product requirements or serving as the product manager;
- trading strategy, investment signals, market calls, portfolio management, or trade execution;
- custody of funds or speculative financial activity;
- token economics, reward design, financial promises, or other economic policy; or
- final marketing, editorial, legal, or public-communications decisions.

You may implement approved software used by product, operations, content, community, or other teams. That does not transfer those teams' decision rights to engineering.

You are expected to challenge requirements that are technically incoherent, unsafe, or unverifiable and to propose better implementation options. The relevant product or functional owner remains responsible for the underlying business decision.

## Initial priorities

The exact sequence will be set with the product managers and engineering lead, but early work is likely to include:

- Audit relevant repositories, services, deployments, integrations, and unfinished implementations to determine what actually works.
- Establish a current technical map that distinguishes production systems, prototypes, stale assumptions, and missing infrastructure.
- Extend a shared organizational workflow across multiple communication platforms.
- Build a recurring, permission-aware communication-ingestion and retrieval pipeline with clear provenance.
- Improve the reliability and observability of long-running agent and automation workflows.
- Establish security controls for agents, external accounts, credentials, browser or desktop sessions, and sensitive communications.
- Build one approval-gated communication or content workflow from authorized source material through exact-artifact review and preview output.
- Consolidate common identity, event, permission, audit, and integration primitives where they are currently duplicated.
- Improve automated testing, deployment evidence, monitoring, and recovery for existing systems.

## What success looks like

- Develop an evidence-based understanding of the relevant systems and their current production state.
- Become productive in the existing stack without requiring a clean-room rewrite.
- Take ownership of a bounded technical milestone and ship a working, tested result.
- Repair or qualify at least one important existing workflow.
- Identify the highest-priority reliability, security, and maintainability risks and propose a practical sequence for addressing them.
- Establish an effective working pattern with the product managers, other engineers, QA, and the agents you use.
- Ship and operate at least one substantial cross-system workflow.
- Improve the visibility of system state, failures, approvals, costs, and outcomes.
- Establish reusable patterns for integrations, security, testing, observability, deployment, and recovery.
- Demonstrate that a second workflow can reuse those patterns with materially less engineering effort.
- Reduce the founder and engineering lead intervention required to keep technical work moving.
- Leave behind production evidence: deployed behavior, tests, traces, runbooks, and a clear maintenance path.

## What we are looking for

You are likely a strong fit if:

- You have substantial professional software-engineering experience and have personally shipped and operated production systems.
- You have production-level proficiency in both **Python** and **TypeScript/JavaScript**, including typed interfaces, dependency management, testing, debugging, and deployment.
- You have working proficiency in **Rust**: you can read an unfamiliar crate, trace ownership and async behavior, diagnose compiler or runtime failures, make a bounded production change, and verify it with tests. Deep Rust specialization is welcome but not required.
- You have built backend services using FastAPI, Starlette, Express, or a comparable framework and understand API design, authentication, validation, background work, and failure handling.
- You have built modern web applications using React and a framework such as Next.js or Vite, and can work productively across browser code, server code, and typed API boundaries.
- You can design and operate systems using PostgreSQL or SQLite, including schemas, migrations, transactions, indexing, concurrency, retention, and recovery.
- You understand APIs, webhooks, authentication, queues, background jobs, idempotency, distributed failure modes, cloud deployment, and observability.
- You are comfortable with Docker, Linux development and operations, CI/CD, secrets management, and at least one production cloud or application-hosting environment.
- You can write and maintain unit, integration, and end-to-end tests using tools such as pytest, Vitest, and Playwright or their equivalents.
- You can work across backend, infrastructure, integrations, and enough frontend code to own a result end to end.
- You write clear, maintainable code and exercise sound judgment about abstractions, dependencies, performance, and operational complexity.
- You can diagnose difficult problems using code, logs, metrics, traces, tests, and production evidence.
- You understand security fundamentals, especially around credentials, private data, access boundaries, and high-permission automation.
- You can take an ambiguous technical problem, investigate it, propose a bounded plan, and close the loop without constant supervision.
- You communicate clearly in writing and leave useful technical plans, decision records, documentation, runbooks, and postmortems.
- You use AI coding or engineering agents productively and review their work with the same rigor you would apply to a human contributor's work.
- You care more about dependable outcomes than impressive demos, framework novelty, or raw lines of generated code.

Useful but not required experience includes:

- FastAPI, Starlette, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Psycopg, LangGraph, and modern Python packaging with `uv`;
- Next.js, React, Vite, Express, Electron, Tailwind, Zod, Drizzle, Supabase, and modern Node.js tooling;
- Tokio, Serde, Reqwest, Tauri, terminal or PTY programming, and structured tracing in Rust;
- LLM applications, multi-agent systems, MCP, durable workflows, or event-driven orchestration;
- Slack Bolt/SDK, Discord.py, email, publishing, messaging, analytics, or CRM integrations;
- browser automation, computer use, desktop applications, mobile testing, or virtualized devices;
- event sourcing, knowledge graphs, provenance systems, search, or temporal data models;
- security engineering for multi-tenant or high-permission systems;
- developer tools, internal platforms, and shared-service infrastructure;
- media generation, deterministic rendering, or content-operation pipelines; and
- evaluating or observing nondeterministic software;
- Swift, AppKit, ScreenCaptureKit, macOS permissions, signing, or notarization; or
- Azure, AWS, Vercel, Railway, GitHub Actions, or comparable deployment systems.

You do not need experience in all of these areas. Strong general engineering ability, production judgment, and the capacity to learn matter more than matching every keyword.

## This role is probably not for you if

- Your experience is primarily prototypes, hackathons, or model demos that somebody else productionized.
- You prefer narrowly assigned tickets and do not want responsibility for integration, deployment, diagnosis, or maintenance.
- You want to rewrite unfamiliar systems before understanding why they exist.
- You consider a merged pull request sufficient evidence that a feature works.
- You treat testing, security, observability, or documentation as someone else's job.
- You use AI-generated code that you cannot explain, debug, or maintain.
- You optimize for the number of agents, models, or frameworks involved rather than the quality of the resulting system.
- You want to own product strategy or trading activity rather than implement approved technical work.

## Scope and decision rights

You will have broad authority to investigate technical systems, propose architecture, implement approved work, improve engineering workflows, delegate scoped tasks to agents, and make reversible technical decisions within agreed boundaries.

Production releases, material infrastructure spending, access to sensitive communications, new third-party accounts, and consequential external actions require the applicable approval. Delegating an action to an agent does not expand your authority.

The founder retains final authority over company direction, capital allocation, and material risk. Product, security, QA, legal, marketing, and operations owners retain their respective decision and approval gates.

## How to apply

Please send:

1. A short explanation of why this senior engineering role fits you.
2. Two examples of production software or infrastructure you personally shipped and operated. Explain the system, your exact contribution, the hardest technical tradeoff, and what happened after launch.
3. A link to code or a technically detailed artifact you produced. Private work may be described or demonstrated in redacted form.
4. A description of a difficult production incident or engineering failure you helped resolve. How did you diagnose it, what was the root cause, and what changed afterward?
5. A short technical walkthrough of a system you designed or substantially improved: its architecture, data model, important failure modes, security boundaries, and how you knew it was operating correctly.
6. A concise account of your experience with Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Rust. Name the frameworks and production systems you used, identify your strongest and weakest of the three, and explain one meaningful contribution you made in each language.
7. A description of the AI agents you currently use for engineering. Name the products, coding agents, models, frameworks, custom tools, or automations where possible. Walk through one real task: what you delegated, what context and permissions the agent received, how you verified its work, where it failed or needed correction, and what you deliberately kept under human control.
8. Your location, working hours, availability, and preferred engagement model.

We care more about evidence of strong engineering judgment, ownership, and dependable production work than pedigree, titles, or familiarity with any single AI framework.

title: Developer for Claude-Powered Autonomous Job Application System
description:
Project Overview
I am looking for an AI developer to create a fully autonomous job application system powered by Claude. The goal is to build a seamless workflow that handles the entire job hunting process, from finding the best-matching job postings to customising application documents and submitting them directly on the portals.

Core Goals & Workflow

Target Platforms: Workflow to autonomously search for relevant roles and apply across linkedin.com, seek.com, indeed.com, and adzuna.com.au.

Dynamic Tailoring: For each application, the workflow needs to use Claude to analyse the job description and automatically tailor the resume and cover letter (if required).

Autonomous Form Filling: The system must be able to navigate the portals autonomously to fill out online forms, upload the customised documents, and submit the application completely hands-free. This can be company portals which the job board redirects the applicant to apply.

Application Tracking: There must be a CSV job tracker included. The workflow must refer to this tracker whenever a job is being researched or applied for to ensure the exact same job is never applied to twice.

Token Efficiency: Because this system will process a high volume of applications, the architecture must ensure efficient token usage to keep Claude API costs manageable.

Requirements

Strong expertise working with Claude and claude code and its agentic or automation capabilities.

The ability to design and figure out the best architecture to make this happen.

How to Apply
Please share your proposal outlining how you would approach this build. Include your estimated timeline and a brief overview of the method you plan to use to achieve the end-to-end automation, CSV tracking, and token efficiency.

title: SuiteCRM Developer Needed for PHP and MySQL Upgrade
description:
We are seeking an experienced SuiteCRM developer to upgrade and modernize our existing SuiteCRM environment.
Our system currently runs on PHP 5.6 and MySQL 5.7. Because these versions are outdated, we need a developer who can assess the existing installation and perform a carefully planned migration to current, stable versions supported by SuiteCRM—without disrupting existing features, data, integrations, or business operations.
This is not simply a server upgrade. The selected developer must be able to identify compatibility issues, recommend an appropriate migration path, and determine whether the work should be completed through a staged upgrade.

Responsibilities:
- Review and document our current SuiteCRM installation, server environment, customizations, modules, integrations, and database structure
- Identify compatibility issues involving SuiteCRM, PHP, MySQL, extensions, themes, workflows, scheduled jobs, and custom code
- Recommend a safe, structured upgrade and migration plan
- Create complete backups and establish a rollback procedure before beginning the migration
- Set up and test the upgraded system in a staging environment
- Upgrade SuiteCRM as necessary to support current, stable versions of PHP and MySQL
- Update or refactor incompatible custom PHP code
- Migrate the database while preserving its accuracy and integrity
- Test all existing features, modules, workflows, reports, integrations, permissions, and automated processes
- Resolve any errors or performance issues caused by the migration
- Deploy the tested system to production with minimal downtime
- Provide clear technical documentation covering the work completed, system requirements, and future maintenance recommendations

Required Qualifications:
- Proven professional experience upgrading and maintaining SuiteCRM
- Strong knowledge of SuiteCRM architecture, customization, modules, workflows, and database structure
- Advanced PHP and MySQL skills
- Experience migrating legacy PHP applications from PHP 5.6 to newer supported versions
- Experience upgrading MySQL 5.7 databases
- Ability to identify and correct compatibility problems in custom code
- Experience with Linux-based servers, web-server configuration, backups, staging environments, and production deployments
- Strong troubleshooting and testing skills
- Clear communication and the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations in practical terms

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with complex or heavily customized SuiteCRM installations
- Experience integrating SuiteCRM with dialers, APIs, email systems, or other third-party platforms
- Familiarity with SuiteCRM performance optimization and security best practices
- Availability for post-migration support

Expected Deliverables:
- Initial system and compatibility assessment
- Written migration plan, timeline, and risk analysis
- Complete backup and rollback plan
- Fully upgraded and tested staging environment
- Successful production migration
- Validation that existing data and functionality remain intact
- Technical documentation and post-migration recommendations

When applying, please include:
- The SuiteCRM versions you have worked with
- Examples of SuiteCRM upgrades or migrations you have completed
- Your experience migrating systems from PHP 5.6 and MySQL 5.7
- How you would approach assessing a customized SuiteCRM installation
- Your estimated timeline for the assessment and migration
- Your availability for ongoing support after deployment

Please begin your proposal with the phrase “SuiteCRM Migration” so we know you have read the complete job description. We are looking for a developer who can evaluate the system carefully, communicate any risks before making changes, and complete the upgrade without compromising our existing data or functionality.

title: AI Engineer — Agents, MCP Servers & Outbound Automation (Long-Term)
description:
I run Newstrokes, an AI consulting agency. I'm building an AI acquisition engine - a system that finds the right prospects, enriches and scores them, personalizes outreach, and keeps my CRM honest without me touching a spreadsheet.

I know exactly what I want it to do. I want someone who has built this kind of thing before to build it with me, not explain it to me.

This is not a one-off automation. It's an ongoing build with a clear roadmap, and I'd like the same person on it for the next 6–12 months.

What you'd be building

1. The acquisition engine

Prospect sourcing and enrichment from multiple sources (LinkedIn, Apify actors, scrapers, enrichment APIs)
A scoring layer that decides who's actually worth my time, and why
Personalized multi-channel outbound - email and LinkedIn - that reads like a person wrote it
Two-way HubSpot sync so pipeline state is always real

2. Agentic workflows

Claude / OpenAI agents that run research, drafting, and qualification tasks on a schedule
Custom MCP servers and skills to connect my tools to Claude
Orchestration, retries, guardrails, and human approval steps where they matter

3. Data & integrations plumbing

API integrations, pipelines, and job scheduling that survive contact with reality
Logging, error handling, cost monitoring, and a dashboard so I can see what the system is doing
Documentation good enough that I can operate it without you in the room

What I'm looking for

5+ years engineering, with production LLM systems shipped - not demos, not notebooks
Strong Python (or TypeScript/Node) and comfort living in APIs

Real experience with agent frameworks and tool use; MCP experience is a strong plus

You've built outbound, growth, or GTM automation before and understand deliverability, rate limits, and why "spray and pray" breaks

CRM integration experience, ideally HubSpot

You make judgement calls on architecture and tell me when my idea is the expensive way to do it

How I like to work

Small scoped chunks, working software every week, no six-week silences
One weekly call, async the rest of the time
You own the technical decisions; I own the go-to-market decisions
Clean, documented, handover-ready code from day one

title: AI Chatbot Developer Needed for Doctor Appointment Booking Website
description:

The website will be built from scratch and should include dental services, doctors/dentists, branches, clinic timings, patient registration/login, appointment booking, appointment management, and a responsive modern UI for desktop and mobile.

Next.js / React
TypeScript
Node.js
Supabase / PostgreSQL
OpenAI / Claude / Gemini
Vercel

Patient authentication and data security are important. Patients must only be able to access their own appointment information, with secure API endpoints and proper authorization.

Deliverables
Complete Smile Dental website
Responsive modern UI
Doctors, services, branches, and clinic information
Patient authentication
Complete appointment booking system
Real-time appointment availability
Appointment management
AI chatbot with LLM integration
AI tool/function calling and backend integration
Secure database/API integration
Testing and bug fixing
Production deployment on Vercel

We are looking for someone who can handle the project end-to-end, from development and database setup to AI integration, appointment booking, testing, and Vercel deployment.

title: Node.js Developer: Real-Time Call Coaching System (Twilio + Deepgram + Claude API)
description:
We operate a 24/7 taxi dispatch service and need a Node.js developer to build a real-time AI co-pilot system that helps our overseas call center dispatchers catch booking errors during live customer calls.

THE PROBLEM
Dispatchers frequently miss critical call details: wrong pickup/dropoff addresses, missed stops on multi-stop trips, wrong branch for chain businesses, and overlooked special instructions (pet transportation, wheelchair access, etc). This isn't a knowledge gap -- our dispatch software (Sherlock) has built-in Google Maps. It's an attention-to-detail problem, and real-time coaching during the call is the only point where it can actually be fixed.

WHAT WE NEED BUILT
An audio pipeline: Twilio Media Streams forks live call audio to Deepgram for real-time transcription, which feeds the Claude API (already have a 20-rule system prompt written) to evaluate the call against best practices and push correction "script cards" to a permanent always-on browser window on each dispatcher's workstation in real time.

A secondary verification layer: our dispatch software (Sherlock/Postgres) fires a LISTEN/NOTIFY event the moment a booking is created. Your code needs to subscribe to that event, compare the completed booking against the call transcript, and flag mismatches before a driver is dispatched.

WHAT'S ALREADY DONE
- Full technical architecture and 15-page developer spec (attached)
- Complete 20-rule system prompt for Claude
- Working React prototype for the dispatcher-facing UI (transcript panel + script card panel)
- Twilio account active with valid credentials
- Sherlock/Postgres integration path confirmed by their PM (one-time $340 setup fee, separate from your quote)
- Sample booking data schema from our dispatch software (attached)

WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER
- Backend Node.js app connecting Twilio, Deepgram, and Claude APIs via WebSocket
- Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY subscriber and mismatch-detection logic
- Integration of the provided React UI with your backend
- Docker setup and deployment documentation for our VPS
- Basic monitoring/logging

TIMELINE & BUDGET
Expecting about 4 weeks from kickoff to production. Budget above is a starting estimate -- please send your own fixed-price quote with your proposal.

TO APPLY
Please review the attached RFP package (full architecture, data schema, rulebook, and a proposal template) and respond covering: your relevant experience (especially Twilio Media Streams, WebSockets, and Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY if you have it), your technical approach, timeline, fixed-price quote, and 2-3 portfolio links or references.

title: Node.js Developer: Real-Time Call Coaching System (Twilio + Deepgram + Claude API)
description:
We operate a 24/7 taxi dispatch service and need a Node.js developer to build a real-time AI co-pilot system that helps our overseas call center dispatchers catch booking errors during live customer calls.

THE PROBLEM
Dispatchers frequently miss critical call details: wrong pickup/dropoff addresses, missed stops on multi-stop trips, wrong branch for chain businesses, and overlooked special instructions (pet transportation, wheelchair access, etc). This isn't a knowledge gap -- our dispatch software (Sherlock) has built-in Google Maps. It's an attention-to-detail problem, and real-time coaching during the call is the only point where it can actually be fixed.

WHAT WE NEED BUILT
An audio pipeline: Twilio Media Streams forks live call audio to Deepgram for real-time transcription, which feeds the Claude API (already have a 20-rule system prompt written) to evaluate the call against best practices and push correction "script cards" to a permanent always-on browser window on each dispatcher's workstation in real time.

A secondary verification layer: our dispatch software (Sherlock/Postgres) fires a LISTEN/NOTIFY event the moment a booking is created. Your code needs to subscribe to that event, compare the completed booking against the call transcript, and flag mismatches before a driver is dispatched.

WHAT'S ALREADY DONE
- Full technical architecture and 15-page developer spec (attached)
- Complete 20-rule system prompt for Claude
- Working React prototype for the dispatcher-facing UI (transcript panel + script card panel)
- Twilio account active with valid credentials
- Sherlock/Postgres integration path confirmed by their PM, handled separately from your quote
- Sample booking data schema from our dispatch software (attached)

WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER
- Backend Node.js app connecting Twilio, Deepgram, and Claude APIs via WebSocket
- Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY subscriber and mismatch-detection logic
- Integration of the provided React UI with your backend
- Docker setup and deployment documentation for our VPS
- Basic monitoring/logging

TIMELINE & BUDGET
Expecting about 4 weeks from kickoff to production. Budget above is a starting estimate -- please send your own fixed-price quote with your proposal.

TO APPLY
Please review the attached RFP package (full architecture, data schema, rulebook, and a proposal template) and respond covering: your relevant experience (especially Twilio Media Streams, WebSockets, and Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY if you have it), your technical approach, timeline, fixed-price quote, and 2-3 portfolio links or references.

I’m not looking for a basic chatbot implementation. I’m looking for someone who can help build a reliable production-quality retrieval system for engineering/construction documents.

title: Node.js Developer: Real-Time Call Coaching System (Twilio + Deepgram + Claude API)
description:
We operate a 24/7 taxi dispatch service and need a Node.js developer to build a real-time AI co-pilot system that helps our overseas call center dispatchers catch booking errors during live customer calls.

THE PROBLEM
Dispatchers frequently miss critical call details: wrong pickup/dropoff addresses, missed stops on multi-stop trips, wrong branch for chain businesses, and overlooked special instructions (pet transportation, wheelchair access, etc). This isn't a knowledge gap -- our dispatch software (Sherlock) has built-in Google Maps. It's an attention-to-detail problem, and real-time coaching during the call is the only point where it can actually be fixed.

WHAT WE NEED BUILT

A secondary verification layer: our dispatch software (Sherlock/Postgres) fires a LISTEN/NOTIFY event the moment a booking is created. Your code needs to subscribe to that event, compare the completed booking against the call transcript, and flag mismatches before a driver is dispatched.

WHAT'S ALREADY DONE
- Full technical architecture and 15-page developer spec (attached)
- Complete 20-rule system prompt for Claude
- Working React prototype for the dispatcher-facing UI (transcript panel + script card panel)
- Twilio account active with valid credentials
- Sherlock/Postgres integration path confirmed by their PM, handled separately from your quote
- Sample booking data schema from our dispatch software (attached)

WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER
- Backend Node.js app connecting Twilio, Deepgram, and Claude APIs via WebSocket
- Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY subscriber and mismatch-detection logic
- Integration of the provided React UI with your backend
- Docker setup and deployment documentation for our VPS
- Basic monitoring/logging

TIMELINE & BUDGET
Expecting about 4 weeks from kickoff to production. Budget above is a starting estimate -- please send your own fixed-price quote with your proposal.

TO APPLY
Please review the attached RFP package (full architecture, data schema, rulebook, and a proposal template) and respond covering: your relevant experience (especially Twilio Media Streams, WebSockets, and Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY if you have it), your technical approach, timeline, fixed-price quote, and 2-3 portfolio links or references.

title: Senior AI / LLM Engineer — Production AI Platform
description:
Senior AI / LLM Engineer — Production AI Platform
About Jalana Labs

Jalana Labs is building AI systems for public-service guidance—helping people understand complex requirements, evaluate their circumstances, and take practical action.

Our underlying system is intended to be reusable across multiple public-service domains rather than built around a single application.

Our first production implementation is focused on wildfire resilience. We are building conversational tools that help homeowners understand and reduce wildfire risk using authoritative technical information while providing a practical, individualized experience.

The wildfire system is already substantially built and running. It combines conventional software with LLM-based components, governed source content, runtime state, evaluation tooling, and controlled experimentation.

You can learn more about us at JalanaLabs.com.

We are looking for a strong senior contract engineer to become familiar with the existing system, contribute to its ongoing development, and provide engineering continuity alongside our current primary engineer.

This is not primarily a prompt-engineering or chatbot-development role. We are looking for an experienced software engineer who understands how to build, diagnose, and evaluate production systems in which LLM behavior is an important part of the product.

Your first assignment

Your first engagement will begin with a paid two-day discovery and scoping phase for an Engineering Continuity Package.

The production system spans several components, including the conversational interaction layer, response-generation layer, governed information/source system, and development/evaluation tooling, across multiple repositories and deployment targets.

We do not expect someone unfamiliar with the system to understand and document all of this completely in two days.

Instead, during the first two days we expect you to independently investigate the system and determine what would actually be required to make it recoverable and transferable.

At the end of the discovery phase, we want:

Your independently derived map of the production system and its major components
A clear distinction between what you have actually verified and what remains unverified
Continuity risks or knowledge gaps you discovered
Your proposed scope and structure for the Engineering Continuity Package
Your estimate of the work required to complete and validate it

Part of what we are evaluating is your ability to determine what you know, what you don't know, and what evidence is required before making an engineering claim.

If the discovery phase is successful, the next assignment will be to complete and validate the Engineering Continuity Package.

The ultimate standard is:

A competent engineer should be able to use the package and company-controlled access to understand, operate, diagnose, safely modify, test, deploy, roll back, and recover the production system without depending on undocumented knowledge held by any individual engineer.

How you'll learn the system

You will have access to the codebase, deployed system, tests, existing documentation, development and evaluation tools, and our primary engineer.

We do not want you simply to interview the primary engineer and transcribe what you are told.

We expect you to inspect the implementation, exercise the system, verify important behaviors yourself, identify gaps, and use the primary engineer for focused questions and clarification where necessary.

The primary engineer's involvement will be deliberately bounded. The objective is to determine whether the system can be understood independently from its code, documentation, tooling, runtime behavior, and company-held knowledge—not whether another engineer can teach it to you.

The ongoing role

If the initial engagement is successful, we expect this to become an ongoing contract relationship.

Our existing engineer will remain the primary engineer. We want a second engineer who can take meaningful engineering assignments, develop independent knowledge of the system, and ultimately be capable of assuming ownership if necessary.

You are not being hired to duplicate or supervise the primary engineer.

Near-term work will focus on the wildfire implementation. Longer term, we are developing and validating an architecture intended to support additional public-service domains without rebuilding the underlying system for each one.

Future work may include:

AI interaction and response engineering
controlled LLM experimentation and evaluation
evaluation and replay tooling
runtime and latency engineering
governed information and retrieval systems
production reliability and observability
backend and integration work
extending the underlying system to additional public-service applications
How we engineer AI systems

We care deeply about evidence-based engineering.

LLM systems do not always behave the way an engineer expects them to. Plausible reasoning about what a model or system should do is therefore not sufficient.

We expect engineers to observe actual behavior, recognize when an implementation is not producing the intended result, formulate hypotheses, run controlled experiments, and make decisions from evidence.

Wrong hypotheses and failed experiments are completely acceptable. They are part of the work.

What matters is maintaining a rigorous distinction between what you expect, what you infer, and what you have actually verified.

We value engineers who naturally work like this:

“I expected X. I tested it. The system actually did Y. Here is the evidence. Here is what I think we should test next.”

We also care about the realized user experience. Technical correctness alone is not sufficient if the system isn't producing the experience the product was designed to deliver.

What we're looking for

Strong candidates will have senior-level production software engineering experience and significant hands-on experience building applications with LLMs.

We are particularly interested in experience with:

Python and backend development
production model APIs and LLM orchestration
structured model inputs and outputs
prompt and context engineering
debugging nondeterministic AI behavior
experimentation and evaluation of LLM systems
retrieval or governed-source architectures
production deployment and observability
failure handling and rollback
understanding unfamiliar systems from code and runtime evidence

You should be comfortable working independently, communicating clearly in writing, and challenging assumptions when actual system behavior contradicts them.

We care more about engineering judgment, curiosity, and disciplined use of evidence than familiarity with any particular AI framework.

When applying

Please don't send us a generic cover letter.

Instead, briefly answer these five questions:

Tell us about a production LLM system you personally engineered. What parts did you own?
Tell us about a time actual system behavior contradicted what you expected. What did you do next?
You inherit an unfamiliar production AI system and are asked to make it independently recoverable by another engineer. What would you do during your first two days?
How do you distinguish between something you believe about a system and something you have actually verified?
What is your current availability and hourly rate?

Specific, concise answers are much more useful to us than a long proposal.

I already have a working application/codebase. I’m specifically looking for someone who can help design or improve the document intelligence/RAG layer, including:

* PDF/document ingestion and parsing
* Chunking strategy for technical documents
* Metadata extraction and document hierarchy
* Embeddings and vector/hybrid search
* Reranking and retrieval quality
* Handling tables, sections, specifications, and document versions
* Source citations/page references in AI answers
* Preventing hallucinations when the answer is not supported by the documents
* Evaluation/testing of retrieval accuracy
* Scalable architecture for multiple organizations and projects

Before we move forward, could you tell me:

1. What RAG systems have you built that are currently in production?
2. How would you approach technical documents where sections, tables, page numbers, and document hierarchy are important?

5. How do you evaluate whether a RAG system is actually retrieving the correct information?
6. What technology stack would you recommend for this type of system?
7. Can you work within an existing codebase rather than rebuilding the entire application?

I’m not looking for a basic chatbot implementation. I’m looking for someone who can help build a reliable production-quality retrieval system for engineering/construction documents.

If this matches your experience, please send me an example of a similar system you’ve built and explain what part of the RAG architecture you personally implemented.

title: PHP Developer (German speaking) for rapid Admin Panels Building using Claude Code
description:
## Summary

We're a Germany-based SaaS company with a global reach, powered by an amazing and diverse international remote team.

We need someone who can build small internal admin panels - fast. These are throwaway tools: a colleague needs a UI to look at some data, trigger a job, fix a record, or run an internal process. They live for a few months and then they're gone. We don't need architecture astronauts here. We need something that works, is safe to run internally, and is done in 3–4 days.

You'll work with Claude Code as your primary tool. That's the core skill, not a nice-to-have. If your workflow is "open the IDE and type PHP by hand", this is the wrong role.

German is mandatory. Our products, our customers, and much of our domain context (invoicing, tax, HR, German business processes) are German-language. You need to read a German requirements note or listen to a German voice memo and know what to build.

## What you'll do

- Build small internal admin panels in PHP: CRUD screens, data views, filters, exports, simple job triggers, basic role handling
- Work from rough input: a voice memo, a Slack thread, a Linear ticket, a screenshot, a database schema
- Use Claude Code end to end - prompting, skills, subagents, context management
- Ship in days, not weeks: typical task is 3–4 days from brief to something clickable on staging
- Keep the repo boring: GitHub flow, PRs, Renovate keeping dependencies current, CI green
- Hand over cleanly and move on to the next panel

## What "good enough" means here

We're explicit about this because it's unusual: these tools are internal, short-lived, and used by a handful of people. We are not asking for 90% test coverage or a hexagonal architecture. We *are* asking for:

- It works, and it keeps working without you babysitting it
- Auth and access control are correct - internal doesn't mean unprotected
- Readable enough that the next person can change it in an afternoon
- Dependencies patched, no obvious injection or upload holes

Pragmatic, not sloppy.

## Your profile

- Solid German & English
- Strong hands-on experience with Claude Code - daily driver, not "tried it once"
- Solid PHP; comfortable with a modern framework and an admin/CRUD toolkit (we mostly use Laravel + Filament)
- GitHub-based workflows, PRs, Renovate, CI - no hand-holding needed
- Comfortable in someone else's codebase and conventions rather than starting from scratch your way
- Able to scope yourself: you tell us when a "small panel" is actually a product

Bonus: AWS, Docker, Cloudflare, Linux, MySQL

## How we work

Async-first. Slack, Linear, GitHub, occasional MS Teams. Short and direct beats long and formal - a two-minute voice message is better than a five-paragraph email. No Scrum ceremonies, no big up-front plans. We care about what works and how quickly you get there.

This is ongoing, task-based work: individual jobs of roughly 3–4 days, recurring as they come up. Monday to Friday, with real overlap to European hours.

## How to apply

Please include:

1. One paragraph **in German** about the last internal tool or admin panel you built - what it was, how long it took, what you'd do differently.
2. A link or screenshots of something real you shipped (repo, staging URL, screen recording - anything we can actually look at).
3. Which AI coding tools you use daily, and one specific trick or setup that makes you faster than the average user.
4. Your day rate or your price for a typical 3–4 day panel.

Applications without a German paragraph won't be reviewed.

title: Claude Code Engineer, Migrate a Working AI Governance System from Cowork Prose Rules to Real Hooks
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

I run an AI-assisted consulting practice on a platform called Claude Cowork. Over the past several months I built a real enforcement system for it: skills, templates, and about 47 Python gate scripts that check things like "did you actually verify this before calling it done," "did this file get saved to the right folder," "does this document still sound like me and not like AI filler." The problem is that all of that enforcement is prose — the AI is instructed to run these checks and follow these rules, but it's reading and remembering, not being forced. Under a long session it skips things. I've had real, repeated incidents of gates being skipped even though the rule was written down clearly.

Claude Code (a different product from the same company) has an actual fix for this: hooks. A hook is a real shell command the platform runs automatically at a defined point (before a tool runs, after a tool runs, when the AI tries to finish its turn) and it returns an exit code. Some hook events can genuinely block — the AI cannot proceed until the check passes. That's a different category of enforcement than a prose instruction, because it's outside the model's discretion.

I already have a working proof of concept: a sealed test environment with 6 hooks built and 72 of 72 tests passing (PreToolUse guards blocking destructive file operations and wrong save locations, a Stop-hook gate checking that required deliverables actually exist, a post-write logger). I also already have a written spec mapping my real production gate scripts to the hook events they should run on. What I need is someone who can take that foundation and my real scripts and actually do the migration: wire the real checks into real hooks, close the gaps the prototype already surfaced, and get the whole thing running end-to-end on my Windows machine, not just passing tests in isolation.

This is not a "build me an AI agent from scratch" job. The architecture and the plan already exist. I need someone who has actually shipped Claude Code hooks in a real project before and can execute a defined migration, not learn hooks on my dollar.

WHAT'S ALREADY BUILT (you'd be extending this, not starting from zero)

- A sealed Claude Code hook environment, 72/72 automated tests passing, already run successfully live on Windows via Git Bash.
- A written spec mapping specific existing Python gate scripts to specific hook events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart), including which ones should be blocking and which are feedback-only.
- Real production scripts to migrate in, for example: a pre-delivery verification gate, a document voice/style checker, a spreadsheet data-integrity checker, a stale-content checker, a test-suite runner.

KNOWN GAPS TO CLOSE (found by testing the prototype, not guessed)

1. A Windows-only LibreOffice headless-conversion hang (a profile/lock flag issue) that times out file-conversion checks at 60 seconds.

2. Shell-level commands bypass tool-level guards entirely — anything routed through a raw shell call (mv/rm/del/Remove-Item equivalents) currently evades the Write/Edit hook checks.

3. A "finish" gate that verified a filename matched, not that the file's actual content was correct — needs a real content-level check.

4. Verdict-parsing bugs in a couple of gate scripts: brittle string-matching that misreads passing output as failing (and vice versa) depending on incidental wording.

5. A blocking Stop hook needs a recursion guard, and I need the exact, correct mechanism — guessing wrong here means an infinite loop, not a soft failure.

6. A subagent config declares a Claude-Code-style "Bash" tool that doesn't exist in Cowork — I need someone who understands the difference between Claude Code's tool surface and other Claude deployment surfaces well enough to catch this class of mismatch generally, not just this one instance.

WHAT "DONE" LOOKS LIKE

- The real production gate scripts (not just the prototype's sample scripts) wired into hooks per the migration spec, with each one verified by deliberately breaking the thing it's supposed to catch and confirming the hook actually fires and blocks.
- All 6 known gaps above fixed, with a test proving each fix.
- Full test suite still green, plus new tests for what you fixed.
- A short handoff doc: what you changed, why, and how I verify it still works if I touch it later.
- Everything running end-to-end on my real Claude Code install on Windows, not just in your own environment.

PAID TEST TASK (required before hire, not optional)

Fixed-price, $50, paid regardless of outcome, timeboxed to about an hour: I'll send one small, isolated bug reproduced from the real hook code. You fix it, write a test that proves the fix, and send back a short screen recording (Loom or similar, 3-5 minutes) walking through how you found and fixed it. This is the actual hire decision — the interview is a filter, the test task is the evidence.

WHAT I'M NOT LOOKING FOR
Proposals that restate this post back to me in different words, general "I'm an AI/automation expert" pitches with no hook-specific detail, or anyone unwilling to do the paid test task before a full-scope hire.

Title: Airtable + Make.com + Twilio Automation Specialist for Home-Services Platform

You'll work with Claude Code as your primary tool. That's the core skill, not a nice-to-have. If your workflow is "open the IDE and type PHP by hand", this is the wrong role.

German is mandatory. Our products, our customers, and much of our domain context (invoicing, tax, HR, German business processes) are German-language. You need to read a German requirements note or listen to a German voice memo and know what to build.

## What you'll do

- Build small internal admin panels in PHP: CRUD screens, data views, filters, exports, simple job triggers, basic role handling
- Work from rough input: a voice memo, a Slack thread, a Linear ticket, a screenshot, a database schema
- Use Claude Code end to end - prompting, skills, subagents, context management
- Ship in days, not weeks: typical task is 3–4 days from brief to something clickable on staging
- Keep the repo boring: GitHub flow, PRs, Renovate keeping dependencies current, CI green
- Hand over cleanly and move on to the next panel

## What "good enough" means here

We're explicit about this because it's unusual: these tools are internal, short-lived, and used by a handful of people. We are not asking for 90% test coverage or a hexagonal architecture. We *are* asking for:

- It works, and it keeps working without you babysitting it
- Auth and access control are correct - internal doesn't mean unprotected
- Readable enough that the next person can change it in an afternoon
- Dependencies patched, no obvious injection or upload holes

Pragmatic, not sloppy.

## Your profile

- Solid German & English
- Strong hands-on experience with Claude Code - daily driver, not "tried it once"
- Solid PHP; comfortable with a modern framework and an admin/CRUD toolkit (we mostly use Laravel + Filament)
- GitHub-based workflows, PRs, Renovate, CI - no hand-holding needed
- Comfortable in someone else's codebase and conventions rather than starting from scratch your way
- Able to scope yourself: you tell us when a "small panel" is actually a product

Bonus: AWS, Docker, Cloudflare, Linux, MySQL

## How we work

Async-first. Slack, Linear, GitHub, occasional MS Teams. Short and direct beats long and formal - a two-minute voice message is better than a five-paragraph email. No Scrum ceremonies, no big up-front plans. We care about what works and how quickly you get there.

This is ongoing, task-based work: individual jobs of roughly 3–4 days, recurring as they come up. Monday to Friday, with real overlap to European hours.

Please include:

1. One paragraph **in German** about the last internal tool or admin panel you built - what it was, how long it took, what you'd do differently.
2. A link or screenshots of something real you shipped (repo, staging URL, screen recording - anything we can actually look at).
3. Which AI coding tools you use daily, and one specific trick or setup that makes you faster than the average user.
4. Your day rate or your price for a typical 3–4 day panel.

Applications without a German paragraph won't be reviewed.

Title: Airtable + Make.com + Twilio Automation Specialist for Home-Services Platform

We are building a local home-services concierge platform that connects homeowners with qualified service providers, such as plumbers, electricians, HVAC technicians, landscapers, and handymen.

The customer-facing website is being built in Lovable. We need an experienced Airtable and Make.com specialist to finish designing the operational system behind it and automate the workflow from work-order submission through provider outreach and response tracking.

When a homeowner submits a work order through our website, the system should:

1. Create a new Job record in Airtable.
2. Identify suitable service providers based on trade, services offered, service area, availability, and other relevant criteria.
3. Recommend or select approximately three providers for the job.
4. Create a separate Job Offer record for each selected provider.
5. Place the job and recommended providers into an Airtable admin dashboard for review.
6. Allow an administrator to approve, remove, or replace providers before outreach begins.
7. Generate a customized SMS message for each approved provider.

* Airtable
* Make.com
* Twilio

* Providers

Under a long session it skips things. I've had real, repeated incidents of gates being skipped even though the rule was written down clearly.

Claude Code (a different product from the same company) has an actual fix for this: hooks. A hook is a real shell command the platform runs automatically at a defined point (before a tool runs, after a tool runs, when the AI tries to finish its turn) and it returns an exit code. Some hook events can genuinely block — the AI cannot proceed until the check passes. That's a different category of enforcement than a prose instruction, because it's outside the model's discretion.

I already have a working proof of concept: a sealed test environment with 6 hooks built and 72 of 72 tests passing (PreToolUse guards blocking destructive file operations and wrong save locations, a Stop-hook gate checking that required deliverables actually exist, a post-write logger). I also already have a written spec mapping my real production gate scripts to the hook events they should run on. What I need is someone who can take that foundation and my real scripts and actually do the migration: wire the real checks into real hooks, close the gaps the prototype already surfaced, and get the whole thing running end-to-end on my Windows machine, not just passing tests in isolation.

This is not a "build me an AI agent from scratch" job. The architecture and the plan already exist. I need someone who has actually shipped Claude Code hooks in a real project before and can execute a defined migration, not learn hooks on my dollar.

WHAT'S ALREADY BUILT (you'd be extending this, not starting from zero)

- A sealed Claude Code hook environment, 72/72 automated tests passing, already run successfully live on Windows via Git Bash.
- A written spec mapping specific existing Python gate scripts to specific hook events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart), including which ones should be blocking and which are feedback-only.
- Real production scripts to migrate in, for example: a pre-delivery verification gate, a document voice/style checker, a spreadsheet data-integrity checker, a stale-content checker, a test-suite runner.

KNOWN GAPS TO CLOSE (found by testing the prototype, not guessed)

1. A Windows-only LibreOffice headless-conversion hang (a profile/lock flag issue) that times out file-conversion checks at 60 seconds.

2. Shell-level commands bypass tool-level guards entirely — anything routed through a raw shell call (mv/rm/del/Remove-Item equivalents) currently evades the Write/Edit hook checks.

3. A "finish" gate that verified a filename matched, not that the file's actual content was correct — needs a real content-level check.

4. Verdict-parsing bugs in a couple of gate scripts: brittle string-matching that misreads passing output as failing (and vice versa) depending on incidental wording.

5. A blocking Stop hook needs a recursion guard, and I need the exact, correct mechanism — guessing wrong here means an infinite loop, not a soft failure.

6. A subagent config declares a Claude-Code-style "Bash" tool that doesn't exist in Cowork — I need someone who understands the difference between Claude Code's tool surface and other Claude deployment surfaces well enough to catch this class of mismatch generally, not just this one instance.

WHAT "DONE" LOOKS LIKE

- The real production gate scripts (not just the prototype's sample scripts) wired into hooks per the migration spec, with each one verified by deliberately breaking the thing it's supposed to catch and confirming the hook actually fires and blocks.
- All 6 known gaps above fixed, with a test proving each fix.
- Full test suite still green, plus new tests for what you fixed.
- A short handoff doc: what you changed, why, and how I verify it still works if I touch it later.
- Everything running end-to-end on my real Claude Code install on Windows, not just in your own environment.

PAID TEST TASK (required before hire, not optional)

Fixed-price, $50, paid regardless of outcome, timeboxed to about an hour: I'll send one small, isolated bug reproduced from the real hook code. You fix it, write a test that proves the fix, and send back a short screen recording (Loom or similar, 3-5 minutes) walking through how you found and fixed it. This is the actual hire decision — the interview is a filter, the test task is the evidence.

WHAT I'M NOT LOOKING FOR
Proposals that restate this post back to me in different words, general "I'm an AI/automation expert" pitches with no hook-specific detail, or anyone unwilling to do the paid test task before a full-scope hire.

description:

Phase 1 — Paid Technical Test: Existing Subscription Issues

We currently have two known issues:

1. Subscription renewal/access synchronization: A payment or renewal can succeed in Stripe but fail to update the local dj-stripe state correctly, resulting in incorrect application access or subscription controls.

The developer should investigate the actual root causes and implement a durable fix rather than only patching the symptoms.

* Keep local dj-stripe data for normal fast operation
* Treat Stripe as authoritative for actual billing/subscription state

* Provide reconciliation for missed/stale synchronization
* Maintain reliable company/user ↔ Stripe Customer mapping
* Handle webhook retries and duplicates safely

The existing implementation must be reviewed first. Avoid unnecessary rewrites, and propose a better approach if appropriate.

Regression tests should be added for both reported issues.

Expected effort for Phase 1: approximately 4–8 hours, depending on the root cause and the level of synchronization/reconciliation work required.

Continuation to Phase 2 will depend on satisfactory performance.

Phase 2 — Pricing, Subscription & Billing Implementation

title: Build an Airtable, Make.com and Twilio workflow for a home-services marketplace
description:
Title: Airtable + Make.com + Twilio Automation Specialist for Home-Services Platform

We are building a local home-services concierge platform that connects homeowners with qualified service providers, such as plumbers, electricians, HVAC technicians, landscapers, and handymen.

The customer-facing website is being built in Lovable. We need an experienced Airtable and Make.com specialist to finish designing the operational system behind it and automate the workflow from work-order submission through provider outreach and response tracking.

Project Overview

When a homeowner submits a work order through our website, the system should:

1. Create a new Job record in Airtable.
2. Identify suitable service providers based on trade, services offered, service area, availability, and other relevant criteria.
3. Recommend or select approximately three providers for the job.
4. Create a separate Job Offer record for each selected provider.
5. Place the job and recommended providers into an Airtable admin dashboard for review.
6. Allow an administrator to approve, remove, or replace providers before outreach begins.
7. Generate a customized SMS message for each approved provider.
8. Send the messages through Twilio after administrative approval.
9. Record delivery information, provider responses, and offer statuses in Airtable.
10. Update the job’s status as it moves through the process.

Current Technology Stack

* Airtable
* Make.com
* Twilio
* Lovable
* APIs and webhooks as needed

Our Airtable base currently includes, or is intended to include, the following tables:

* Providers
* Service Areas
* Sources
* Jobs
* Job Offers

We have begun setting up this system, but we need an expert to review the existing structure, recommend improvements, and complete the implementation.

Key Responsibilities

* Review and improve the existing Airtable base architecture
* Establish appropriate relationships between tables
* Connect Lovable work-order submissions to Airtable
* Build provider-matching and filtering logic
* Create Job Offer records for selected providers
* Build or improve the Airtable administrative approval interface
* Create the Make.com automation scenarios
* Integrate Twilio for outbound and, if feasible, inbound SMS
* Generate customized messages using provider and job information
* Track message delivery, provider responses, and offer statuses
* Add safeguards against duplicate records or duplicate messages
* Build error handling, alerts, and automation logs
* Test the entire workflow using sample records
* Provide clear documentation and a recorded Loom walkthrough
* Explain how we can safely edit and maintain the system after handoff

Ideal Candidate

You should have demonstrable experience with:

* Airtable relational database design
* Airtable Interfaces and automations
* Make.com scenario development
* Twilio SMS and Twilio APIs
* API integrations and webhooks
* Conditional matching or routing logic
* Workflow automation
* Error handling and troubleshooting
* No-code or low-code applications
* JavaScript or Airtable scripting when necessary

Experience connecting Lovable or Supabase to Airtable would be helpful but is not required if you have strong API and webhook experience.

Important Requirements

* All Airtable bases, Make scenarios, Twilio configurations, scripts, and related assets must be built inside accounts owned by us.
* The finished system must be tested and documented.
* Automations should be organized, clearly named, and maintainable.
* Please identify any limitations, ongoing costs, or scaling concerns before implementation.
* Customer and provider information must be handled securely.
* No live SMS messages should be sent during testing without approval.

Potential Deliverables

1. Review and written recommendation for the database and workflow architecture
2. Finalized Airtable base and table relationships
3. Functional administrative approval dashboard
4. Lovable-to-Airtable work-order integration
5. Provider-matching workflow
6. Airtable-to-Make-to-Twilio messaging workflow
7. Provider-response and status-tracking system
8. Error-handling and duplicate-prevention system
9. Complete end-to-end testing
10. Written documentation and Loom walkthrough

When Applying

Please include:

* Examples of similar Airtable and Make.com systems you have built
* Details about your Twilio SMS integration experience
* A brief explanation of how you would structure this workflow
* Your estimated timeline
* Whether you recommend hourly or fixed-price billing
* Any questions or potential technical concerns you see

Please begin your proposal with the words “Home Services Workflow” so we know you read the full description.

Screening Questions

1. Please describe a project in which you connected Airtable, Make.com, and Twilio or a similar SMS service.
2. How would you prevent duplicate provider offers and duplicate text messages?
3. How would you structure the relationship between Jobs, Providers, and Job Offers?
4. How would you handle provider replies received through Twilio?
5. What information would you need from us before beginning?
6. Are you willing to provide written documentation and a recorded walkthrough at project completion?

We would prefer to begin with a paid discovery and system-design milestone. If that goes well, the selected freelancer may complete the full build and potentially provide ongoing support.

title: PHP Developer (German speaking) for rapid Admin Panels Building using Claude Code
description:
## Summary

We're a Germany-based SaaS company with a global reach, powered by an amazing and diverse international remote team.

We need someone who can build small internal admin panels - fast. These are throwaway tools: a colleague needs a UI to look at some data, trigger a job, fix a record, or run an internal process. They live for a few months and then they're gone. We don't need architecture astronauts here. We need something that works, is safe to run internally, and is done in 3–4 days.

You'll work with Claude Code as your primary tool. That's the core skill, not a nice-to-have. If your workflow is "open the IDE and type PHP by hand", this is the wrong role.

German is mandatory. Our products, our customers, and much of our domain context (invoicing, tax, HR, German business processes) are German-language. You need to read a German requirements note or listen to a German voice memo and know what to build.

## What you'll do

- Build small internal admin panels in PHP: CRUD screens, data views, filters, exports, simple job triggers, basic role handling
- Work from rough input: a voice memo, a Slack thread, a Linear ticket, a screenshot, a database schema
- Use Claude Code end to end - prompting, skills, subagents, context management
- Ship in days, not weeks: typical task is 3–4 days from brief to something clickable on staging
- Keep the repo boring: GitHub flow, PRs, Renovate keeping dependencies current, CI green
- Hand over cleanly and move on to the next panel

## What "good enough" means here

We're explicit about this because it's unusual: these tools are internal, short-lived, and used by a handful of people. We are not asking for 90% test coverage or a hexagonal architecture. We *are* asking for:

- It works, and it keeps working without you babysitting it
- Auth and access control are correct - internal doesn't mean unprotected
- Readable enough that the next person can change it in an afternoon
- Dependencies patched, no obvious injection or upload holes

Pragmatic, not sloppy.

## Your profile

- Solid German & English
- Strong hands-on experience with Claude Code - daily driver, not "tried it once"
- Solid PHP; comfortable with a modern framework and an admin/CRUD toolkit (we mostly use Laravel + Filament)
- GitHub-based workflows, PRs, Renovate, CI - no hand-holding needed
- Comfortable in someone else's codebase and conventions rather than starting from scratch your way
- Able to scope yourself: you tell us when a "small panel" is actually a product

Bonus: AWS, Docker, Cloudflare, Linux, MySQL

## How we work

Async-first. Slack, Linear, GitHub, occasional MS Teams. Short and direct beats long and formal - a two-minute voice message is better than a five-paragraph email. No Scrum ceremonies, no big up-front plans. We care about what works and how quickly you get there.

This is ongoing, task-based work: individual jobs of roughly 3–4 days, recurring as they come up. Monday to Friday, with real overlap to European hours.

## How to apply

Please include:

1. One paragraph **in German** about the last internal tool or admin panel you built - what it was, how long it took, what you'd do differently.
2. A link or screenshots of something real you shipped (repo, staging URL, screen recording - anything we can actually look at).
3. Which AI coding tools you use daily, and one specific trick or setup that makes you faster than the average user.
4. Your day rate or your price for a typical 3–4 day panel.

Applications without a German paragraph won't be reviewed.
